Finally, Tom asked his friends, the other subway trains, to help him look for Sue's mom. They all worked together and found her mom on a different train. Tom was so happy that he could help Sue and be a useful subway train. Sue and her mom thanked Tom and his friends, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a little hut, lived a kind rabbit named Remy. Remy had a friend named Tina, the turtle. One day, Remy saw Tina with a big, red ball. Remy felt jealous. He wanted a big, red ball too.

Remy said to Tina, "Can I play with your ball?" Tina said, "Yes, but we have to be careful. The ball can break the hut." They played with the ball, but Remy leaned on the hut too much. The hut started to shake.

Suddenly, the hut fell down! Remy and Tina were sad. They learned to be more careful when playing. Remy was not jealous anymore. They both built a new hut together and played with the ball outside.

Lily asked her friend Tom for help. Tom said, "I can help you unlock the knot, if you give me half of what's inside the box." Lily agreed, and Tom unlocked the knot. Inside the box, there were many pretty toys and candy.

Lily and Tom started to fight over the toys and candy. They both wanted more than half. They pulled and pulled at the toys until they broke them. The candy fell on the ground and got dirty. In the end, Lily and Tom had nothing left to play with or eat. The moral of the story is that being greedy can lead to losing everything.

The next day, Spot found a new friend. It was a little bird who liked to play. They ran and played together all day. Spot was happy and did not stop playing. The rude cat saw them and felt lonely. Spot and the bird invited the cat to play, and they all became friends.

A little bird named Lily saw Max and flew down to say hello. "Hi, Max!" said Lily. "Why did you yawn?" Max looked at Lily and said, "I yawned because I am tired, and this patch is nice to rest on."

Lily and Max became good friends. They played in the soft patch of grass all day. When they were tired, they would yawn and rest together under the tree. They were very happy to have each other as friends.

Once upon a time, in a small pond, there lived a little fish named Fin. Fin was scared of the big pond. One day, a wise old turtle named Mr. Green came to visit.

"Fin, why are you scared of the big pond?" asked Mr. Green.

"I don't know, it's just so big!" said Fin.

Mr. Green had an idea. "Let's play a game. We will splash in the water, and you will see there is nothing to be scared of!"

Fin thought about it for a moment and agreed. They started to splash and play together. Fin was having so much fun that he forgot to be scared.

A year went by, and Fin was no longer scared of the big pond. He had many friends and loved to splash and play with them every day. And whenever he saw a scared little fish, he would teach them how to splash and have fun, just like Mr. Green taught him.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. It was Jack! He had found Timmy! But just as Jack was about to tag Timmy, Timmy yelled, "Pause!" Jack froze in his tracks, giving Timmy enough time to run and win the game.

When they got home, Lily's mom put the strawberries in the fridge. Lily was so excited to eat them, but she knew she had to wait until after dinner. During dinner, Lily couldn't stop thinking about the strawberries. She asked her mom, "Can we have the strawberries now, please?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. I know how much you love them." Lily was so happy and ate the strawberries with a big smile on her face. From that day on, Lily knew that sometimes you have to wait for the things you need, but it's always worth it in the end.

Timmy went back home and continued listening to his music. But he couldn't stop thinking about the old lady. He wondered if she was really okay. So, he went back to her house and knocked on the door again. This time, there was no answer. 

Timmy opened the door and found the old lady lying on the floor. She had fallen and hurt herself. Timmy quickly called for help, but it was too late. The old lady had passed away. Timmy was sad and didn't understand why bad things happen to good people.

Sam liked to play with his toy cars on the couch. He zoomed them up and down the cushions, making loud noises. He pretended they were racing on a big track. He did not see the scissors that his mom left on the couch. The scissors were sharp and shiny.

"Sam, be careful with your cars," his mom said. "Don't scratch the couch or hurt yourself. And don't touch the scissors. They are not for playing. They are for cutting paper."

Sam nodded, but he did not listen. He wanted to make his cars go faster and louder. He reached for the scissors. He thought they would make a good ramp for his cars. He did not know they were sharp and dangerous.

He lifted the scissors and put them on the edge of the couch. He picked up his favorite car, a red one with a big spoiler. He pushed it hard towards the scissors. He hoped it would fly over them and land on the other side.

But the car did not fly. It hit the scissors and bounced back. The scissors fell off the couch and landed on Sam's leg. Sam felt a sharp pain. He screamed and dropped his car. He saw blood on his leg and on the scissors.

"Mommy, mommy, help!" he cried. "It hurts, it hurts!"

His mom heard his scream and ran to him. She saw the scissors and the blood. She was scared and angry. She picked up Sam and hugged him. She took him to the bathroom and cleaned his wound. She put a bandage on it and kissed it.

"Sam, what did you do?" she asked. "Why did you touch the scissors? I told you they were not for playing. They are sharp and they can hurt you. You could have cut yourself badly. You were very lucky."

Sam felt sorry and sad. He knew he was wrong. He did not mean to hurt himself or the couch. He just wanted to have fun. He looked at his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mommy. I won't touch the scissors again. I love you."

His mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sam. But you have to listen to me and be careful. Scissors are not toys. They are tools. And couches are not tracks. They are for sitting and resting. Come on, let's go back to the couch and read a book. Maybe that will make you feel better."

Sam nodded and followed his mom. He left his cars and the scissors on the floor. He did not want to play with them anymore. He climbed on the couch and snuggled with his mom. She opened a book and read to him. He liked the book. It had pictures of animals and sounds. He forgot about his pain and his mistake. He felt happy and safe.

But the couch felt uncomfortable. It had a scratch from the scissors and a stain from the blood. It looked sad and hurt. It wished Sam would be more careful and gentle. It wished he would play with his cars somewhere else. It wished he would love it as much as his mom.

"Be careful, Anna," mom said. "Bees can sting you if they feel scared. They don't like it when you touch them."

Anna did not listen. She reached out her hand to touch the bee. But the bee did not like that. It flew up and buzzed angrily. Then it stung Anna on her finger.

"Ow!" Anna cried. She ran back to mom, holding her finger. "It hurts, mom, it hurts!"

Mom hugged Anna and looked at her finger. She saw a little red bump. She took out a band-aid from her bag and put it on Anna's finger.

"It's okay, Anna," mom said. "The bee was just trying to protect itself. It did not mean to hurt you. You have to be compassionate to the bees. They are important for the flowers and the honey."

Anna sniffed. She looked at the bee, still on the daisy. She felt sorry for the bee. She did not want to hurt it either.

"I'm sorry, bee," Anna said. "I won't touch you again. You can make honey and be happy."

The bee seemed to notice Anna's words. It flew away from the flower and buzzed around Anna's head. Then it landed on her band-aid and rubbed its legs. It was like saying thank you.

One of Timmy's friends said, "I have some bread. Maybe we can feed the bird." Timmy was excited and ran to get the bread. He carefully tore it into small pieces and threw it to the bird.

Suddenly, the bird swooped down and grabbed Timmy's toy sword with its sharp claws. "Oh no!" Timmy cried. "My sword!" But then the bird dropped the sword and flew away. Timmy and his friends laughed and played happily at the park, feeling safe and happy.

The little girl said, "Okay, let's go inside."

They learned about the history of dinosaurs and the history of the world. They had so much fun together. The big red car and the little girl went on many adventures after that day.

Suddenly, a big bad wolf appeared and demanded that Benny give him all his money. Benny was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, Benny had an idea. He told the wolf that he would give him all his money if he could help Benny find his magazine.

The wolf agreed and they searched high and low until they found the magazine. Benny was so happy and gave the wolf his money. The wolf was surprised that Benny was so kind, and decided to leave him alone. From that day on, Benny wasn't so shy anymore and made a new friend.

Her friend Jack saw her crying and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

"I hurt my toe on that big rock over there," Lily said, pointing to the ancient stone in the grass.

Jack said, "I'm sorry that happened. Can you forgive me for not telling you about the rock?"

Lily thought about it for a moment and said, "Yes, I forgive you. Let's go play again." And with that, they ran off to play together, forgetting all about the rock and Lily's sore toe.

Later that night, Lily and her mom were sitting outside when they heard a strange noise. "What's that?" asked Lily. "It sounds like a cricket," said her mom. Suddenly, they saw the jar with the cricket in it start to shake. The lid popped off and the cricket hopped out, chirping loudly. 

Lily and her mom laughed and chased after the cricket, trying to catch it again. From then on, whenever they heard a cricket, they remembered the fun they had trying to catch their reliable little pet.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. They have a big ball and a kite. They throw the ball and run with the kite. They are happy.

But then, a big cloud comes. The cloud is angry. It makes loud noises and rain. The rain is wet and cold. Anna and Ben are sad. They want to play, but they can't.

"Go away, cloud!" Anna says. "You are mean. You can't own the sky. The sky is for everyone."

But the cloud does not listen. It stays and makes more rain and noise. Anna and Ben are scared. They run to their house. They leave the ball and the kite outside.

They look out the window. They hope the cloud will go away soon. They want to play with their ball and kite again. They want to see the sun and the blue sky. They want to be happy.

Tom liked to collect things. He had a big box of things he found in the park, like stones, feathers, and leaves. One day, he saw a goose in the pond. He wanted to collect the goose too. He thought the goose was pretty and soft.

He went to the pond and tried to catch the goose. But the goose did not like that. The goose was angry and scared. It honked and bit Tom's hand. Tom cried out loud. He ran away from the pond. His hand hurt a lot.

A lady saw Tom and came to help him. She had a bandage and a cookie. She put the bandage on Tom's hand and gave him the cookie. She said, "Why did you try to catch the goose? That was not nice. The goose is not a thing. The goose is a living being. It has feelings and needs. You should not collect living beings. You should respect them and leave them alone."

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, lady. I did not know. I was ignorant. I thought the goose was pretty and soft. I wanted to collect it. But now I know better. I will not try to catch the goose again. I will only collect things that are not living."

The lady smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's go back to your mom and dad. They must be worried about you. And don't forget to say sorry to the goose too."

Tom nodded and said, "Okay, lady. Thank you for helping me. And sorry, goose. I hope you are okay." He waved to the goose and followed the lady. He still liked to collect things, but he never tried to collect living beings again. He learned to be kind and respectful to all creatures.

Ben and Mia like to play with puzzles. They have many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. Ben's favorite puzzle is the one with the fierce lion. He likes to roar like the lion when he finishes the puzzle.

One day, Ben and Mia are playing with puzzles in their room. Ben sees the lion puzzle on the shelf and wants to play with it. He asks Mia, "Can I have the lion puzzle, please?"

Mia shakes her head. "No, Ben. I want to play with the lion puzzle. You can play with the car puzzle."

Ben feels sad and angry. He really wants the lion puzzle. He says, "No, Mia. I asked first. Give me the lion puzzle, now!"

Mia holds the lion puzzle tight. She says, "No, Ben. You are being mean. The lion puzzle is mine!"

Ben and Mia start to fight over the puzzle. They pull and tug and shout. The puzzle breaks into pieces. They both cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees the broken puzzle and the crying children. She says, "What happened here? Why are you fighting?"

Ben and Mia tell Mom what happened. They both say they wanted the lion puzzle. They both say they asked for it.

Mom says, "You both made a mistake. You did not request the puzzle. You demanded the puzzle. Requesting is asking nicely and waiting for an answer. Demanding is asking rudely and not listening to the other person. Requesting is kind. Demanding is not."

Ben and Mia feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not request the puzzle. We demanded the puzzle. We were not kind. We were not good friends."

Mom says, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to learn to request and not demand. And you have to learn to share and take turns. Sharing and taking turns are also kind and good."

Ben and Mia nod. They say, "We will learn to request and not demand. We will learn to share and take turns. We will be kind and good."

Mom smiles. She says, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, let's fix the puzzle together. And then you can play with it together. And then you can play with another puzzle together. And then you can have a snack together. And then you can hug each other and say, 'I love you.'"

Ben and Mia smile. They say, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."

Timmy didn't listen and picked up the bug. He thought it was cool, but his friends thought it was gross. Timmy didn't care and continued to gaze at the bug. Suddenly, the bug bit him and Timmy started to feel sick.

Timmy learned that sometimes things that look cool can be dangerous. He also learned that it's important to listen to your friends when they warn you about something. From that day on, Timmy never picked up bugs again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play together and have fun. One day, they saw a big billboard with their favorite cartoon characters on it. They wanted to go see it up close, but they didn't know how to get there.

Timmy said, "Let's ask the nice lady over there for directions." Tommy said, "No, let's just walk and see if we can find it."

So they walked and walked, but they couldn't find the billboard. They started to quarrel and argue about which way to go. Timmy said, "I'm not comfortable with this. Let's just ask for directions." Tommy finally agreed, and they asked the nice lady for help.

She told them the way to the billboard, and they finally got to see it up close. They were so happy and excited, and they hugged each other. They realized that it was better to work together and ask for help when they needed it.

Mom and Anna picked up the dolls and put them on the bed. Mom got some tools and nails and fixed the shelf. She put the dolls back on the shelf. She said, "There, all done. The shelf is strong and the dolls are happy. Do you want to kiss them good night?"

Anna smiled and nodded. She kissed each doll and said, "I love you, doll. Good night." She kissed mom and said, "I love you, mom. Good night." Mom kissed Anna and said, "I love you, Anna. Good night." They went to sleep.

Lily and her daddy were playing with a magic wand. It was a toy, but it looked like a real wand. It had a star on the end and made a funny noise when you waved it.

"Can I try, daddy?" Lily asked. She wanted to make some magic too.

"Sure, sweetie, but be careful. Don't point it at anything you don't want to shrink," daddy said. He gave her the wand and smiled.

Lily waved the wand around and giggled. She pointed it at a flower, a book, a ball. They all became very small. She thought it was fun.

Then she saw a cake on the table. It was a chocolate cake, and it looked delicious. Lily loved chocolate cake. She wanted a big slice.

She pointed the wand at the cake and said, "Shrink!" But she made a mistake. She pointed the wand at her daddy too. He was standing behind the cake.

Suddenly, daddy became very small. He was smaller than the cake. He was smaller than Lily's hand. He was smaller than a bug.

"Daddy!" Lily cried. She dropped the wand and ran to the table. She tried to pick up her daddy, but he was too tiny. She couldn't see him well.

Then she heard a loud crunch. She looked up and saw a big cat. It was her cat, Fluffy. Fluffy had jumped on the table and eaten the cake. And her daddy.

Lily screamed. She was very sad. She had lost her daddy. And her cake. She wished she had never played with the magic wand.

Tom is a tall boy who likes to write poems. He writes poems about his toys, his friends, and his family. He keeps his poems in a big book that he hides under his bed.

One day, his mom calls him from downstairs. "Tom, it's time for lunch!" she says. Tom does not want to stop writing. He wants to finish his poem about his red truck. He says, "Just a minute, mom!"

But his mom does not hear him. She thinks he is playing with his toys. She calls him again. "Tom, come on, your sandwich is getting cold!" she says. Tom still does not come. He writes another line for his poem.

His mom gets worried. She goes upstairs to check on him. She opens his door and sees him sitting on the floor with his book and his pen. She smiles and says, "What are you doing, Tom?"

Tom looks up and says, "I'm writing a poem, mom. Do you want to hear it?" He shows her his book and reads his poem aloud. His mom listens and claps. She says, "That's a wonderful poem, Tom! I'm so proud of you!"

Tom beams and says, "Thank you, mom! Can I write more poems later?" His mom nods and says, "Of course, you can. But first, let's go have lunch. You must be hungry after all that writing." She hugs him and takes his hand. They go downstairs together and enjoy their sandwiches.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the yard. They had cars, dolls, balls and blocks. One day, Tom's car broke. The wheel came off and he could not make it go. He was sad and angry.

He went to his neighbor, Sam, who had many tools. Sam liked to fix things. He fixed bikes, radios, clocks and lamps. Tom asked Sam to fix his car. Sam said yes and took the car to his garage.

But Sam was stubborn. He did not listen to Tom. He wanted to make the car better. He put a bigger wheel, a louder horn, a shiny sticker and a long antenna on the car. He thought it looked cool.

He gave the car back to Tom. Tom did not like it. He said it was not his car. He said it was ugly and noisy and silly. He wanted his old car back. He was very mad at Sam.

Lily saw Tom and Sam fighting. She did not like it. She wanted them to be friends. She had an idea. She took her doll and went to Sam. She asked him to fix her doll. She said her doll needed a new dress, a hat, a necklace and a purse. She said she liked shiny things.

Sam smiled. He liked to fix things. He took the doll and went to his garage. He found some fabric, some beads, some glue and some scissors. He made a new dress, a hat, a necklace and a purse for the doll. He thought it looked pretty.

He gave the doll back to Lily. Lily liked it. She said it was beautiful and thanked Sam. She gave him a hug. She took the doll and went to Tom. She showed him the doll and said Sam fixed it. She said Sam was good at fixing things. She said he could fix Tom's car too.

Tom looked at the doll. He saw it was different, but Lily was happy. He thought maybe Sam was not so bad. He said he was sorry for being mad. He asked Sam to fix his car again. He said he wanted his old wheel, his old horn, his old sticker and his old antenna back. He said he liked his car the way it was.

Sam nodded. He said he was sorry for not listening. He said he wanted to make Tom happy. He took the car and went to his garage. He took off the bigger wheel, the louder horn, the shiny sticker and the long antenna. He put back the old wheel, the old horn, the old sticker and the old antenna. He fixed the car.

He gave the car back to Tom. Tom liked it. He said it was his car and thanked Sam. He gave him a high-five. He took the car and went to Lily. He showed her the car and said Sam fixed it. He said Sam was good at fixing things. He said he was his friend.

Lily smiled. She was glad Tom and Sam were friends. She said they were both good at playing. She said they could play together. She said she had balls and blocks. She asked them to join her.

Tom and Sam agreed. They went to Lily's yard. They played with their toys. They had fun. They were happy. They were neighbors and friends.

Tommy was grumpy. He did not want to share his toys with his sister. He wanted to play with his cars and his blocks by himself. His sister wanted to play with him, but he said no. He pushed her away and made her cry.

"Tommy, that is not nice!" his mother said. "You have to share with your sister. She is smaller than you and she loves you. Say sorry to her and give her a hug."

Tommy did not say sorry. He did not give a hug. He said, "No, she is bad. She always takes my toys. I don't love her. Go away, mother!"

His mother was sad. She said, "Tommy, you are being very rude and mean. You have to learn to forgive and be kind. If you don't, you will have no friends and no fun. Do you want that?"

Tommy did not care. He said, "Yes, I want that. I don't need friends. I don't need fun. I only need my toys. Leave me alone, mother!"

His mother sighed. She said, "Okay, Tommy. If that is what you want, I will leave you alone. But I hope you will change your mind soon. I love you, Tommy, even if you are grumpy."

She left the room and closed the door. Tommy was alone with his toys. He played with his cars and his blocks. He did not hear his sister laughing and singing in the other room. He did not see his mother smiling and reading a book. He did not feel the sun shining and the wind blowing outside. He only felt grumpy and lonely. He did not know how to forgive and be happy. He had a bad ending.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big net in the grass. They think it is funny.

"Look, Ben, a net!" Lily says. "What can we do with it?"

"Maybe we can catch something," Ben says. "Like a bird or a bug."

They run around with the net. They try to catch a bird, but the bird flies away. They try to catch a bug, but the bug is too fast. They are not happy.

"Let's mail the net to someone else," Lily says. "Maybe they can have fun with it."

"Good idea," Ben says. "But who can we mail it to?"

They think hard. They remember their teacher, Miss Lee. She is nice and kind. She always helps them learn new things.

"Let's mail the net to Miss Lee," Lily says. "She likes animals. Maybe she can use the net to help them."

"OK," Ben says. "But how do we mail it?"

They look around. They see a big box near the trash can. They put the net in the box. They write "To Miss Lee" on the box. They carry the box to the mailman.

"Hello, kids," the mailman says. "What do you have there?"

"We have a net for Miss Lee," Lily says. "Can you mail it to her?"

"Sure, I can," the mailman says. "But why do you want to mail a net to her?"

"Because she likes animals," Ben says. "And we want to make her happy."

The mailman smiles. He takes the box. He puts it in his truck. He drives away.

Lily and Ben wave goodbye. They feel good. They have done something nice for their teacher.

The moral of the story is: It is better to share than to be greedy. You can make someone happy by giving them something they like.

Lily and Sam are playing with their toys in the living room. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, and books. They like to make stories with their toys and pretend they are different people.

"Let's play restaurant," Sam says. "I will be the cook and you will be the customer. What do you want to eat?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She likes many things: pizza, ice cream, apples, and cheese. She decides to order pizza and ice cream.

"I want pizza and ice cream, please," she says.

"Okay," Sam says. "I will make it for you. Wait here."

Sam goes to the kitchen and looks for the toy pizza and ice cream. He finds the pizza, but he cannot find the ice cream. He looks in the fridge, in the cupboard, and under the table. He does not see it anywhere.

He forgets that he left the ice cream in the bedroom. He was playing with it before and he put it on the bed. He does not remember that.

He goes back to the living room with the pizza. He gives it to Lily.

"Here is your pizza," he says. "But I am sorry, I do not have ice cream. I cannot find it."

Lily is sad. She really wanted ice cream. She likes it a lot. It is sweet and cold and yummy.

"But I ordered ice cream," she says. "You have to give me ice cream. It is not fair."

Sam feels bad. He wants to make Lily happy. He tries to think of something else to give her.

"I can give you something else," he says. "How about a cookie? Or a banana? Or a carrot?"

Lily shakes her head. She does not want a cookie, or a banana, or a carrot. She only wants ice cream.

"No, no, no," she says. "I want ice cream. Ice cream, ice cream, ice cream."

Sam does not know what to do. He thinks it is hard to be a cook. He wishes he could find the ice cream. He wonders where it is. He does not like to forget things. He wants to play with Lily and have fun. He hopes they can still be friends.

"Mom, can I feed the ducks?" Lila asked.

"Sure, honey. Here, take some prunes. They are good for the ducks," Mom said. She gave Lila a small bag of prunes.

Lila walked to the pond. She saw a big duck with a green head. She threw a prune to the duck. The duck ate the prune. It quacked happily.

"Hello, duck. Do you like prunes?" Lila said.

The duck nodded. It came closer to Lila. It wanted more prunes. Lila gave the duck another prune. The duck ate the prune. It quacked again.

"Thank you, Lila. You are very kind," the duck said.

Lila smiled. She felt happy. She liked the duck. She gave the duck a hug.

"You are welcome, duck. You are very cute," Lila said.

The duck hugged Lila back. They became friends. They sat on the grass. They watched the other birds and ducks. They felt peaceful. They enjoyed the park.

"Oh, Sara, you have a fever. You need to stay in bed and drink some water. You can't go to school today," Mommy said.

"But I want to go to school, Mommy. Today is important. We have a sack race and I want to win," Sara said.

Liz followed him and looked over his shoulder. She saw a lot of socks and underwear, but nothing else. She was bored.

"This drawer is no good, Tim. There is no treasure here. Let's try another one," she said, pulling him away.

"Ah, a monster!" Tim shouted, dropping the drawer handle. He ran to the other side of the room, scared.

Liz laughed and took off the mask. She saw Tim under the bed and felt sorry for him.

"Wow, this is the best bone ever!" he said to himself. "I will cover it with dirt and keep it safe. No one will find it here."

But he did not see that a little cat was watching him. The cat was curious and hungry. She wanted to see what the dog had. She waited until the dog left and then ran to the hole. She used her paws to uncover the bone.

"Ha, this is a nice bone!" she said. "I will take it and eat it. Thank you, silly dog!"

She picked up the bone with her mouth and ran away. But she did not see that the dog was coming back. He had forgotten something and wanted to check on his bone. He saw the cat with his bone and got very angry.

"Hey, that is my bone!" he barked. "Give it back, you bad cat!"

He chased the cat across the park. The cat was fast, but the dog was faster. He caught up with her and snatched the bone from her mouth. He growled and showed his teeth.

"This is my bone, and you can't have it!" he said. "Go away, and don't come back!"

"Ha, this is still a nice bone!" she said. "I will try again and eat it. Sorry, silly dog!"

"Ha, this is a tasty bone!" he said. "I will take it and eat it. Thank you, silly cat and silly dog!"

One day, Tommy saw a new friend in the pool. It was a duck who had flown in from the pond nearby. The duck was swimming and quacking happily. Tommy was curious and wanted to say hello. He ran to the edge of the pool and barked.

"Who are you?" he asked the duck.

"I'm Ducky. I'm looking for a place to rest and swim. Can I join you?" the duck answered.

Tommy was a friendly dog, but he was also a little anxious. He had never met a duck before. He wondered if the duck would be nice or mean. He wondered if the duck would share his toys or take them away. He wondered if the duck would bite his tail or his ears.

"Um, okay. You can swim with me. But be careful. Don't splash me too much. And don't touch my ball. It's mine." Tommy said.

Ducky nodded and smiled. He swam over to Tommy and gave him a gentle nudge with his beak.

"Thank you, Tommy. You're very kind. Don't worry. I won't hurt you or your ball. I just want to have fun. Do you want to play a game with me?" Ducky asked.

Tommy felt his anxiety melt away. He realized that Ducky was not a threat, but a friend. He wagged his tail and nodded.

"Sure, Ducky. I want to play with you. What game do you want to play?" Tommy asked.

Ducky thought for a moment and then said.

"How about tag? I'll be it. You have to run away from me. If I touch you with my beak, you're it. And then you have to chase me. Ready, set, go!" Ducky said.

Tommy laughed and agreed. He ran away from Ducky, who followed him with his wings flapping. They chased each other around the pool, having a lot of fun. They swam and splashed and giggled. They used their paws and their beaks to tag each other. They became good friends and played until the sun set. Tommy was happy that he had met Ducky. He learned that new friends can be fun and nice, even if they are different. He hoped that Ducky would come back again. He had a new swimming buddy.

"Fire! Fire!" Lily screamed.

"Those were not pencils. Those were matches. Matches are very dangerous. They can start fires and burn things and hurt people. You should never play with matches. Do you understand?" Mom said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They did not want to play with matches again.

"Mom, we are sorry. We did not know. We were just trying to draw," Lily said.

Tom and Lily said, "OK."

Tom and Lily said, "OK."

They went inside and had some cookies. They learned a lesson. They did not want to discover matches again.

Ben was envious of Lily's rocks. He wanted to have them for himself. He said, "These rocks are not very good. They are dirty and boring. You should give them to me. I can make them better."

Ben said, "She has some rocks that I want, but she won't give them to me. I am a lawyer and I can sue her."

Lily's dad said, "You are not a lawyer. You are a liar. You are a bully and a thief. You can't sue anyone. You can't take anyone's rocks. You should be ashamed of yourself."

Ben was embarrassed and ashamed. He realized he was wrong and mean. He said, "I'm sorry. I was envious of her rocks. I don't have any rocks of my own. I lied about being a lawyer. I just wanted to impress her."

Lily's dad said, "You don't need to lie or be envious to impress anyone. You need to be honest and kind. You need to respect other people's things. You need to apologize to Lily and leave her alone."

Lily said, "Okay, dad. I love you. And I love my rocks."

The moral of the story is: Don't be envious of what others have. Be honest and kind. Respect other people's things. Collect your own rocks.

But then, Lily saw that they had no eggs. She started to worry. How could they make a cake without eggs? She asked her dad what to do. He said they could go to the store and buy some eggs. He said they had enough time.

Lily and her dad put on their coats and shoes and went to the car. They drove to the store. Lily saw many things in the store. She saw fruits and vegetables and bread and cheese. She saw toys and books and candy. She wanted to look at everything.

But her dad said they had to hurry. He said they only needed eggs. He took a carton of eggs and paid for them. He said they had to go back to the car. He said they had to bake the cake.

Lily and her dad got in the car and drove back home. Lily hoped they would make it in time. She hoped the cake would be yummy. She hoped her mom would like it.

They got home and went to the kitchen. They mixed the flour and the eggs and the sugar. They poured the batter in a pan and put it in the oven. They waited for the cake to bake. Lily watched the clock. She saw the hands move. She saw the cake rise. She smelled the yummy smell.

Her dad said it was time to take the cake out. He used oven mitts and took the pan out. He put it on a rack to cool. He said they had to wait a little bit. He said they had to put icing and sprinkles on the cake.

Lily waited and waited. She was very excited. She wanted to see the cake. She wanted to taste the cake. She wanted to give the cake to her mom.

Finally, her dad said the cake was ready. He gave Lily a knife and a spatula. He helped her spread the icing on the cake. He helped her sprinkle the sprinkles on the cake. He helped her write "Happy Birthday Mom" on the cake.

The cake looked very pretty. It looked very yummy. Lily was very proud. She said thank you to her dad. He said thank you to her. He said they did a great job.

They put the cake on a plate and covered it with a cloth. They hid it in the living room. They waited for mom to come home. They heard the door open. They heard mom's voice. They ran to the door and hugged her. They said happy birthday to her. They said they had a surprise for her.

They took her to the living room and showed her the cake. Mom's eyes got big. She smiled. She said wow. She said it was the most beautiful cake she ever saw. She said it looked very yummy. She said she loved it. She said she loved Lily and dad.

She hugged them and kissed them. She said thank you to them. She said they were the best. She said they made her very happy.

They cut the cake and ate it. It was very yummy. They all enjoyed it. They all laughed and talked. They all had a good time.

Lily was very happy. She was not worried anymore. She had made a cake for her mom. She had made her mom happy. She had made her dad happy. She had made herself happy.

She thought baking was fun. She thought she would bake more cakes. She thought she would try new things. She thought she would learn more words.

She thought she was a big girl. She thought she was a good girl. She thought she was a happy girl.

Lily nodded and smiled. She liked music too. Ben put the CD in the player and turned it on. The music was very fun and loud. Ben and Lily started to dance and jump. They had a lot of fun.

But Lily's mom did not like the music. She was upset. She came to the room and said, "What is this noise? Turn it off! It is too loud and rude. It hurts my ears."

Ben and Lily stopped dancing and jumping. They looked at Lily's mom. They were scared. Ben said, "I'm sorry, Lily's mom. This is my favorite music. It is not noise. It is fun and loud."

Lily's mom said, "I don't care. I don't like it. It is not good music. You have to turn it off. And you have to go home, Ben. You can't play here anymore."

Ben and Lily were very sad. They did not understand why Lily's mom was so upset. They liked the music. They liked to play together. They did not want to go home. They did not want to stop being friends.

But they had to accept what Lily's mom said. They turned off the music. Ben took his CD and said goodbye to Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I hope you are not mad at me. I still like you. You are still my best friend."

Ben and Lily were playing in the backyard with their toy cars. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Sometimes they would crash into each other and laugh.

But then they saw a big bird on the roof of their house. It was black and white and had a long yellow beak. It was making loud noises too.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

Ben shrugged. "I don't know. Maybe a duck?"

Lily shook her head. "No, ducks are not black and white. And they don't go on roofs. They go in ponds."

Ben frowned. "Well, maybe it's a penguin?"

Lily rolled her eyes. "No, penguins are not noisy. And they don't go on roofs. They go in snow."

Ben thought hard. He wanted to explain what the bird was, but he didn't know. He wished his mom or dad were here. They would know.

Then the bird flew down from the roof and landed near them. It looked at them with its shiny eyes and opened its beak.

"Hello, children," it said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Ben and Lily gasped. They had never heard a bird talk before. They were scared and amazed.

"Who are you?" Ben asked.

"I'm a magpie," the bird said. "I like shiny things and I like to talk. I saw your toy cars and I wanted to see them. They are very shiny and pretty."

Ben and Lily looked at their toy cars. They were shiny and pretty. They liked them too.

But they didn't like the magpie. He was crazy and rude. He had no right to take their toy cars.

"Go away," Lily said. "These are our toy cars. You can't have them."

The magpie tilted his head. "Why not? I like them. And I'm bigger than you. I can take them if I want."

He reached his beak to grab one of the toy cars. Ben and Lily shouted and tried to stop him. They were angry and scared. They wanted their toy cars back.

"Help!" they cried. "Mom! Dad! There's a crazy bird on our toy cars!"

One day, Tom and Lily went to the farm with their mom. They saw many animals, like cows, sheep, chickens and horses. They liked to watch them and feed them. But there was one animal that they did not know. It was big and pink and had a curly tail. It made a loud noise like "oink oink".

"What is that?" Tom asked his mom.

"That is a pig," mom explained. "Pigs are animals that live on farms. They like to eat and roll in the mud. They give us meat and bacon."

Tom and Lily nodded. They wanted to see the pig closer. They walked to the fence where the pig was. The pig saw them and came to them. It sniffed them with its nose and rubbed its head on the fence.

"Hello, pig," Lily said. "You are very cute. Can we pet you?"

The pig oinked and wagged its tail. It seemed to like them. Tom and Lily reached out their hands to touch the pig. But then, something unknown happened. The pig opened its mouth and bit Tom's finger. Tom screamed and pulled his hand back. He started to cry. The pig oinked again and ran away.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The pig bit me! Why did it do that?"

Mom ran to Tom and hugged him. She looked at his finger. It was red and sore, but not bleeding.

"I'm sorry, Tom," mom said. "The pig did not mean to hurt you. Sometimes, pigs bite when they are scared or hungry. Maybe the pig thought your finger was food. You have to be careful when you touch unknown animals. They might not like it."

Tom nodded. He felt better. Mom gave him a band-aid and a kiss. Lily gave him a hug and a cookie.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, I'm okay," Tom said. "But I don't like pigs anymore. They are mean and rude."

Lily smiled. She still liked pigs. She thought they were funny and silly.

"Maybe the pig was just playing with you," she said. "Maybe it wanted to be your friend."

Tom shook his head. He did not believe her. He did not want to be friends with a pig. He liked the other animals better. He decided to stay away from the pig for the rest of the day. He hoped the pig would not bite him again.

Lily was a very intelligent girl. She liked to read books and learn new things. She also liked to make crafts with paper, scissors and glue. She had many colorful papers and stickers in her room.

One day, she wanted to make a card for her friend Sam, who was sick. She cut out a big heart from red paper and wrote "Get well soon" on it. Then she looked for some glue to stick the heart on a white card. But she could not find any glue. She searched in her drawers, her shelves and her backpack. She only found a bottle of water, a pencil and a banana.

She was sad and did not know what to do. She asked her mom for help. Her mom was very kind and smart. She said, "Lily, I have an idea. Why don't you use the water and the pencil to make glue? You can recommend this to your friends too. It is easy and fun."

Lily was curious and happy. She said, "How do I do that, mom?" Her mom said, "You need to peel the banana and mash it with a fork. Then you need to add some water and stir it well. You will get a sticky paste that you can use as glue. You can use the pencil to draw some dots or lines on the paper where you want to stick the heart. Then you can spread the paste on the heart and press it on the paper. It will dry and stick very well."

Lily followed her mom's instructions and made her own glue. She was amazed and proud. She used it to make a beautiful card for Sam. She also wrote "I made this glue with a banana" on the back of the card. She thought Sam would like it and feel better. She thanked her mom and gave her a hug. She said, "Mom, you are the most intelligent and the best. I will recommend this glue to all my friends." Her mom smiled and said, "You are very intelligent and creative too, Lily. I love you."

One day, Lila saw a shiny thing in the water. She was curious and wanted to see what it was. She swam towards it, forgetting her mother's words. She did not notice that the river was getting faster and deeper. She reached the shiny thing and saw that it was a bottle. She tried to grab it, but it slipped from her paws.

"Help!" she cried. "I'm stuck!"

She looked around and saw that she was far away from her home. She did not know where she was. She was scared and cold. She wished she had listened to her mother.

Then she heard a voice. It was her father. He had heard her cry and followed the river. He saw her trapped by the bottle and the current. He quickly swam to her and pushed the bottle away. He grabbed her by the scruff and carried her to the shore.

"Lila, are you okay?" he asked.

He hugged her and licked her fur. He felt her soft and warm.

"Lila, why did you wander so far? You know it's dangerous. Your mother was very worried about you," he said.

They snuggled together and waited for her mother to come. They were happy and safe. Lila learned her lesson. She never wandered again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide on the grass. But they had to be careful not to get too dirty. Their mom had told them not to go near the mud.

"Mud is bad," mom had said. "It makes your clothes and shoes dirty. And it can make you sick if you eat it. So stay away from the mud, okay?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They did not want to make mom angry or sad. They wanted to be good children. But the mud looked interesting. It was brown and wet and sticky. It made funny shapes and sounds when they touched it.

"Can we play with the mud, just a little bit?" Ben asked Lily. He picked up a stick and poked the mud.

"No, Ben, we can't," Lily said. She pulled Ben away from the mud. "Mom said no. We have to prevent the mud from getting on us. Do you want to get in trouble?"

Ben sighed. He did not want to get in trouble. But he was curious about the mud. He wondered what it felt like and smelled like and tasted like. He thought it would be fun to make mud pies and mud castles and mud animals.

"Come on, Lily, let's play with the mud," Ben said. He tried to sneak back to the mud.

"No, Ben, stop!" Lily said. She ran after Ben and grabbed his hand. "We can't play with the mud. It's bad. It's dirty. It's yucky. Let's play with something else. Look, there's a swing and a slide and a seesaw. They are more fun than the mud."

Ben looked at the swing and the slide and the seesaw. They were fun. But they were not as interesting as the mud. He still wanted to play with the mud. He pulled his hand away from Lily and ran to the mud.

"Ben, no!" Lily shouted. She followed Ben and tried to stop him. But it was too late. Ben had reached the mud and jumped into it. He splashed and laughed and rolled in the mud. He was covered in mud from head to toe. He looked like a mud monster.

"Ben, what have you done?" Lily cried. She was shocked and scared. She did not want to join Ben in the mud. She did not want to get dirty and sick. She did not want to make mom angry and sad. She wanted to prevent the mud from getting on her. But how could she do that? How could she get Ben out of the mud? How could she clean him up? How could she explain to mom what had happened?

She did not know what to do. She wished she had prevented Ben from playing with the mud. She wished they had listened to mom. She wished they had stayed away from the mud. She wished they had played with something else. She wished the mud was not so interesting.

Ben likes to fly his kite in the park. He has a red kite with a long tail. He flies it high in the sky and makes it go up and down. He feels happy when he sees his kite.

One day, it is very windy. Ben goes to the park with his kite. He runs and lets go of his kite. But the wind is too strong. The kite flies away from Ben. He tries to catch it, but he can't. He sees his kite get stuck in a tree. He feels sad.

He asks his dad to help him get his kite. His dad climbs the tree and gets the kite. But the kite is dirty. It has mud and leaves on it. Ben feels sorry for his kite.

His dad says, "Don't worry, Ben. We can clean your kite. Let's go home and polish it." Ben nods and smiles. He holds his kite and his dad's hand. They go home and polish the kite. They use a cloth and some water. They make the kite shiny and red again. Ben feels happy.

The next day, it is not windy. Ben goes to the park with his kite. He flies it high in the sky and makes it go up and down. He sees his kite sparkle in the sun. He feels proud of his kite. He says, "Thank you, dad, for polishing my kite. I love my kite." His dad hugs him and says, "You're welcome, Ben. I love you."

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. Sometimes they help their mom and dad with work. Work is important, mom and dad say.

One day, mom and dad have to go to a big work. They ask Tom and Lily to stay with grandma. Grandma is nice and fun. She makes cookies and reads stories. Tom and Lily are happy.

But after a while, Tom and Lily miss mom and dad. They wonder what they are doing at the big work. They want to talk to them.

"Can we call mom and dad, grandma?" Tom asks.

"Sure, my dear. Let me get the phone," grandma says.

She leans over the table and picks up the phone. She dials the number and gives the phone to Tom.

"Hi, mom. Hi, dad. It's Tom," Tom says.

"Hi, Tom. How are you? How is Lily? How is grandma?" mom says.

"We are good. We are having fun. Grandma is nice. But we miss you. What are you doing at the big work?" Tom says.

"We are doing some important work, Tom. We are talking to some people and writing some papers. We are trying to help other people," dad says.

"That sounds hard. Do you like it?" Tom says.

"We like it, Tom. But we also miss you. We love you very much. We will be home soon," mom says.

"We love you too, mom. We love you too, dad. Bye," Tom says.

He gives the phone to Lily. Lily talks to mom and dad too. She tells them about the cookies and the stories. She says she loves them and bye.

Tom and Lily hug grandma. They feel better. They know mom and dad are doing important work. They know they will be home soon. They go back to play with their toys and books. They are happy.

One day, Sara had a friend over to play. His name was Ben. Ben liked to make a mess. He took out all of Sara's toys and threw them around the room. He mixed up the dolls, the cars, and the books. He laughed and said it was fun. Sara felt angry and sad. She did not like to see her toys in a mess.

Sara told Ben to stop. She said she wanted to organize her toys. Ben did not listen. He kept throwing the toys. Sara started to cry. She felt embarrassed that her friend did not respect her toys. She wished he would go away.

Sara's mom heard her cry. She came to the room and saw the mess. She asked Sara what happened. Sara told her that Ben was making a mess and did not listen to her. Sara's mom said she was sorry. She told Ben that he had to help Sara organize her toys. She said that was the polite thing to do.

Ben felt ashamed. He realized he had been rude to Sara. He said he was sorry. He helped Sara organize her toys. He put the dolls in the big box, the cars in the small box, and the books in the basket. He said he liked Sara's toys. He said he wanted to be her friend.

Sara felt better. She thanked Ben for helping her. She said she liked him too. She said they could play together again. She said they could organize her toys or do something else. She said she wanted to have fun with him.

Sara and Ben hugged. They felt happy. They learned to respect each other's toys and feelings. They learned to organize and to play. They learned to be good friends.

Ben ran to help his sister. He picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. He shouted, "Go away, bad dog! Leave Lily alone!"

A lady came running after the dog. She was the dog's owner. She called his name and put a leash on him. She said, "I'm so sorry, kids. He's a friendly dog, but he doesn't know his manners. He just wanted to play with you."

Lily and Ben were still scared and angry. They did not want to play with the dog. They wanted their toy cars back. They said, "No, thank you. We don't like your dog. He's too big and noisy. He scared us and ruined our game."

The lady said, "I'm sorry, again. He didn't mean to. He's still a puppy. He needs to learn how to behave. Come on, boy, let's go home."

She took the dog away. Lily and Ben picked up their toy cars and hugged each other. They were glad the dog was gone. They decided to play somewhere else. They hoped they would not see the dog again.

They follow Mom to a big hole in the ground. They see many people and stairs. Mom says, "This is the subway station. We have to go down the stairs and buy tickets. Then we can get on the train that goes under the ground."

Anna and Ben are curious. They wonder what the train looks like. They wonder why it goes under the ground. They wonder if it is fun or scary. They hold Mom's hand and go down the stairs.

They hear a loud noise. They see a big metal snake with windows and doors. It stops at the platform. Mom says, "This is the subway train. We have to get in quickly and find a seat. The doors will close soon."

Anna and Ben are nervous. They think the train is scary. It is dark and noisy and crowded. They see strange faces and hear strange sounds. They squeeze Mom's hand and get in the train.

The train starts to move. It goes very fast. It makes a whooshing sound. It shakes and bumps. Anna and Ben feel dizzy and scared. They close their eyes and hug Mom.

Mom says, "Don't worry, my loves. The subway is safe and fast. It will take us to the park where we can play and have fun. It will be over soon. Just breathe and relax."

Anna and Ben try to listen to Mom. They wonder if the park is nice. They wonder if they will see birds and flowers and swings. They wonder if they will like the subway more when they go back. They open their eyes and look out the window. They see a light at the end of the tunnel.

Lily liked to sew. She had a box of cloth and thread and needles. She made dolls and animals and hats. She gave some to her friends and some to her family. She was very popular.

One day, Lily wanted to make a big bear. She found a brown cloth and cut out two shapes. She sewed them together with a stitch. She left a hole to put in some cotton. She looked for her cotton, but she could not find it. She asked her mom.

"Mom, where is my cotton?" Lily said.

"Sorry, Lily, I used it to make a pillow for your dad. He needed a new one. He had a bad neck," Mom said.

Lily was sad. She wanted to finish her bear. She looked around the house for something else to fill her bear. She saw a bag of popcorn on the table. She had an idea.

She took some popcorn and put it in her bear. She sewed the hole with a stitch. She made a face with buttons and yarn. She was happy. She had a big bear.

She showed her bear to her mom. Mom smiled.

"That's a very creative bear, Lily. What did you use to fill it?" Mom said.

"Popcorn!" Lily said.

Mom laughed. "Popcorn? That's funny. But be careful, Lily. Popcorn can get old and smelly. And bugs might like it too."

Lily did not think about that. She hugged her bear and took it to her room. She put it on her bed. She was proud of her bear.

The next day, Lily went to school. She took her bear with her. She wanted to show it to her friends. She thought they would like it. She thought she would be more popular.

But when she got to school, something was wrong. Her bear was not big and fluffy anymore. It was small and wrinkly. Some of the popcorn had popped out of the stitch. Some of it had turned yellow and green. It smelled bad. And there were ants crawling on it.

Lily was shocked. She did not understand. She felt sad and embarrassed. She hid her bear in her backpack. She did not show it to anyone.

She learned a lesson that day. She learned that popcorn is not a good thing to fill a bear with. She learned that some things do not last. She learned that being popular is not as important as being smart and careful.

She went home and threw away her bear. She asked her mom for some new cotton. She decided to make a new bear. A better bear. A bear that would not smell or pop or attract bugs. A bear that she would love and keep. A bear that would be her friend.

She asked her mom and dad, her big brother, and her grandma to sit on the couch and watch her. She put on a sparkly dress and a cape, and she said, "Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Mia's magic show!"

After the game, Timmy and his friends went to the playground. They saw a blue bird in a cage. Timmy asked the owner why the bird was locked up. The owner said, "I don't want the bird to fly away." Timmy said, "That's not fair. The bird should be free to fly wherever it wants."

The moral of the story is that it's important to have fun and not just focus on winning. Also, it's not right to lock up animals or anything that should be free.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and wanted to eat at a restaurant. He asked his mom if they could go to a restaurant. His mom said, "Sure, let's go find one."

They walked down the street and saw a tall building with a sign that said "restaurant". They went inside and sat down at a table. Timmy looked around and saw that the chairs were tall too.

Suddenly, the waiter appeared and asked what they wanted to eat. Timmy said, "I want pizza, please." His mom ordered a salad. They waited for their food and when it arrived, Timmy was very happy. He ate his pizza and said, "This is yummy!"

After they finished their meal, Timmy said, "Thank you, Mom. That was fun." His mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. Let's go home now." And so they did. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy hated beans. He would never eat them, no matter how much his mom tried to convince him they were good for him. One day, Timmy went to his friend's house for dinner. His friend's mom made a big pot of beans for everyone to eat. Timmy didn't want to be rude, so he tried a small spoonful. To his surprise, he liked them!

Timmy realized that he had been missing out on something good just because he thought he didn't like it. He decided to be more compassionate towards foods he didn't like and give them a chance. From that day on, Timmy tried new foods and discovered many new favorites. He learned that it's important to keep an open mind and not hate things without trying them first.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was her dog barking. Lily became alert and looked around. She saw a little bird sitting on a branch. The bird was chirping and singing a happy song. After a few minutes, the bird flew away. Lily finished her ice cream and felt content. She hugged her mommy and went to bed with a happy heart. She dreamed of sharing ice cream with all the little birds in the world. The end.

One day, the rhinoceros was walking through the jungle when he saw a little bird sitting on a rock. The bird was chirping and singing a beautiful song. The rhinoceros stopped and listened to the bird's song. He thought it was the most beautiful thing he had ever heard.

Tim put the bow on the front of his train and smiled. He thought his train looked very pretty with the bow. He pushed the button and made the train move on the tracks.

"Look, Amy, look at my train. It has a bow. It is a special train," he said.

Amy was very upset. She did not think Tim's train was special. She thought he was mean and rude. She wanted her bow back. She ran to the train and tried to pull the bow off. Tim did not let her. He held the bow and pushed Amy away.

"Stop, Amy, stop. This is my train and my bow. You can't have it," he said.

Amy and Tim started to fight over the bow. They pulled and pushed and yelled. They did not hear their mom coming into the living room. She saw them fighting and was not happy.

"What are you two doing? Why are you fighting?" she asked.

Tim and Amy stopped and looked at their mom. They both tried to explain.

"He took my bow, mom. He won't give it back," Amy said.

"She won't let me play with her bow, mom. She is selfish," Tim said.

Mom looked at the train and the bow. She saw that they were both nice toys, but they were not meant for each other. She had an idea.

"Tim, Amy, listen to me. I know you both like your toys, but you have to share and be kind. How about this? Tim, you can play with Amy's bow for a little while, but then you have to give it back to her. Amy, you can play with Tim's train for a little while, but then you have to give it back to him. That way, you can both try something new and have fun. What do you think?" she said.

Tim and Amy thought about it. They did not like the idea at first, but they also did not want to make their mom angry. They agreed to try it.

"Okay, mom. We will share and be kind," they said.

Mom smiled and gave them a hug. She helped them swap their toys and showed them how to play with them. Tim put the bow on his hair and pretended to be a princess. Amy made the train go fast and slow and made noises. They laughed and had fun. They learned that sharing and being kind was better than fighting and being mean. They also learned that sometimes, trying something new can be fun. They thanked their mom and each other for the toys. They were happy and played nicely. Mom was proud of them. She watched them play and smiled.

She said she was sorry, but they had missed their chance. She said maybe next time they would listen and come to the table when she asked them.

Tim and Sam realized they had made a big mistake. They had lost their favorite toy and their special dish. They had made their mom unhappy and themselves unhappy. Lila and Ben were friends who lived in a hut near the forest. They liked to play and explore together, but sometimes they argued over toys and food. One day, they found a big basket of apples in the forest. They were very happy and wanted to take them home.

"Let's share the apples," Lila said. "You can have half and I can have half."

"No, I want more apples," Ben said. "I found them first. You can have only one."

"That's not fair," Lila said. "You are not a good friend. I don't want to play with you anymore."

Lila ran away, crying. Ben took the basket and went back to the hut. He ate some apples, but he felt lonely and sad. He missed Lila and wished he had been nicer to her.

Meanwhile, Lila met a fox in the forest. The fox was hungry and saw the apple in Lila's hand. He smiled and said, "Hello, little girl. What a nice apple you have. Can I have a bite?"

Lila was scared of the fox, but she remembered what her mother had taught her. She said, "No, thank you. This is my apple. But I can give you something else. I have some bread and cheese in my bag. You can have them if you are hungry."

The fox was surprised and touched by Lila's kindness. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very generous and good. You have a big heart. I will not hurt you. I will be your friend."

Lila and the fox shared the bread and cheese. They talked and laughed and had fun. Lila felt happy and forgot about Ben and the apples.

Later, Lila and the fox went back to the hut. They saw Ben sitting outside, looking sad and bored. He had eaten all the apples, but he still felt hungry and sick. He saw Lila and the fox and felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "Lila, I'm sorry. I was mean and greedy. I should have shared the apples with you. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends again?"

Lila smiled and said, "Of course, Ben. I forgive you. We can be friends again. But you have to learn to care for others and not only for yourself. Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy. Look, I have a new friend. This is the fox. He was hungry and I gave him some food. He is very nice and friendly. He can be our friend too."

Ben was happy and grateful. He said, "Thank you, Lila. You are a good friend. And hello, fox. You are welcome to our hut. Can we play together?"

Lila, Ben, and the fox hugged and played together. They learned to care for each other and share what they had. They lived happily in the hut near the forest.

The end.

"Maybe massage is good for tired people," Timmy thought. He decided to try it on his teddy bear. He put the book on the floor and picked up his teddy bear. He lay down on his bed and put the teddy bear on his chest. He looked at the book and copied what the people did. He rubbed the teddy bear's back with his hands. He squeezed the teddy bear's feet with his fingers. He tapped the teddy bear's head with his palm.

"Does that feel good, teddy?" Timmy asked. The teddy bear did not answer. He was a toy. He could not talk. But Timmy pretended that he could. He imagined that the teddy bear was happy and relaxed. He smiled and hugged the teddy bear. He felt warm and sleepy.

Suddenly, he heard a knock on the door. It was his mom. She opened the door and saw Timmy and the teddy bear on the bed. She also saw her book on the floor.

"Timmy, what are you doing?" she asked.

"I'm giving teddy a massage, mom," Timmy said. "He was very tired and I wanted to help him."

Mom smiled and walked to the bed. She picked up her book and looked at the cover. It said "How to Massage Your Helpless Partner". She laughed and shook her head.

"Timmy, this book is not for you. It's for grown-ups. Massage is a nice way to show love and care, but it's also a special way to make someone feel good. You need to ask permission before you touch someone like that. And you need to be careful not to hurt them."

"I'm sorry, mom," Timmy said. "I didn't know. I just wanted to make teddy happy. He's my best friend."

Mom hugged Timmy and kissed his cheek. She was not angry. She was proud of Timmy for being kind and gentle.

"I know, sweetie. You're a good boy. And teddy is lucky to have you. But next time, please use a different book. Maybe one with stories or pictures that you like. And if you want a massage, you can ask me. I'll be happy to give you one."

"Really, mom?" Timmy asked.

"Really, Timmy," mom said.

"Can you give me one now?" Timmy asked.

"Sure, Timmy," mom said.

She lay down next to Timmy and the teddy bear. She put her arm around them and rubbed Timmy's back. She whispered in his ear.

"Good night, Timmy. I love you."

"Good night, mom. I love you too," Timmy said.

He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of massage and teddy bears and mom. He was happy.

"Can I try your jelly?" Lily asked Ben. "I want to see if it is different from mine."

"Sure, you can try it," Ben said. "But you have to give me some of yours too."

They swapped their jars and spread some jelly on their bread. They took a big bite and smiled.

"Mmm, this is good!" Lily said. "Your jelly is like mine, but a little more sour."

"I like your jelly too," Ben said. "It is like mine, but a little more sweet."

They were happy to share their jelly and try something new. They finished their sandwiches and put the jars back on the shelf.

But they did not notice that they had mixed up the jars. Lily's red jar had a label that said "raspberry", and Ben's purple jar had a label that said "grape". They had put the wrong jars in the wrong places.

Later, their mom came home and wanted to make a cake. She needed to add some jelly to the batter, to make it moist and fruity. She reached for the red jar, thinking it was raspberry. She did not read the label, because she trusted her children to be reliable and put things back where they belonged.

She added a big spoonful of jelly to the batter and stirred it well. She poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. She was looking forward to having a delicious raspberry cake for dessert.

But when she took the cake out of the oven, she smelled something strange. She cut a slice and tasted it. She made a face and spat it out.

"Yuck, this is not raspberry, this is grape!" she exclaimed. "Who switched the jars?"

She called Lily and Ben to the kitchen and showed them the cake. They looked at each other and realized their mistake. They felt sorry and guilty.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We swapped the jars when we made sandwiches, and we forgot to put them back."

They apologized and hugged their mom. She was not too angry, because she knew they did not mean to ruin the cake. She decided to make another cake, with the right jelly this time. She asked Lily and Ben to help her, and to be more careful and reliable in the future.

They agreed and learned their lesson. They helped their mom make a new cake, and they enjoyed it together. They still liked to add jelly to their bread, but they always checked the labels first.

They searched all around the farm until they finally found the toy. The boy was so happy and gave Jack a big hug. From that day on, the boy visited Jack's farm every week and they became good friends.

From that day on, the bird would always go back to the hanger and spin around. It was its favorite thing to do. The hanger became the bird's new home and it never felt poor again.

They both grabbed the gem and pulled hard. They did not want to share. They started to yell and fight.

"Stop it! Stop it!" a voice said. It was their mom. She came into the room and saw them fighting. She was angry. "What are you doing? Why are you fighting over a gem? It is just a toy! You have to share and be nice to each other!"

"But mom, this gem is special!" Ben said. "It can do magic! Watch!"

He held the gem in his hand and said, "I wish Mia was a frog!"

The gem glowed and made a sound. Mia felt a strange feeling. She looked at her hands and feet. They were green and slimy. She had turned into a frog!

"Ribbit! Ribbit!" she croaked. She was scared and sad.

"Ben, what did you do?" mom said. She was shocked and worried. "How did you do that? How can we change her back?"

"I don't know, mom!" Ben said. He was sorry and scared too. "I just repeated what I heard on TV! It was a show about magic gems!"

Mom looked at the gem. She saw a label on it. It said, "Warning: Do not repeat any wishes while holding this gem. They will come true. No refunds. No returns."

Mom realized that the gem was not a toy. It was a real magic gem. And it was a very stupid gem. It did not care about people's feelings. It only did what it heard.

She tried to repeat a wish to change Mia back. But nothing happened. The gem did not glow or make a sound. It did not work anymore. It had used up all its magic.

Mom hugged Ben and the frog. She cried. She did not know what to do. She wished she had never bought the gem from the strange man at the park. She wished she had never let Ben and Mia play with it. She wished they could be happy again. But her wishes did not come true. The end.

"Ben, please come with me," Mia said. "The fog is fun. We can pretend we are in a fairy tale. And we can take one toy each. Which one do you want?"

Ben looked at his toys. He had a hard time choosing. He liked them all. But he saw Mia's eyes and he saw how much she wanted to go. He loved his sister, even if she was bossy.

"Okay, okay, I will go," Ben said. He picked his teddy bear and followed Mia.

Mama smiled and said, "Have fun, my loves. But don't stay too long."

Timmy asked Mr. Smith what a license was, and Mr. Smith explained that it was a special paper that said Timmy was allowed to ride his bike on the street. Timmy was so happy to finally understand what a license was.

From that day on, Timmy made sure to always have his bike license with him when he rode his bike. He even told his friends about it and they all got their own bike licenses too. Timmy learned that it's important to ask questions and reply when someone explains something to you. And that having a license is a clear way to show that you are responsible and allowed to do something.

"I am hunting for deer," the hunter replied. "I observe the forest to find them."

Timmy didn't like the idea of the hunter hurting the deer. "I don't like hunting," he said.

The hunter smiled. "That's okay, Timmy. Not everyone likes hunting. I'll be careful not to hurt any animals you like." 

Timmy was happy that the hunter was being kind. He waved goodbye and continued playing in the forest.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara cried. "It is biting me!"

Tom saw the other thing and laughed. He knew what it was. It was not a mouse. It was a harmless mole.

"Don't worry, Sara. It is not biting you. It is just curious. It is a mole. Moles live under the ground and dig tunnels. They have poor eyesight and use their noses to smell," Tom explained.

Sara stopped crying and looked at the mole on her toe. It was harmless. It was just curious. She laughed too and put the mole in her hand next to the other one. They squeaked and cuddled.

"They are so cute, Tom. Can we keep them?" Sara asked.

Tom shook his head. "No, Sara. We can't keep them. They belong to the garden. They need to dig and eat worms and be free. We can play with them for a while, but then we have to let them go," Tom said.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big goose by the pond. The goose had white feathers and a long neck. Tim and Sam wanted to touch the goose, so they ran towards it.

"Hello, goose!" Tim said. "Can we be your friends?"

But the goose did not want to be their friend. The goose was angry and scared. It hissed and flapped its wings. It bit Tim's hand with its hard beak.

"Ow!" Tim cried. "The goose is mean!"

Sam was brave and tried to help his brother. He picked up a stick and waved it at the goose. He shouted, "Go away, goose! Leave Tim alone!"

But the goose did not go away. It flew up in the air and swooped down at Sam. It pecked his head with its hard beak.

"Ow!" Sam cried. "The goose is mean!"

Tim and Sam ran away from the goose. They ran back to their house and told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and put band-aids on their wounds.

"I'm sorry, boys," she said. "The goose was just protecting its home. It did not want you to bother it. Next time, you should not go near the goose. You should watch it from far away."

Tim and Sam nodded. They learned their lesson. They did not want to play with the goose anymore. They decided to play with their dog instead. Their dog was nice and soft. He licked their faces and wagged his tail. He was their friend.

Sam and Mia were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big truck arrive in their street. The truck had a cooler on the back. Sam and Mia were curious and wanted to see what was inside the cooler.

They ran to the truck and climbed on the back. They opened the cooler and saw many ice creams. They were smooth and cold and had different colors. Sam and Mia smiled and took some ice creams. They did not ask anyone if they could have them. They thought no one would notice.

They ate the ice creams and felt happy. They did not know that the ice creams belonged to Mr. Lee, who sold them to people in the park. Mr. Lee was inside the truck, getting some money. He did not see Sam and Mia take his ice creams.

When Mr. Lee came back to the truck, he saw the cooler was open and many ice creams were gone. He was angry and sad. He worked hard to make the ice creams and he needed the money to buy food and clothes. He looked around and saw Sam and Mia with ice cream on their faces and hands. He knew they were the ones who took his ice creams.

He went to Sam and Mia and said, "Why did you take my ice creams? You did a bad thing. You stole from me. You should have asked me first. Now I have less ice creams to sell and less money to live. How would you feel if someone took your toys or your clothes?"

Sam and Mia felt ashamed and scared. They realized they did a bad thing. They did not think about Mr. Lee and how he needed the ice creams. They were selfish and greedy. They said they were sorry and tried to give back the ice creams, but they were already melted and dirty.

Mr. Lee said, "Sorry is not enough. You have to pay for what you took. You have to work for me and help me sell the ice creams. You have to learn to respect other people's things and to be honest and kind."

Sam and Mia nodded and agreed. They followed Mr. Lee to the park and helped him sell the ice creams. They worked hard and felt sorry for what they did. They learned their lesson and never took anything that was not theirs again.

The moral of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. It is wrong and it hurts others. Ask before you take and be grateful for what you have.

Jill and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big glass jar where they kept some bugs and worms they found. They liked to watch them crawl and wiggle inside the jar.

One day, they saw an unusual bug in the grass. It had six legs, two wings, and a long tail. It was shiny and green. They wanted to catch it and put it in their jar.

"Look, Tom, a new bug!" Jill said. "Let's get it!"

They ran after the bug, but it was fast and flew away. They chased it across the garden, until they reached the fence. The bug landed on a flower on the other side of the fence.

"Quick, Jill, give me the jar!" Tom said. He took the jar from Jill and climbed over the fence. He tried to catch the bug with the jar, but he was not careful. He dropped the jar on the ground and it broke into many pieces.

The bugs and worms in the jar escaped and crawled away. The glass pieces cut Tom's hand and made him bleed. He cried out in pain and dropped the bug. The bug flew away and was gone.

Jill heard Tom's cry and climbed over the fence. She saw the broken jar, the blood, and the bug. She felt sorry for Tom and for the bugs and worms. She hugged Tom and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. We should not have chased the bug. We should have left it alone. We should have taken care of our jar and our bugs and worms. They were our friends."

Tom nodded and said, "You're right, Jill. We were greedy and foolish. We hurt ourselves and our friends. We learned a hard lesson today."

They went back to their house and told their mom what happened. Their mom cleaned Tom's wound and bandaged it. She scolded them for being careless and cruel. She said, "You should respect all living things, even the smallest ones. They have a right to live and be free. You should not take them away from their home and trap them in a jar. You should not chase them and break them. You should be kind and gentle to them. That is the moral of your story."
