One day, two boys named Tom and Sam went to play in the forest. They liked to pretend they were hunters and warriors. They each had a wooden spear that they made from sticks and stones.

They saw a big rabbit hopping in the grass. They wanted to catch it for their lunch. They ran after it with their spears, but the rabbit was too fast and clever. It ran into a hole under a tree.

"Let me try!" said Tom. He pushed Sam aside and stuck his spear into the hole. He felt something soft and pulled it out. It was the rabbit's tail.

"Ha! I got it!" he shouted. He held the tail in his hand and laughed.

"Hey, that's not fair!" said Sam. "You took my turn! You should share the rabbit with me!"

"No, it's mine!" said Tom. "I caught it, so I keep it! Go find your own rabbit!"

He ran away with the tail, leaving Sam behind. Sam felt sad and angry. He wanted to have some of the rabbit too.

He looked around and saw another hole under a different tree. He thought maybe there was another rabbit inside. He put his spear into the hole and pushed hard. He heard a loud roar and a growl. He pulled out his spear and saw a big, sharp tooth stuck to it. It was a bear's tooth.

He looked up and saw a huge, brown bear coming out of the hole. It was angry and hungry. It saw Sam and his spear and roared again. It wanted to eat him for its lunch.

Sam was very scared. He dropped his spear and ran away as fast as he could. He screamed for help.

Tom heard Sam's scream and saw the bear chasing him. He felt sorry for Sam. He remembered that Sam was his friend and that they always played together. He decided to help him.

He ran towards the bear with his spear and the rabbit's tail. He waved them in the air and shouted at the bear.

"Hey, bear! Leave Sam alone! Look what I have! A tasty rabbit tail! You want it? Come and get it!"

The bear saw the rabbit tail and smelled it. It forgot about Sam and turned to Tom. It wanted the rabbit tail more than the boy.

Tom threw the rabbit tail far away. The bear ran after it, leaving Tom and Sam alone.

Tom and Sam hugged each other. They were happy and relieved. They picked up their spears and ran back to their home.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharing is better than fighting. They learned that friends should help each other. They learned that being greedy can be dangerous. They learned that simple words can save lives.

Sam and Mia were twins who liked to play on the beach. They lived near a big port where many ships came and went. Sometimes they saw huge ships with many things on them. They wondered what the things were and where they came from.

One day, they saw a huge ship that was very shiny and had many flags on it. It looked very pretty and different from the other ships. Sam said to Mia, "Let's go and see the shiny ship. Maybe we can find something nice on it." Mia said, "But we are not allowed to go near the port. Mom and Dad said it is dangerous. There are many cars and machines and people there. They might hurt us or yell at us." Sam said, "Don't be scared. I dare you to go with me. It will be fun. We can hide behind the boxes and barrels and nobody will see us. Come on, let's go."

Sam and Mia ran towards the port, holding hands. They did not see the sign that said "Keep Out". They did not hear the horn that warned them to stop. They did not see the big truck that was backing up towards them. They only saw the shiny ship that was waiting for them. They wanted to reach it and touch it and see what was on it.

But they never did. The truck hit them and they fell down. They screamed and cried and bled. The people in the port heard them and ran to help them. But it was too late. Sam and Mia were gone. The shiny ship sailed away, taking their dreams with it.

Tim and Lily were playing by the river. They saw a big raft with many boxes on it. The raft was floating on the water.

"Who is on the raft?" Lily asked.

"Maybe it is someone who delivers things," Tim said.

They waved at the raft, but no one waved back. The raft was too distant. They could not see anyone on it.

"Let's make our own raft," Tim said. "We can deliver our toys to each other."

They found some sticks and leaves and tied them together. They put their toys on the raft. They pushed the raft into the water.

"Bye, bye, raft," Lily said. "Have a good trip."

They ran along the river bank, following the raft. They pretended they were talking to each other on the raft.

"Hello, Lily," Tim said. "I have a teddy bear for you."

"Thank you, Tim," Lily said. "I have a ball for you."

They laughed and clapped. They had fun delivering their toys. They did not notice that the raft was getting farther and farther away.

Tim and Mia are playing with their toys on the floor. They have cars, dolls, blocks and books. They are having fun and making noises.

Mom is in the kitchen. She is making a cake for Dad's birthday. She needs eggs, flour, sugar and butter. She also needs lemon juice to make the cake sour. She likes sour cakes.

She hears Tim and Mia on the floor. They are too loud. She says, "Shh, please be quiet. You are disturbing me. I need to focus on the cake. Do not come to the kitchen."

Tim and Mia nod. They try to be quiet. But they are bored. They want to see the cake. They are curious.

They sneak to the kitchen. They see Mom is not there. She is in the bathroom. They see the cake on the table. It looks yummy. They want to taste it.

They climb on a chair. They reach for the cake. They take a big bite. But the cake is not yummy. It is sour. Very sour. They make a face. They spit out the cake. They cry.

Mom hears them. She runs to the kitchen. She sees the cake. It is ruined. She sees Tim and Mia. They are crying. She is angry. She says, "What have you done? You have spoiled the cake. You have disobeyed me. You have disturbed me. You are naughty. Go to your room. No cake for you."

Tim and Mia are sad. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We are sorry." But Mom does not listen. She sends them to their room. They have no cake. They have no toys. They have no fun. They have a bad ending.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the yard. One day, they see a big pool of water. It is from the laundry machine. It is broken.

"Let's swim in the water!" says Lily. She jumps in the pool. She splashes and laughs.

"No, Lily, we can't swim in the water!" says Ben. He is scared. He thinks Mom will be angry. "The water is dirty and messy. It is for the clothes, not for us."

But Lily does not listen. She swims and swims. She makes the water go everywhere. She makes the clothes wet and dirty. She makes the grass muddy.

Ben tries to stop her. He pulls her out of the pool. He says, "Lily, stop! You are making a big mess. Mom will be mad. We have to clean up."

But Lily does not want to clean up. She wants to swim more. She pushes Ben away. She jumps back in the pool. She says, "No, Ben, you stop! You are no fun. I like to swim. The water is cool and nice."

They start to fight. They yell and cry. They make more mess.

Mom hears them. She comes out of the house. She sees the pool of water. She sees the clothes. She sees the grass. She sees Lily and Ben. She is very angry.

She says, "Lily and Ben, what are you doing? You are not supposed to swim in the laundry water. You are supposed to help me with the laundry. You have made a big mess. You have ruined the clothes. You have wasted the water. You have to go inside. You have to take a bath. You have to say sorry."

Lily and Ben feel bad. They know they did wrong. They say sorry to Mom. They say sorry to each other. They go inside. They take a bath. They help Mom with the laundry. They promise to not swim in the laundry water again.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play with bricks. They had many bricks of different colors and shapes. They could build houses, towers, bridges and more with their bricks. They had fun every day with their bricks.

One day, they decided to prepare a big surprise for their mom and dad. They wanted to build a huge castle with all their bricks in the backyard. They worked hard and used all their bricks to make the castle. They made walls, windows, doors, towers and flags. They were very proud of their castle.

They ran inside to call their mom and dad. "Mom, dad, come and see what we made!" they shouted. "We have a big surprise for you!" Mom and dad followed them to the backyard. They were curious to see what Lila and Tom had made.

But when they got to the backyard, they saw a big mess. The wind had blown down the castle and the bricks were everywhere. Some bricks had broken the flowers, some bricks had hit the fence, some bricks had landed on the dog. The dog was barking and the flowers were sad. The fence was bent and the bricks were dirty.

Mom and dad were not glad. They were angry and sad. They scolded Lila and Tom for making such a mess. They told them to clean up the bricks and to be more careful next time. They said that bricks are not toys and that they should not build things that can fall and hurt someone or something.

Lila and Tom were not glad. They were sorry and sad. They cried and said they were sorry. They cleaned up the bricks and put them away. They learned that they should not play with bricks without permission and that they should think about the consequences of their actions. They also learned that surprises are not always good and that sometimes it is better to ask before doing something.

Tom and Lily were fishing with Dad by the lake. They had a big bucket of worms to put on their hooks. Dad showed them how to be careful with the hooks, because they were sharp and could hurt.

"Look, I got one!" Tom shouted, as he pulled his rod. A shiny fish was wiggling on his hook. He was very happy and proud.

"Good job, Tom!" Dad said. "Now, let's take the fish off the hook and put it in the basket. Be careful not to touch its teeth, it might bite you."

Tom nodded and followed Dad's instructions. He held the fish firmly and gently removed the hook from its mouth. He put the fish in the basket and smiled.

"Can I have a worm, please?" Lily asked. She wanted to catch a fish too. Dad gave her a worm and helped her put it on her hook. He told her to cast her line into the water and wait patiently.

Lily watched her bobber float on the water. She hoped a fish would come and bite her worm. She waited and waited, but nothing happened.

She felt bored and hungry. She looked at the bucket of worms. They looked juicy and tasty. She wondered what they would taste like. She reached for a worm and put it in her mouth. She started to chew it.

"Yuck!" she spat out the worm. It was slimy and bitter. She made a face and wiped her tongue. She felt sick and sorry.

"Lily, what are you doing?" Dad asked, shocked. He saw the worm on the ground and the bucket of worms next to Lily. He realized what she had done.

"I was hungry, Dad. I wanted to try a worm. But it was yucky!" Lily said, crying.

"Oh, Lily, you shouldn't eat worms. They are not food for people. They are food for fish. They could make you sick. You should only eat what I give you, okay?" Dad said, hugging her.

"Okay, Dad. I'm sorry. Can I have a sandwich, please?" Lily said, sniffling.

"Of course, sweetie. Here, have a sandwich. And some water. And a hug. And a kiss. And a smile. You'll feel better soon. And maybe you'll catch a fish too. But don't chew it, okay?" Dad said, laughing.

"Okay, Dad. I love you. And I love fishing. But not worms." Lily said, smiling.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys in the park. One day, they find a big wheel. It is red and shiny. Ben and Mia both want to play with the wheel.

"Let me have the wheel!" Ben says. He tries to grab the wheel from Mia.

"No, it is my turn!" Mia says. She holds the wheel tight.

They pull and push the wheel. They are angry and loud. They do not share the wheel. They are selfish.

A dog comes to the park. It sees the wheel. It thinks the wheel is a toy. It runs to the wheel. It bites the wheel. It makes a hole in the wheel. The air comes out of the wheel. The wheel is flat and sad.

Ben and Mia stop fighting. They look at the wheel. They feel sorry for the wheel. They feel sorry for each other.

"Sorry, Ben. I was selfish. You can have the wheel." Mia says.

"Sorry, Mia. I was selfish too. You can have the wheel." Ben says.

They decide to be friends again. They decide to share the wheel. They patch the hole in the wheel. They take turns to roll the wheel. They have fun with the wheel. They are happy and kind. They are not selfish.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. They saw many flowers that were pink, yellow, and purple. They smelled sweet and made them happy.

One day, they found a new flower that was white and had a big round center. It looked like a sun. Lily and Ben wanted to make it more colorful, so they ran to get some ink from their art box.

They dipped their brushes in the ink and painted the flower with red, blue, and green. They thought it looked beautiful and fun. They giggled and showed each other their work.

But then, they heard a voice from the flower. It said, "Why did you do that? You ruined my petals. I was waiting to bloom and show my true colors. Now I look like a mess."

Lily and Ben were scared and sorry. They did not know the flower could talk. They did not mean to hurt it. They said, "We are sorry, flower. We wanted to make you happy. We thought you would like the ink. We did not know you had your own colors."

The flower sighed and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. You were just curious and generous. But please, don't paint me again. Let me bloom in my own way. Then you can see how beautiful I am."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We promise, flower. We will wait and see. We are sorry and we love you."

The flower smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily and Ben. I love you too. Now, go and play. And come back tomorrow. I have a surprise for you."

Lily and Ben hugged the flower and ran to play. They wondered what the surprise was. They hoped it was something good. They learned to respect the flower and its colors.

Lily liked jazz. She liked the sounds of the horns and the drums and the piano. She liked to dance and clap when she heard jazz. She had a jazz CD that her dad gave her. She played it every day.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a man playing a saxophone. He was making jazz music. Lily ran to him and listened. She smiled and nodded. The man saw her and smiled back.

"Hello, little girl. Do you like jazz?" he asked.

"Yes, I do. I love jazz. It is fun and happy," Lily said.

"That's good. I love jazz too. It is my job and my passion. Do you know what a saxophone is?" he asked.

Lily shook her head. She did not know that word.

"It is this instrument. It is like a big horn with keys. You blow into it and press the keys to make different sounds. Do you want to try?" he asked.

Lily nodded. She was curious. She wanted to try. The man helped her hold the saxophone and showed her how to blow and press. Lily made a loud noise. She laughed. It was hard, but it was fun.

"Wow, you are a natural. You have a good ear for jazz. Maybe you will be a jazz musician when you grow up," he said.

Lily wondered what that meant. She wondered if she could play jazz like him. She wondered if there were other instruments that made jazz. She wondered if jazz was normal or special.

She asked the man, "Is jazz normal or special?"

The man smiled and said, "Jazz is both. It is normal because it is made by people who love music and express themselves. It is special because it is different and creative and beautiful. Jazz is a gift that we can share with others. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She understood. She liked jazz. She liked the man. She liked the park. She thanked the man and gave him a hug. She ran back to her mom and told her what she learned. Her mom smiled and hugged her.

They went home and played the jazz CD. Lily danced and clapped. She was happy. She loved jazz.

"Hi, dog. Do you want to play with us?" Lily said.

The dog barked and ran to the football. It picked it up with its mouth and ran away.

"Hey, that's our football!" Tom shouted. He ran after the dog.

Lily ran after Tom. They chased the dog around the park. The dog was fast and clever. It dodged and turned and made them fall. It thought it was a game.

"Give us our football, dog!" Tom said.

The dog stopped and looked at them. It wagged its tail and dropped the football. It barked and ran to them again. It licked their faces and jumped on them.

"Good dog. You are funny," Lily said.

One night, she picks a book about rubber ducks. She likes rubber ducks. They are yellow and soft. She has a rubber duck in her bathtub. She opens the book and starts to read.

She turns the page and reads more. "One day, it was very cold. The pond froze. I could not swim. I was stuck in the ice. Quack, quack, I was sad."

Sara feels sorry for the rubber duck. She wonders what will happen next. She turns the page and reads on.

"Then, a boy came. He saw me in the ice. He broke the ice and took me out. He put me in his pocket. He took me home. He gave me a warm bath. He played with me. Quack, quack, I was happy again."

Sara is happy for the rubber duck. She thinks the boy is nice. She finishes the book and closes it. She hugs the book and says, "I like this book. I like rubber ducks. They are cute and fun."

"Look, our snowman is smiling!" Lily said.

"Yes, he is. He likes the snow," Ben said.

They wanted to find something for his arms. They looked around and saw a pole. It was long and brown and had a red flag on top.

"Let's use the pole!" Lily said.

They ran to the pole and tried to pull it out of the ground. But it was stuck. They pulled harder and harder, but it did not move.

"Ow, this pole is too hard!" Ben said.

They heard a loud noise. It was a siren. A big truck came to the pole. It had a sign that said "Fire Station".

"Hey, kids, what are you doing?" a man said. He got out of the truck. He wore a yellow hat and a black coat. He was a fireman.

"We are making a snowman. We want the pole for his arms," Lily said.

The fireman shook his head. He looked sad.

"I'm sorry, kids, but you can't have the pole. It's a fire hydrant. We need it in case of a fire. It has water inside. If you pull it out, the water will spray everywhere and make a big mess," he said.

Lily and Ben did not know what a fire hydrant was. They did not know what a fire was. They felt sad.

"But our snowman needs arms," Ben said.

The fireman smiled. He had an idea.

"I have something else for you. Come with me," he said.

He took them to his truck. He opened a box and gave them two hoses. They were long and green and had nozzles.

"Here, you can use these hoses for your snowman's arms. They are flexible and you can bend them any way you want. They are also safe and won't make a mess," he said.

Lily and Ben thanked the fireman. They took the hoses and ran back to their snowman. They put the hoses on his sides and made them look like arms. They were very happy.

"Look, our snowman has arms!" Lily said.

"Yes, he does. And they are cool!" Ben said.

Jenny was a big girl who liked to do things by herself. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. She liked to dress herself, brush her teeth, and pack her bag for school. She was proud of her uniform, which was blue and white and had a badge with her name on it.

One day, she woke up early and got ready for school. She put on her uniform, but she did not notice that she had put her shirt on backwards. She did not mention it to her mom, who was busy making breakfast. She thought she looked fine and did not need anyone to fix her clothes.

She went to the kitchen and ate her toast and jam. She said goodbye to her mom and walked to the bus stop with her bag. She met her friend Tom, who also wore a uniform. He looked at her and smiled.

"Hi, Jenny," he said. "You look different today."

Jenny smiled back. She thought he was being nice. She did not know what he meant by different.

"Thank you, Tom," she said. "You look nice too."

They got on the bus and sat together. They talked about their favorite games and animals. They did not mention anything about Jenny's shirt.

When they got to school, they went to their classroom. Their teacher, Miss Lee, was waiting for them. She greeted them and asked them to sit down. She looked at Jenny and frowned.

"Jenny, what happened to your shirt?" she asked. "It's on backwards."

Jenny felt her face turn red. She looked down and saw that her shirt was indeed on backwards. She felt silly and embarrassed. She did not know how she had made such a mistake.

She wanted to cry, but she remembered that she was a big girl. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. She tried to act brave and smiled.

"I'm sorry, Miss Lee," she said. "I did not notice. I can fix it by myself."

Lily agreed. She put the glove back in dad's closet. She learned her lesson. She decided to be a bear only in her imagination.

When Anna and Ben came to the kitchen, they saw the eggs and toast on the table. They were sad and confused. They did not like eggs and toast. They liked waffles.

"Where are our waffles, dad?" Anna asked.

"Waffles? What waffles?" dad said.

Anna saw the note on the fridge and ran to get it. She gave it to dad and said: "Look, dad. Mom left a note. She said to make waffles for us. They are in the freezer."

Dad looked at the note and felt sorry. He had not been very thoughtful. He had not read the note. He had not made waffles for his twins.

"I'm sorry, Anna and Ben. I did not see the note. I did not make waffles for you. I made eggs and toast. Do you want some?" dad said.

Anna and Ben shook their heads. They did not want eggs and toast. They wanted waffles.

"Can you make waffles for us, dad? Please?" Ben said.

Dad smiled and nodded. He was glad that Anna had reminded him of the note. He was glad that Ben had asked nicely. He wanted to make his twins happy.

"Of course, I can make waffles for you. Let me get them from the freezer. You can help me put them in the toaster. How about that?" dad said.

Anna and Ben clapped their hands and cheered. They were happy and excited. They liked to help dad in the kitchen. They liked to eat waffles for breakfast. They loved their dad.

Lily and Ben were at the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, but their favorite was the hippo. The hippo was big and gray and had a huge mouth. He was playful and liked to splash in the water.

"Look, mom, the hippo is smiling!" Lily said.

"He is happy to see us," mom said. "But we have to be careful and not get too close. He might grab us with his teeth."

Lily and Ben nodded. They did not want to be grabbed by the hippo. They watched him from behind the fence and waved at him.

Suddenly, they saw a boy run past them. He was naughty and did not listen to his mom. He climbed over the fence and tried to touch the hippo.

"Stop, stop, you are in danger!" mom shouted.

But the boy did not stop. He reached out his hand and grabbed the hippo's ear. The hippo did not like that. He roared and shook his head. He threw the boy into the water.

"Help, help, the hippo grabbed me!" the boy cried.

Mom ran to the fence and called for help. A zookeeper came and rescued the boy. He was wet and scared and sorry.

"Never grab a hippo or any other animal," the zookeeper said. "They are wild and can hurt you. You have to respect them and keep a safe distance."

The boy nodded. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to the hippo and to his mom.

Lily and Ben watched the boy leave. They were glad they were not naughty. They thanked the hippo for being playful and not angry. They hugged their mom and went to see the other animals.

The end.

Moral value: Respect animals and follow the rules.

One day, she saw a monkey at the zoo. The monkey was brown and furry, and had a long tail. Lily thought the monkey was cute and funny. She wanted to talk to the monkey, but she did not know how. She asked her mom, "How can I talk to the monkey?"

Her mom said, "You can use sign language, like we do. Maybe the monkey will understand you." Lily nodded and smiled. She knew some sign language, because she used it to communicate with her family and friends. She decided to test her sign language with the monkey.

She walked closer to the cage, and waved at the monkey. The monkey looked at her and tilted his head. Lily signed, "Hello, monkey. My name is Lily. What is your name?" The monkey watched her hands, and then copied her signs. He signed, "Hello, Lily. My name is Max. I am deaf too."

Lily was surprised and happy. She found a friend who was like her. She signed, "You are deaf too? That is amazing. How do you learn new things?" Max signed, "I watch and copy. I learn from other monkeys and people. I like to learn new things too."

Lily and Max talked for a long time, using sign language. They shared their stories, their likes, and their dislikes. They made each other laugh and smile. They became good friends. Lily's mom and dad watched them and smiled too. They were proud of Lily for being brave and curious.

The moral of the story is: You can make friends with anyone, even if they are different from you. You can use sign language to communicate with deaf people and animals. You can learn new things by watching and copying. You can have fun and be happy with your friends.

One day, they found a door that they had never seen before. It was at the end of a long hall, and it had a sign that said "Do not enter". Tom and Lily were curious and brave, so they decided to open the door and see what was inside. They wondered if there was a secret treasure or a hidden garden or a magic mirror.

They pushed the door and it creaked open. They saw a dark and dusty room, full of boxes and cobwebs and old clothes. They walked in and looked around, hoping to find something interesting. But they only found more boxes and cobwebs and old clothes. They were disappointed and bored, and they wanted to leave.

But then they heard a noise. It was a soft and spooky noise, like a whisper or a sigh. They turned around and saw a white shape floating in the air. It had two eyes and a mouth and a nose, but no arms or legs or hair. It was a ghost!

Tom and Lily were scared and screamed. They ran to the door and tried to open it, but it was locked. They banged on the door and shouted for help, but no one heard them. They were trapped in the room with the ghost.

The ghost floated closer and closer to them. It looked sad and lonely, and it said in a low voice, "Hello. I'm sorry I scared you. I don't want to hurt you. I just want to talk to you. I've been alone in this room for a long time. Will you be my friends?"

Tom and Lily stopped screaming and looked at the ghost. They saw that it was not mean or evil, but friendly and gentle. They felt sorry for the ghost, and they wanted to help it. They said, "Hello. We're Tom and Lily. We're twins. We live in this house. We're sorry we opened your door. We were curious and brave. We'll be your friends. What's your name?"

The ghost smiled and said, "Thank you. You're very kind and brave. My name is Anna. I used to live in this house too, a long time ago. I was also a twin. But my twin brother died when we were young, and I was very sad. I stayed in this room with his things, and I never left. I became a ghost."

Tom and Lily felt sad for Anna, and they hugged her. They said, "We're sorry you lost your twin. We love each other very much. We can't imagine being without each other. We'll stay with you for a while, and we'll talk to you and play with you. Maybe we can make you happy."

Anna was very happy and hugged them back. She said, "Thank you. You're very sweet and nice. I'm glad you came to this room. You're the best friends I ever had. Maybe we can be like a family."

They stayed in the room for a while, and they talked and played and laughed. They forgot about the door and the sign and the dust. They only remembered the friendship and the fun and the love.

The moral of the story is: Be careful with electricity and listen to your parents and friends. They want to protect you and help you.

"Is it over?" Lily asked.

"Can we help them?" Tom asked.

"Of course, we can help them. We can share our water and food. We can give them some blankets and toys. We can be kind and friendly. We can be brave and strong," Dad said.

Ben was sad. He liked the sparks. He wanted to play with them. He looked at the jar. He saw a small hole on the lid. He had an idea.

"Maybe we can make more holes," he said. He took a stick and poked the lid. He made a big hole.

Lily gasped. "Ben, what are you doing? Stop!"

But it was too late. The sparks saw the hole. They flew out of the jar. They made a bright trail in the air. They were free.

Lily and Ben watched the sparks. They were happy for them. But they also missed them. They wished they could see them again.

"Maybe they will come back," Lily said. "Maybe they will glow for us again."

"Maybe," Ben said. He hoped so. He hugged the jar. He felt sorry for it. It was empty.

But one day, Mom says they have to go to school. Lily and Ben are scared. They do not want to leave Mom. They do not want to meet new people. They do not want to split.

Miss Lee is frustrated. She says, "Lily and Ben, I know you are twins. I know you love each other. But you have to sit apart. You have to make new friends. You have to learn to share and cooperate. You have to try new things. That is what school is for. Trust me, you will like it."

Lily and Ben are sad. They do not trust Miss Lee. They do not like school. They do not want to split. They cry and hug each other. They say, "We want to go home. We want to be with Mom. We do not want to split."

One day, the tutor is late. Lily waits and waits, but the tutor does not come. Lily is sad and bored. She looks out the window and sees a big truck. The truck has a loud horn. Lily thinks the horn is funny. She wants to hear it again.

Lily runs out of the house. She does not tell her mom. She does not look both ways. She runs to the truck and calls to the driver. "Hey, hey, honk your horn!" she shouts.

Lily picked up the pencil and the book. She felt the difference in her hands. She nodded. She understood.

"Can I weigh other things?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can. But be careful not to break anything," Mom said.

Lily ran to her room. She found a toy scale that she got for her birthday. She put the pencil on one side of the scale and a stuffed bear on the other side. The scale tipped to the bear's side.

"The bear weighs more than the pencil," Lily said to herself.

She tried other things. She weighed a ball, a flower, a cookie, and a necklace. She had fun comparing them.

Then she saw her cat sleeping on her bed. She wondered how much the cat weighed. She was very curious. She picked up the cat and put it on the scale. The cat did not like it. It meowed and scratched Lily's arm. It jumped off the scale and ran away.

Mom heard Lily and came to her room. She saw the scratch on Lily's arm and the scale on the floor.

"What happened, Lily?" Mom asked.

"I wanted to weigh the cat, but the cat was angry," Lily said.

Mom hugged Lily and cleaned her wound. She explained to Lily that the cat did not like to be weighed. She said that some things are better left alone.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was just curious," Lily said.

"I know, Lily. Curiosity is good, but you have to be gentle and respectful with living things. They have feelings too," Mom said.

Lily nodded. She learned something new. She said sorry to the cat and gave it a treat. She decided to weigh only things that did not mind. She still liked to be curious, but she also liked to be kind.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play outside. She had a yellow dress and a yellow hat that she wore every day. She thought yellow was the best color in the world.

One day, it started to rain. Lily did not like rain. She wanted to go outside and play, but her mom said no. She said rain was good for the plants and the animals, and that Lily should stay inside and read a book or draw a picture. Lily was mad. She did not want to read or draw. She wanted to play.

She looked out the window and saw a lady walking in the rain. The lady had a yellow coat and a yellow umbrella. She looked happy. She smiled and waved at Lily. Lily was curious. She wondered why the lady liked the rain. She decided to go outside and ask her.

She put on her yellow dress and her yellow hat and ran outside. She did not take a coat or an umbrella. She ran to the lady and said, "Hello, lady. Why do you like the rain?"

The lady smiled and said, "Hello, little girl. I like the rain because it makes everything fresh and clean. It also makes rainbows. Do you see the rainbow in the sky?"

Lily looked up and saw a beautiful rainbow. It had many colors, including yellow. She was amazed. She said, "Wow, the rainbow is so pretty. It has yellow, like my dress and hat and your coat and umbrella."

The lady nodded and said, "Yes, it does. Yellow is a lovely color, but so are the other colors. They make the rainbow more beautiful. Just like people, they are different and special in their own way. Do you understand?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I think I do. I like yellow, but I also like the other colors. They make the world more fun. Thank you, lady, for showing me the rainbow."

The lady hugged Lily and said, "You're welcome, little girl. You are very sweet and smart. But you should go back inside now. You are wet and cold. You don't want to get sick."

Lily realized she was shivering. She said, "Okay, lady. I will go back inside. Goodbye, lady. Have a nice day."

She ran back to her house and knocked on the door. Her mom opened it and said, "Lily, what are you doing? You are soaked. Come in, quick. You need to change and dry off."

Lily said, "Sorry, mom. I went outside to talk to a lady. She had a yellow coat and a yellow umbrella. She showed me the rainbow. It was so pretty. It had yellow and other colors. I learned that other colors are good too. I'm sorry I was mad at you. I love you, mom."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. I'm glad you learned something new. But next time, please listen to me and stay inside when it rains. Or at least take a coat and an umbrella. Okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will. Can I have some hot chocolate?"

Her mom said, "Of course, you can. Come on, let's go to the kitchen."

They went to the kitchen and had some hot chocolate. Lily felt warm and happy. She looked out the window and saw the lady walking away. She waved at her and said, "Thank you, lady. You are very nice."

The lady waved back and said, "You're welcome, little girl. You are very brave."

The end.

Tim and Mia are friends who like to draw pictures. They have a big folder where they keep their drawings. One day, they want to show their pictures to their teacher, but they have a problem. The folder is too heavy and difficult to carry.

"Can you help me, Tim?" Mia asks. "The folder is too heavy for me."

"Sure, Mia. I can help you," Tim says. He takes one side of the folder and Mia takes the other. They walk slowly to the teacher's desk.

But on the way, they see a butterfly. It is very pretty and colorful. Tim loves butterflies. He wants to catch it and look at it.

"Look, Mia! A butterfly!" Tim says. He lets go of the folder and runs after the butterfly.

"Tim, wait! Don't release the folder!" Mia says. But it is too late. The folder falls to the floor and all the pictures come out. They get mixed up and dirty.

Mia is very sad and angry. She worked hard on her pictures and now they are ruined. She cries and picks up the folder.

"Tim, you are a bad friend!" Mia says. "You did not help me. You only cared about the butterfly. You made a big mess."

Tim comes back with the butterfly in his hand. He sees Mia crying and the pictures on the floor. He feels sorry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, Mia. I was wrong. I should have helped you. I should not have released the folder. The butterfly is not important. You are my friend and your pictures are important. Can you forgive me?" Tim says.

Mia looks at Tim and the butterfly. She sees that Tim is sorry and that he still likes her. She decides to forgive him.

"It's okay, Tim. I forgive you. You are my friend and I still like you. But next time, please don't release the folder. Let's fix the pictures and show them to the teacher together," Mia says.

Tim and Mia hug and smile. They put the pictures back in the folder and carry it to the teacher. The teacher is proud of them and their pictures. They learn that they should help each other and not be distracted by things that are not important. They also learn that they should say sorry and forgive when they make a mistake. They are happy and good friends.

Sam and Ben were brothers. They liked to play with cars and trucks. One day, they saw a big black car parked outside their house. It had shiny wheels and a loud horn.

"Wow, look at that car!" Sam said. "I want to have a car like that when I grow up."

"Me too," Ben said. "But we need a lot of money to buy a car like that. How can we get money?"

Sam thought for a while. Then he had an idea. He saw a can of paint and a brush in the garage. He smiled and said, "I know! We can paint the car and make it look nicer. Then the owner will give us money for our work. Come on, let's go!"

Ben was not sure. He said, "But that is not our car. Maybe the owner will be angry if we paint it. Maybe we should ask first."

Sam shook his head. He said, "No, no, no. Trust me, the owner will be happy. He will see how good we are at painting. He will encourage us and thank us. Come on, don't be scared. It will be fun!"

Sam took the can of paint and the brush and ran to the car. Ben followed him. They started to paint the car with different colors. They painted stripes and dots and stars and hearts. They painted the windows and the wheels and the horn. They painted until the car was covered with paint.

They stepped back and looked at their work. They smiled and said, "Wow, we did a great job! The car looks so pretty now. The owner will love it. He will give us a lot of money for sure."

They waited for the owner to come out. They were excited and proud. They did not see the man who was watching them from the window. He was the owner of the car. He was very angry. He saw his black car turned into a mess of colors. He saw his paint and his brush in the hands of the boys. He yelled and ran out of the house. He grabbed the boys by their collars and said, "What have you done to my car? How dare you paint my car without my permission? You have ruined my car! You have to pay for this! You have to pay a lot of money!"

Sam and Ben were scared. They cried and said, "We are sorry, we are sorry. We wanted to make your car look nicer. We wanted to get money for our work. We thought you would encourage us and thank us."

The man did not listen. He did not encourage them or thank them. He dragged them to their house and knocked on the door. He told their parents what they had done. Their parents were shocked and angry. They apologized to the man and said they would pay for the damage. They scolded Sam and Ben and said they were very naughty and foolish. They said they had to go to their room and stay there for a long time. They said they had to give up their cars and trucks and toys as punishment. They said they had to learn to respect other people's things and ask before they touch.

Sam and Ben were very sad. They went to their room and cried. They wished they had not painted the car. They wished they had listened to Ben. They wished they had used simple words and asked first. They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that painting a car without permission is not a good way to get money or encouragement. It is a good way to get in trouble and lose everything.

Lily was a little girl who liked to explore. She liked to find new things and learn about them. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a big stone with strange marks on it. She ran to the stone and touched it.

"What is this, mom?" she asked.

"That is an ancient stone, Lily. It is very old and has writing on it. People long ago made it to tell stories or remember things," her mom said.

Lily looked at the writing and tried to read it. She saw shapes and lines and dots. She wondered what they meant.

"Can you read it, mom?" she asked.

"No, Lily. I don't know this writing. It is from a different language and time. Maybe someone who studies ancient things can read it," her mom said.

Lily wanted to learn more. She wanted to know the stories and things that the stone said. She looked around and saw a man with a big camera and a notebook. He was taking pictures and writing notes. He looked like he knew about ancient things.

"Mom, can we ask him?" Lily said.

"Sure, Lily. But be polite and don't bother him too much. He might be busy," her mom said.

They walked to the man and said hello. The man smiled and said hello back.

"Excuse me, sir. My daughter Lily is curious about this ancient stone. Do you know what it says?" Lily's mom asked.

The man looked at Lily and saw her bright eyes and eager face. He liked children who were curious and wanted to learn.

"Well, hello, Lily. I am a professor and I study ancient things. This stone is very special. It is from a very old civilization that lived here long before us. They had their own language and culture and history. This stone is part of a big story that they wrote. Do you want to hear some of it?" the man asked.

Lily nodded and said yes. She wanted to hear the story. She wanted to know what the ancient people said.

The man told Lily and her mom a story about a brave hero, a wise king, a fierce dragon, and a hidden treasure. He showed them how the writing matched the words and how the stone was part of a bigger picture. He made the story come alive with his voice and gestures.

Lily listened and watched with wonder. She felt like she was in the story. She imagined the hero, the king, the dragon, and the treasure. She asked questions and learned new things.

She thanked the man for telling her the story. She said it was amazing and exciting. She said she wanted to know more about ancient things.

The man smiled and said he was happy to share his knowledge. He said he hoped Lily would keep exploring and learning. He said she had a great mind and a big heart.

Lily hugged the man and said he was very nice and smart. She said he was her new friend. She said she loved ancient things.

She ran back to the stone and touched it again. She felt a connection to the people who made it. She felt a spark of curiosity and wonder. She felt a love of stories and learning.

She looked at her mom and said, "Mom, this is the best day ever. Can we come back to the park and see the ancient stone again?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. We can come back anytime you want. I'm glad you had fun and learned something new. I'm proud of you, Lily. You are a wonderful girl."

They hugged and said they loved each other. They walked away from the stone, holding hands. They had a new appreciation for ancient things and a new friend to share them with. They had a great day at the park.

Tom was a bald man who liked to listen to his radio. He liked to hear songs and stories and jokes on his radio. He had a big radio in his living room and a small radio in his bedroom.

One day, Tom's niece Lily came to visit him. Lily was a little girl who liked to play with toys and draw pictures. She saw Tom's big radio and wanted to touch it. She asked Tom, "Can I play with your radio, uncle?"

Tom said, "No, Lily, you can't play with my radio. It is not a toy. It is a machine that makes sounds. If you play with it, you might break it or hurt yourself."

Lily was sad and angry. She thought Tom was mean and stingy. She waited until Tom went to the kitchen to make some tea. Then she sneaked to the living room and grabbed the big radio. She tried to turn it on, but she did not know how. She pushed and pulled and twisted the buttons and knobs. She heard a loud noise and saw sparks and smoke. She dropped the radio and ran away.

Tom heard the noise and came back to the living room. He saw his big radio broken and burned. He was very upset and angry. He shouted, "Lily, what did you do? You ruined my radio! Why didn't you listen to me?"

Lily was scared and sorry. She cried and said, "I'm sorry, uncle. I just wanted to play with your radio. I didn't mean to break it."

Tom calmed down and hugged Lily. He said, "I know, Lily, but you should have obeyed me. I was trying to prevent you from making a mistake. My radio was very important to me. It was a gift from your grandma. She gave it to me before she died. She loved to listen to the radio with me. Now I can't hear her voice anymore."

Lily felt very bad. She said, "I'm sorry, uncle. I didn't know that. I love grandma too. Can we fix your radio?"

Tom said, "I don't know, Lily. Maybe we can, maybe we can't. But we can still listen to my small radio in my bedroom. And we can still talk to each other and remember grandma. She would want us to be happy and kind."

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Okay, uncle. I will be happy and kind. And I will listen to you next time. I love you, uncle."

Tom said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go to my bedroom and listen to some songs and stories and jokes."

They went to Tom's bedroom and turned on his small radio. They heard some songs and stories and jokes. They laughed and sang and hugged. They felt closer and happier.

The moral of the story is: We should respect other people's belongings and listen to their advice. They might be trying to prevent us from making mistakes or getting hurt. We should also appreciate the gifts and memories we have from our loved ones. They can make us feel less lonely and more joyful.

But then, she hears her mom's voice. "Sara, what are you doing?" Mom asks. She sounds angry.

Sara turns around and sees her mom. Mom looks at the shampoo bottle and the sink. She sees the water and the bubbles. She sees Sara's wet hair.

"Sara, this is not your shampoo. This is my shampoo. It is for grown-ups. It is not good for your hair. You need to use your shampoo. It is for kids. It is gentle and safe. Do you understand?" Mom says.

Sara feels sorry. She did not know. She wanted to have shiny hair like mom. She says, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to use your shampoo. I wanted to have shiny hair. Can I use your shampoo?"

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, Sara. You cannot use my shampoo. It is not for you. It can hurt your eyes and your scalp. You need to use your shampoo. It is for you. Mom hugs Sara. She says, "You're welcome, Sara. You're my sweet girl."

Mom smiled and hugged them. "That's wonderful, my loves. You have such good imaginations. I am proud of you."

She looked at the curtain and saw that it was a bit torn and dirty. She did not get angry, but she said, "Can I ask you a favor? Can you help me wash the curtain and fix it? It will be more fun to play with it when it is clean and whole."

Lily and Max nodded. They liked to help Mom. They took the curtain and followed her to the laundry room. Mom showed them how to put the curtain in the washing machine and how to sew the tear. She encouraged them to try and praised them when they did well.

"Thank you, Lily and Max. You are very helpful and kind. The curtain looks much better now. Do you want to hang it back in your room?"

"Yes, please!" Lily and Max said. They ran back to their room and helped Mom hang the curtain. It was smooth and blue again, and it sparkled in the sun.

"Can we play with it again, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Of course, my princess. You can play with it as much as you want. Just be careful not to rip it again, okay?"

"Okay, Mom. We will be careful. We love you, Mom!" Lily and Max said.

"I love you too, my little royals. Have fun!" Mom said, kissing them and leaving them to play.

"Let's enter the loop!" said Lila. "It looks like fun!"

"OK!" said Ben. "But be careful. It is very high."

They ran to the loop and climbed on it. Lila went first. She was brave and strong. She held on to the metal and swung her legs. She made a graceful circle in the air. She smiled and laughed.

"Wow! You are good!" said Ben. "Can I try?"

"Sure!" said Lila. "But be careful. It is very fast."

Ben went next. He was excited and eager. He held on to the metal and pushed his feet. He made a big circle in the air. He shouted and cheered.

"Yay! This is fun!" said Ben. "Can I do it again?"

But then he heard a loud noise. It was a dog. It was big and black. It was barking and running. It was coming to the loop.

"Look out!" said Lila. "There is a dog!"

Ben saw the dog. He was scared and surprised. He let go of the metal and fell. He landed on the grass. He hurt his knee. He cried and whimpered.

"Are you OK?" said Lila. She ran to Ben and hugged him. "Don't worry. I am here."

The dog came to the loop. It sniffed and licked. It was friendly and curious. It wagged its tail and barked.

"Hello!" said the dog. "Do you want to play?"

"But I want to go fast!" Sam said. He liked to speed down the slide and feel the wind in his hair.

"Me too!" Lily said. She was Sam's little sister. She wanted to do everything Sam did.

"Maybe we can find something else to do," Mom said. She looked around the park. She saw a big hill covered with snow. "How about we make a snowman?"

Sam and Lily nodded. They liked to make snowmen. They followed Mom to the hill. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot, a hat, and some buttons to make the snowman's face and clothes.

"Look, Mom! We made a snowman!" Sam said.

"He's very nice," Mom said. "But he looks a bit cold. Maybe he needs a scarf."

"I have a scarf!" Lily said. She took off her pink scarf and wrapped it around the snowman's neck.

"There, now he's warm," Lily said.

They smiled at their snowman. They had fun in the park, even if they couldn't go on the slide. They forgot about the icy slide and enjoyed the snow.

Tom's friend, Sam, said, "No, Tom. You are dizzy. You should not sail today." But Tom did not listen. He wanted to sail. So, Tom went on his boat. He did not allow Sam to help him.

The boat went fast. Tom was still dizzy. He could not see well. Then, the boat hit a big rock. The boat broke. Tom was sad.

The moral of the story is to listen to your friends and not to do things when you are not feeling well.

Once upon a time, there was a funny elephant named Ella. Ella had a big trunk. She loved to play with her friends.

One day, Ella saw a little bird named Bobby. Bobby was sad. Ella asked, "Why are you sad, Bobby?" Bobby said, "I want to play, but I can't fly high like my friends."

Ella had an idea. She said, "Bobby, you can play with me! My trunk can help you fly high." Bobby was happy. He sat on Ella's trunk, and she lifted him up high.

Bobby and Ella played all day. They laughed and had fun. Bobby was not sad anymore. Ella was happy too, because she had a new friend to play with. And they lived happily ever after.

Tim was sad, but he wanted to find a way to eat the lollipop. He tried to be sneaky and eat it when his mom was not looking. But his mom was very smart. She always knew when Tim was trying to eat the old lollipop. She would stop him and say, "No, Tim! I told you not to eat that."

One day, Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. Tim showed Sam the old lollipop and told him about his mom preventing him from eating it. Sam had an idea. He said, "Let's trade! I have a new lollipop at home. I will give it to you, and you can give me the old one."

Tim liked the idea. He and Sam traded lollipops. Tim's mom saw the new lollipop and said, "Yes, you can eat that one." Tim was so happy. He finally got to eat a lollipop, and he did not have to eat the old one that could make him sick.

So they both went to the park together and Ben's brother allowed him to splash and jump in the puddles, but he told Ben to stay close by him.

Ben was having so much fun and didn't realise that he had run away from his brother. He was so excited about the new view he was getting, that he kept running away further and further.

When his brother caught up with him, he was very angry and told Ben he should not wander off like that. He explained to him that it's not safe for children to wander off, and if he wanted to go exploring again, he had to stay close by so that his brother could keep an eye on him.

The moral of the story is that it's always important to stay close to the people in charge, even if itâ€™s fun to explore on your own.

One day, a little boy named Jake was exploring his backyard and he came across a patch of clay. He decided to play with it and try to make something.

Jake's mum saw him outside playing and said, "Jake, why don't you try to make something with the clay? It looks like fun!" 

So, Jake began to play with the clay. He tried to make a clay snake but it was a bit hard. He was about to give up when his mum came back and said, "Hey Jake, why don't you try mixing the clay with some water? It would make it easier to shape."

Jake was so excited to try it. He added some water to the clay and soon it was much easier to shape. He had so much fun making different creatures and shapes with the clay. When he was finished, he was so happy with his work that he wanted to keep it forever. 

So Jake's mum said, "That's great Jake! But we need to clean up the clay now. It looks like it's making a bit of a mess in the backyard." 

Jake was a bit sad but he understood. He got a cloth and started to wipe up the clay. After a few minutes, the backyard was clean again. 

Jake was glad that he could have fun with the clay but also clean it up afterwards.

Once upon a time there was a wall that was very tall. Every day it would stand there, blocking the path between two cities. The people in each city tried to find different ways to get across the wall, but none of them worked. 

One day, two young children played together. They were from cities on either side of the wall. The two children wanted to be friends, but the wall made that difficult. 

So, the two children decided to do something about it. With hard work, they united their two cities. The children stood near the wall, holding hands. They began to run. 

The children ran quickly and soon they reached the top of the wall. Suddenly, the wall disappeared and the two cities could see each other. Everyone was very happy that their cities could unite. From that day onwards, the two cities always stayed together.

Candy town was a fun place to live. Everyone in the town always behaved in the best manner and always looked fashionable. But then something strange happened - the town became dull and grey.

One day, two little girls were walking to school and noticed just how dull the town had become.

"Why is everything so dull?" asked Kay.

"I don't know" replied her friend, Louise.

Just then, they noticed an old lady walking towards them.

"Good morning!" said the old lady with a friendly smile.

Kay and Louise smiled back politely.

"I know why the town has become so dull lately. You see, everyone in Candy Town has stopped behaving in the right way. We have to start behaving better if we want to make the town look colourful again."

Kay and Louise nodded in agreement.

"That's a great idea," said Kay.

From that moment onwards, everyone in the town started behaving better and looking fashionable. Sure enough, Candy Town changed from a dull place to one that was colourful and happy.

Lily said, "Don't worry, we'll help you find it." They searched all over the park and finally found the toy under a bush. The boy was so happy and said, "Thank you so much for helping me. You are very kind."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "Lily, you did a good thing by helping someone in need. It's important to always yield and help others when we can." Lily nodded and said, "Yes, helping others is important." They all walked home together, happy and proud of their good deed.

"I glow to light up the night," replied the firefly. "Why are you so high up in the tree?"

"I like to be up high where I can see everything," said the raven. "But sometimes it's nice to come down and explore."

The firefly and the raven became friends and spent the night talking about all the things they loved. As the sun rose, the raven flew back up to its high tree, while the firefly continued to glow in the morning light.

Sam was a tall boy, and he could reach the tree. "Sure, Tim! I will help you," Sam said. Sam lifted Tim up, and Tim grabbed the cat. They saved the cat, and it was happy. The cat danced with Tim and Sam to the rhythm of their laughter. From that day on, they all became good friends and had many silly adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a big crane. The crane liked to pick up things and move them. It was very good at its job. One day, the crane saw a little boy crying. The boy had a spoiled toy. The toy was broken and the boy was very sad.

The crane wanted to help the boy. It tried to fix the toy, but it was not easy. The crane tried and tried, but the toy was still broken. Then, the crane had an idea. It went to find a new toy for the boy.

The crane found a new toy and gave it to the boy. The boy was very happy. He played with the new toy and stopped crying. The crane realized it could not fix the spoiled toy, but it could still make the boy happy. The boy and the crane became good friends, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a kind bunny named Bobo. Bobo had many friends, and they all played together. One day, while they were playing, they found a big apple tree. They were so happy because they loved apples.

But, a mean snake lived near the apple tree. The snake said, "These apples have poison. If you eat them, you will feel sick." Bobo and his friends were sad and scared. They didn't want to feel sick, but they really wanted to eat the apples.

Bobo thought and thought. He wanted to solve the problem. Then, he had a good idea. He said to his friends, "Let's ask the wise owl for help. He will know what to do." So, they went to the wise owl and told him about the poison apples.

The wise owl listened and said, "The snake is not telling the truth. He just wants the apples for himself. Go and enjoy the apples, my friends." Bobo and his friends went back to the apple tree and ate the apples. They were not sick, and they were very happy. They thanked the wise owl for helping them solve the problem.

At the park, they saw a big, tall tree. One friend said, "Let's climb the tree!" They all agreed and started to climb. The first friend climbed up and waved to the others. "Look how high I am!" he shouted. The others laughed and waved back.

But as they climbed higher, the tree started to shake. The friends did not notice, and they kept climbing. Suddenly, the tree broke, and they all fell down. They were sad and hurt. The day was not fun anymore.

As they walked, they saw a big fence that was separate from the other fences. Behind the fence, Spot saw his family! He barked and ran to them. Spot's mom said, "Thank you, Lucy, for helping my little puppy." Lucy smiled and waved goodbye as Spot and his family played together happily.

The next day, the fridge was happy. The apple and the cheese were separate. The apple was on one side, and the cheese was on the other side. They did not talk anymore. The other foods in the fridge were happy too.

Now, the fridge was not terrible anymore. It was a good fridge. The foods were separate and happy. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to help his mom in the kitchen. One day, Tim's mom was making soup in a big pot. The pot was hot and steamy. Tim wanted to help, so he tried to reach for the pot.

"Wait, Tim!" his mom said. "It is not safe to reach for the pot. It is hot and you could get hurt."

Tim felt sad, but he listened to his mom. He wanted to be safe. So, Tim asked his mom, "What can I do to help?"

His mom smiled and said, "You can help by getting the bowls and spoons for the soup."

Tim felt happy and proud. He got the bowls and spoons, and they had a nice meal together. The soup was yummy.

The moral of the story is to listen to your parents and always be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bun Bun. Bun Bun was very weak and tired. He wanted to lay down and rest.

Bun Bun's friend, a little bird named Tweet, came to visit him. "Hi Bun Bun, how are you feeling today?" asked Tweet.

"I'm feeling very weak and tired," replied Bun Bun. "I just want to lay down and rest."

Tweet had an idea. "I know a way to make you feel better. Let's trade some carrots for some bird seeds. Carrots will make you strong and healthy."

Bun Bun smiled and agreed to the trade. He ate the carrots and soon felt much better. "Thank you, Tweet! You're a good friend," said Bun Bun.

The two friends sat together and enjoyed the sunshine. Bun Bun felt happy and grateful for his friend's help.

Lily liked to lift things. She lifted her toys, her books, her cat. She lifted everything she could find. But she had to be careful. Some things were fragile. Fragile means they can break easily.

One Tuesday, Lily saw a big box in the living room. It had a bow on it. It was a gift for her birthday. Lily wanted to lift the box. She wanted to see what was inside. She grabbed the box and tried to lift it. But it was too heavy. She could not lift it. She pulled and pushed and tugged. But the box did not move.

Then she heard a crack. The box was fragile. It broke open. Lily saw a beautiful doll inside. It had a pink dress and a blue hat. It had long hair and a smile. Lily loved the doll. She wanted to play with it. But the doll was fragile too. It had a crack on its face. Lily had broken the doll.

Lily felt sad. She had ruined her birthday gift. She started to cry. She did not mean to break the doll. She just wanted to lift the box.

Her mom heard her cry. She came to the living room. She saw the broken box and the broken doll. She saw Lily's tears. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie. I know you did not mean to break the doll. You were just curious. But you have to be gentle with fragile things. They can break easily. I can fix the doll for you. Don't worry. I love you."

Lily felt better. She said sorry to her mom and to the doll. She learned to be careful with fragile things. She still liked to lift things. But she lifted them gently. She played with her doll every day. She gave it a name. She called it Tuesday.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to swim. They had a big pool in their backyard where they played every day. They also liked to race each other in the water. They were very competitive and always wanted to win.

One day, they decided to have a swim contest. They asked their mom to be the judge. She said yes and gave them each a towel. She told them to get ready and wait for her signal. Lily and Ben ran to the pool and jumped in. They swam to the other side and waited.

Mom counted to three and said, "Go!" Lily and Ben kicked and splashed as fast as they could. They both wanted to reach the other side first. They were very close to each other. They could see their mom cheering for them.

But then, something happened. Lily felt something pull her leg. She looked down and saw a big fish. It was orange and white and had a long tail. It was their pet fish, Nemo. He had escaped from his tank in the drawer and followed them to the pool. He wanted to play with them.

Lily was surprised and scared. She stopped swimming and screamed. Ben heard her and turned around. He saw Nemo and laughed. He thought it was funny. He kept swimming and reached the other side. He shouted, "I win! I win!"

Mom ran to Lily and helped her out of the water. She hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. It's just Nemo. He won't hurt you. He's your friend." She took Nemo in her hand and put him back in his tank. She said, "Sorry, Nemo. You can't swim with Lily and Ben. You have to stay in your drawer."

Lily was still shaking. She said, "Mom, I don't like Nemo. He scared me. He made me lose." She looked at Ben and said, "You cheated. You had help from Nemo. You didn't win fair."

Ben said, "No, I didn't cheat. I didn't know Nemo was there. I swam faster than you. I won fair." He smiled and said, "I'm the best swimmer. You're the worst swimmer."

Lily and Ben started to argue. They both said mean things to each other. They made each other cry. Mom said, "Stop it, Lily and Ben. You're being rude and unkind. You're not good swimmers. You're bad swimmers. You need to learn how to share and be nice. You need to say sorry to each other and to Nemo."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they said. They said sorry to each other and to Nemo. They hugged and said, "We love you." They said sorry to mom and said, "We love you too." Mom said, "I love you too. Now, let's dry off and have some snacks. And maybe later, we can swim again. But this time, no racing. Just having fun." Lily and Ben agreed. They said, "Okay, mom. That sounds good." They smiled and followed mom to the house. They left the pool and Nemo behind. They were happy again.

"Hello, my dear children," she says. "How are you today? Are you hungry? Do you want some tea and cookies?"

The dolls do not answer, but Anna nods for them. She picks up one doll and makes her voice high and sweet.

"Yes, mommy, I am hungry. Thank you for the tea and cookies. They look yummy."

She puts the doll back on the chair and picks up another one. She makes his voice low and grumpy.

"No, mommy, I am not hungry. I don't like tea and cookies. I want juice and candy."

She puts the doll back on the chair and shakes her head.

"No, no, no," she says. "You cannot have juice and candy. They are bad for your teeth and your tummy. You have to drink tea and milk. They are good for you. They make you grow big and strong."

She picks up the teapot and pours some water in the doll's cup. She adds some milk and stirs it with a spoon.

"Here, drink this. It is delicious. You will like it."

She holds the cup to the doll's mouth and makes a slurping sound.

"Mmm, you are right, mommy. It is delicious. I like it."

She nods and smiles.

"See, I told you. Now, do you want a cookie?"

She holds a cookie to the doll's mouth and makes a crunching sound.

"Mmm, yes, I want a cookie. Thank you, mommy. You are the best."

She nods and hugs the doll.

"You are welcome, my dear. You are the best, too."

She looks at the other dolls and says.

"Now, who else wants some tea and cookies?"

Mom says, "Do not be sad. We can play a game inside. It is fun and different. You can win a prize." Ben and Mia are curious. They want to play the game. They follow Mom to the living room.

Mom has a big box. She says, "This is the game. It is called Memory. You have to find two cards that are the same. If you find them, you keep them. The one who has the most cards at the end wins the prize." Ben and Mia are excited. They want to win the prize.

Mom opens the box and shows them the cards. The cards have pictures of animals, fruits, colors and shapes. Mom shuffles the cards and puts them face down on the floor. She says, "You take turns to flip two cards. If they are the same, you say 'Match!' and keep them. If they are different, you say 'No match!' and turn them back. Remember where the cards are. Ready? Let's play!"

Ben and Mia start to play. They flip the cards and look at the pictures. Sometimes they find a match, sometimes they do not. They say 'Match!' and 'No match!' and laugh. They try to remember where the cards are. They have fun.

The rain stops. The sun comes out. Ben and Mia do not notice. They are busy playing the game. They want to win the prize. They do not care about the rain. They like the game. It is fun and different.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the yard with their toy cars. They pretend to be hunters and chase animals with their cars. Tim has a red car and Sam has a blue car.

One day, they see a big rabbit in the grass. They want to catch it with their cars. Tim says, "Look, Sam, a rabbit! Let's go get it!" Sam says, "OK, Tim, let's go!" They drive their cars towards the rabbit.

But the rabbit is fast and smart. It runs away from the cars. It jumps over a rock and hides behind a bush. Tim and Sam cannot see it. They are confused. They say, "Where did it go? Where is the rabbit?"

The rabbit is clever. It waits for the right moment. When Tim and Sam are close to the bush, it jumps out and runs behind them. It runs towards their cars. It pushes Tim's car with its nose. Tim's car flips over and stops. Tim says, "Oh no, my car!"

The rabbit does the same to Sam's car. It pushes Sam's car with its nose. Sam's car flips over and stops. Sam says, "Oh no, my car too!"

The rabbit is happy. It hops away from the cars. It says, "Ha ha, I tricked you! I am the hunter and you are the animals!"

Tim and Sam are sad. They look at their cars. They are upside down and cannot move. They say, "How did the rabbit do that? That was impressive!"

They try to fix their cars. They turn them over and reverse them. They say, "Let's try again. Maybe we can catch the rabbit next time!" They drive their cars around the yard. They look for the rabbit. But the rabbit is gone. It is hiding in another place. It is laughing. It says, "You cannot catch me! I am the best hunter!"

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park. They have a ball, a kite and a bike. They share their toys and have fun.

One day, they see a big bird in the sky. It is black and white and has a long, sharp beak. It is a crow. The crow flies over the park and looks for food.

"Look, Sam, a crow!" Tom says. "It is very big and sharp. Do you think it is hungry?"

"Maybe, Tom," Sam says. "But we have no food for it. Let's play with our kite. It is red and blue and flies high."

They run to their kite and hold the string. They make the kite go up and down and left and right. The crow sees the kite and thinks it is a bird too. It wants to catch it and eat it.

The crow flies fast and dives at the kite. It opens its beak and tries to bite the kite. But the kite is not a bird. It is made of paper and sticks. The crow's beak tears the paper and breaks the sticks. The kite falls to the ground.

"Oh no, our kite!" Tom says. "The crow broke it. It is very bad and mean."

"I know, Tom," Sam says. "But we still have our ball and our bike. Let's play with them. The crow can't break them."

They leave the kite and go to their ball and their bike. They kick the ball and ride the bike. They have fun again.

The crow sees them and feels sorry. It did not mean to break their kite. It was just hungry and confused. It flies to the west and looks for other food.

Tom and Sam see the crow fly away. They wave at it and say:

"Bye, crow. We are not mad at you. But please don't break our toys again. They are ours and we like them."

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play near the river. One day, they saw a kayak on the shore. It was red and shiny and had two paddles.

"Let's try it!" Tom said. "It looks fun!"

"But we don't know how to use it," Lily said. "We should study first. Maybe we can ask Dad or Mom to teach us."

"Study? That's stupid!" Tom said. "We can learn by ourselves. Come on, don't be scared!"

Tom dragged Lily to the kayak and pushed it into the water. He climbed in and told Lily to sit behind him. He grabbed a paddle and started to move.

"See? It's easy!" Tom said. "Just follow me!"

Lily was not happy. She felt the kayak wobble and shake. She saw the water splash and swirl. She heard the river roar and rush.

"Tom, I don't like this!" Lily said. "It's too fast and too hard! Let's go back!"

"Stop being a baby!" Tom said. "It's fun! Look, there's a big wave ahead! Let's ride it!"

Tom paddled harder and steered the kayak towards the wave. Lily screamed and held on tight. The wave was huge and angry. It lifted the kayak high and then threw it down. The kayak flipped over and sank. Tom and Lily fell into the water. They were cold and wet and scared. They tried to swim, but the current was too strong. They cried for help, but no one heard them. They disappeared under the water. They never came back.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. Sara found a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and fuzzy. She was very happy.

"Look, Ben, I found a caterpillar!" she said, holding the leaf in her hand.

"Wow, it's so cute!" Ben said, leaning closer. "Can I hold it too?"

Sara nodded and gave him the leaf. Ben gently touched the caterpillar. It tickled his finger. He smiled.

"Can we keep it as a pet?" he asked.

Sara thought for a moment. She liked the caterpillar, but she also wanted to share it with Ben. She said, "OK, but we have to take good care of it. It needs food and water and a home."

They decided to make a home for the caterpillar in a shoebox. They put some grass and leaves and a bottle cap of water in the box. They made a hole in the lid so the caterpillar could breathe. They named the caterpillar Lily.

They took turns holding and watching Lily. They were very happy.

But one day, when they opened the box, they saw that Lily was gone. They only saw a hard shell hanging from a leaf. They were very sad.

"Where did Lily go?" Sara asked, tears in her eyes.

"I don't know," Ben said, sniffing. "Maybe she ran away."

They looked everywhere for Lily, but they could not find her. They felt like they had lost their friend.

They did not know that Lily had changed into a butterfly. She had broken out of the shell and flown away. She was now free and beautiful. She saw Sara and Ben looking for her. She felt sorry for them, but she also felt happy for herself. She was envious of no one. She flew over their heads and said, "Goodbye, Sara and Ben. Thank you for taking care of me. I will always remember you." But they did not hear her. They only saw a flash of color in the sky. They wondered if it was Lily. They hoped she was happy too.

One day, she saw a new gorilla in the zoo. It was white, not black like the others. Lily was curious and wanted to know more. She asked her mom, "Mom, why is that gorilla white?"

Her mom explained, "That gorilla is called Snowy. He is very rare and special. He has a condition that makes his fur white, but he is still a gorilla like the others. He came from another zoo, where he had no friends. He was lonely and sad."

Lily felt sorry for Snowy. She wanted him to be happy and have friends. She said, "Mom, can we go closer and say hello to Snowy?"

Her mom nodded and took her hand. They walked to the fence where Snowy was sitting. Lily waved and smiled at him. She said, "Hi, Snowy! I'm Lily. You are very beautiful and special. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

Snowy looked at Lily and saw her kind eyes and friendly smile. He felt something warm in his chest. He had never met a human like her before. He decided to give her a chance. He nodded and grunted softly. He reached out his hand and touched Lily's hand gently. He said, "Hi, Lily. I'm Snowy. You are very nice and brave. I like you too. Yes, I want to be your friend."

Lily and Snowy smiled at each other. They had made a new friend. They accepted each other for who they were. They were happy.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big red tomato on a vine. They both wanted to eat it, but they did not want to share.

"I saw it first!" Tom said.

"No, I did!" Sam said.

They pulled and tugged on the tomato, but it did not come off. They pulled harder and harder, until the tomato burst and the juice and seeds spread all over them and the ground.

"Yuck!" Tom said.

"Ew!" Sam said.

They looked at each other and felt silly. They had wasted a good tomato and made a mess. They wished they had been nice and split the tomato in half.

They heard a voice behind them. It was their grandpa, who had an ancient hat and a kind smile.

"What are you two doing?" he asked.

"We were fighting over a tomato, grandpa," Tom said.

"And we broke it," Sam said.

Grandpa nodded and said, "That's a shame. You know, tomatoes are like friends. They are better when you share them and enjoy them together. If you fight over them, you lose them and make a mess. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sam nodded and said, "We're sorry, grandpa. We learned our lesson. Can we help you clean up?"

Grandpa smiled and said, "Of course. And maybe later, we can make some tomato soup and share it with the whole family. How does that sound?"

Tom and Sam smiled and said, "That sounds great, grandpa. We love you and we love tomatoes."

Lila and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find worms and stones. They had a bucket and a shovel each. They made a big pile of dirt.

"Look, a raven!" Tom said, pointing at the black bird on the fence. "It has shiny feathers and a sharp beak."

"No, don't do that!" Tom said, stopping her. "That's mean. The raven is alive. It will be scared and hurt."

"But I want to bury it!" Lila said, pouting. "It's just a bird. It's not our friend."

"Yes, it is!" Tom said. "It's a living thing. It has feelings. It likes to fly and sing and eat. We should be nice to it."

"Maybe you're right," she said. "Maybe it is our friend. Maybe it wants to play with us."

"Then let's make it a nest!" Tom said, smiling. "We can use some of the dirt and some grass and leaves. We can make it cozy and tidy."

Lily followed him. She was worried about her brother. She knew Mom was right. She wore her socks even though they were a little rough.

At the park, Lily and Tom had fun. They slid on the slide, swung on the swings, and climbed on the monkey bars. But then Tom stepped on a sharp rock. He cried out in pain. His foot was bleeding.

Mom came to help him. She cleaned his wound and put a band-aid on it. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. You should have listened to me. Socks are not just for warmth. They are for safety too. Next time, please wear them."

Tom felt sorry too. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. You were right. Socks are good. I will wear them next time. And I will listen to you more."

Lily smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. I'm glad you learned your lesson. I love you, brother."

Tom smiled back and said, "I love you too, sister."

Mom kissed them both and said, "I love you both. Now let's go home and have some ice cream."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of listening to parents, wearing appropriate clothes, and caring for siblings.

Stitch smiled and said goodbye to Victoria as she swam away, happy and excited to show off her new crystal.
