Spot ran faster and faster. He passed all the other dogs and crossed the finish line first. Spot won the race! His friends were so happy and proud of him. They all said, "Good job, Spot!"

After the race, Spot and his friends went to a special dog party. There were lots of treats for the dogs to taste. Spot tasted a big bone and it was very yummy. He shared the bone with his friends and they all had a great time. Spot was happy he won the race and made his friends proud.

Once upon a time, there was a big, powerful sunflower. It lived in a small garden with many other flowers. The sunflower was very tall and strong. It loved to dance in the sun and play with its friends.

One day, a little girl named Lily came to the garden. She saw the sunflower and said, "Wow, you are so big and strong! Can I play with you?" The sunflower nodded its head and smiled. Lily and the sunflower played all day long. They laughed and had so much fun.

As they were playing, a big wind came. The wind was very strong and it made the sunflower sway back and forth. Lily held on to the sunflower to help it stay up. But the wind was too strong, and the sunflower began to break. Lily was sad and said, "Oh no! I don't want you to break!" The sunflower smiled at Lily and said, "Don't worry, I will grow back even stronger." And so it did. The sunflower and Lily became best friends, and they played together in the garden every day.

Tim and Sue were happy that they found the medal. They played with it all day. They took turns wearing the medal and pretending to be winners. At the end of the day, they put the medal in a safe place so they could find it and play with it again.

Bobo wanted the fruit, so he said, "Please, can I have the fruit?" The bush didn't say anything. Bobo was very happy and took the fruit. He started to eat it, and it was so yummy.

But then, Bobo's tummy started to hurt. He didn't feel good. The yummy fruit was bad for him. Bobo was very sad and went home. He didn't eat from the bush again.

When they got back, the cabin was very clean. The family who stayed home was proud. They saw the big, yummy cake and smiled. They knew it was important to share the cake with everyone.

Together, they ate the cake and laughed. The family knew that even though they had to separate sometimes, they were still a strong, loving family. They were happy in their little cabin in the woods.

One day, Anna went to a friend's house. Lily saw the crown on Anna's bed. She thought Anna would not mind if she borrowed it for a little while. She put it on her head and looked in the mirror. She felt like a princess. She danced and sang and pretended to rule the world.

But then, she heard the door open. It was Anna. She came back early. Lily was scared. She tried to take off the crown, but it was stuck. She pulled and pulled, but it did not move. She started to cry.

Anna ran to her room and saw Lily with the crown. She was angry. She yelled at Lily and grabbed the crown. She pulled and pulled, but it did not move. She realized that the crown was not a real crown. It was a modern crown. It had a zipper on the back. She had to unzip it to take it off.

Lily liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She was a good helper. She could stir the soup, wash the salad, and set the table. She liked to make things nice for her family.

One day, mom was very busy. She had to cook a big dinner for dad's birthday. She asked Lily to help her with a special cake. Lily was happy. She loved cake. She helped mom mix the batter, pour it in the pan, and put it in the oven. She helped mom make the frosting, too. It was pink and yummy.

Mom told Lily to wait for the cake to cool down before they could frost it. She gave Lily a napkin to wipe her mouth. She said, "You did a great job, Lily. Thank you for helping me. Why don't you go play for a while? I have to finish some other things."

Lily nodded. She took her napkin and went to the living room. She saw her teddy bear on the couch. She decided to play with him. She pretended he was her friend. She talked to him and hugged him. She was having fun.

But then, she smelled something. Something sweet and good. She remembered the cake. She wondered if it was ready. She wanted to see it. She wanted to taste it. She left her teddy bear and went back to the kitchen. She saw the cake on the counter. It looked so pretty. It had pink frosting and sprinkles. It had candles, too. Lily smiled. She wanted to surprise mom. She wanted to show her how much she loved her. She climbed on a chair and reached for the cake. She wanted to bring it to mom.

But she did not see the napkin. The napkin that she had left on the counter. The napkin that was close to the cake. The napkin that caught fire from the candles. Lily did not see the fire. She did not see the smoke. She only saw the cake.

She grabbed the cake with both hands. She lifted it up. She was proud. She was happy. She turned around. She saw mom. She saw dad. She saw her brother and sister. They were all in the kitchen. They were all looking at her. They were all looking at the cake. They were all looking at the fire.

They all screamed. They all ran. They all grabbed Lily and the cake. They all put out the fire. They all hugged Lily. They all checked if she was okay. They all told her they loved her. They all told her they were glad she was not hurt.

They all looked at the cake. It was a mess. It was burned. It was smashed. It was ruined. Lily felt sad. She felt sorry. She wanted to make mom happy. She wanted to make dad happy. She wanted to make a nice cake. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, dad. I wanted to help. I wanted to surprise you. I wanted to give you the cake."

Mom and dad smiled. They kissed Lily. They said, "It's okay, Lily. We know you wanted to help. We know you wanted to surprise us. We know you wanted to give us the cake. And you did. You gave us the best cake ever. You gave us a cake that we will never forget. You gave us a cake that made us laugh. You gave us a cake that showed us how much you love us. And we love you, too. You are our sweetest cake."

They all laughed. They all clapped. They all applauded Lily. They all said, "Happy birthday, dad. Happy birthday, cake. Happy birthday, Lily." They all hugged each other. They all ate the cake. It was not pretty. It was not yummy. But it was the best cake ever. Because it was made with love.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many trees. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Ben!" Lily said. "Maybe we can find a bear!"

Ben was not sure. He was a little scared of bears. He had seen them in books and on TV. They looked big and strong and loud.

"I don't know, Lily," Ben said. "What if a bear is not nice? What if it chases us or bites us?"

Lily laughed. She was not scared of anything. She was brave and curious and ready.

"Don't be silly, Ben," Lily said. "Bears are not mean. They are just animals. They like honey and berries and fish. Maybe we can be friends with a bear!"

Ben thought for a moment. He did not want to miss the fun. He did not want to make Lily sad. He decided to be brave too.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. "Let's go and find a bear. But we have to be careful and quiet. And we have to stick together."

Lily nodded. She took Ben's hand and they started to climb the hill. They walked through the trees and looked for signs of a bear. They saw some paw prints and some scratch marks and some fur. They followed the trail until they reached the top of the hill.

There, they saw a big cave. It was dark and deep and mysterious. They heard a loud snore coming from inside. They knew it was a bear.

"Wow, Ben," Lily whispered. "We found a bear! Do you want to see it?"

Ben felt his heart beat fast. He was very nervous. He wanted to see the bear, but he also wanted to be safe.

"I don't know, Lily," Ben whispered. "Maybe we should go back. Maybe the bear is sleeping and we should not wake it up."

Lily shook her head. She was too excited to leave. She wanted to see the bear, and maybe touch it and talk to it.

"No, Ben," Lily whispered. "We came this far. We have to see the bear. Come on, it will be fun!"

Lily let go of Ben's hand and crept towards the cave. She moved slowly and quietly. She peeked inside and saw a big brown bear lying on the ground. It was covered with fur and had a big nose and ears and claws. It looked very cozy and warm.

Lily smiled. She thought the bear was cute and friendly. She wanted to say hello. She took a step inside the cave and said in a soft voice:

"Hi, bear. We are Ben and Lily. We came to see you. We want to be your friends."

The bear heard the voice and opened its eyes. It saw a small girl standing in front of it. It was surprised and angry. It did not like strangers in its home. It did not want to be friends. It wanted to be alone.

The bear roared and jumped up. It showed its teeth and growled. It was ready to attack.

Lily screamed and ran out of the cave. She was scared and sorry. She did not mean to make the bear mad. She did not know the bear was not nice.

Ben saw Lily running and heard the bear roaring. He was terrified and worried. He wanted to help Lily and get away from the bear.

He ran after Lily and grabbed her hand. He pulled her down the hill and away from the cave. He did not stop until they reached the park.

They were safe and sound. They hugged each other and cried. They were sorry for being foolish and brave. They learned their lesson.

They never went to look for a bear again.

The end.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. They had a big bucket that they filled with water and mud. They used the bucket to make cakes and castles with the mud. They had a lot of fun, but they also made a big mess.

One day, their mom told them to clean the bucket and put it away. She said they had to do it before dinner, or they would not get any dessert. Tom and Sam did not want to clean the bucket. They wanted to play more. They said they would do it later, and ran away.

Mom was very angry. She waited for them to come back, but they did not. She went outside to look for them, and saw the bucket. It was still full of water and mud, and it was dripping on the grass. She also saw their cakes and castles, and how they ruined the flowers and the fence. She was very sad.

She took the bucket and poured out the water and mud. She scrubbed the bucket with a cloth and soap, until it was clean and dry. She put the bucket in the shed, and locked the door. She went back inside, and made dinner.

Tom and Sam came back when they smelled the food. They were hungry and dirty. They ran to the kitchen, and asked for dinner. Mom looked at them, and shook her head. She said they did not clean the bucket, and they did not listen to her. She said they could not have any dinner, or any dessert. She said they had to go to bed, without a story or a hug.

Tom and Sam were very sorry. They cried and begged for forgiveness, but Mom did not change her mind. She said they had to learn their lesson, and be more responsible and respectful. She sent them to their room, and turned off the light.

Tom and Sam lay in their beds, feeling hungry and sad. They wished they had cleaned the bucket, and obeyed their mom. They realized they had been very naughty, and they hurt their mom's feelings. They decided to be better brothers, and better sons, from now on.

The moral of the story is: You should always do your chores, and listen to your parents, or you will face the consequences.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe someone was naughty and ripped the page. Or maybe the book is old and the page broke," Tom says. He feels sorry and confused.

They look at the book and see that there are more pages that are torn or missing. They cannot read any more stories. They feel very disappointed.

They start to cry. They cry loud and hard. They want to read the book, but they cannot.

Mom hears them cry. She comes to the sofa and sees the book. She hugs them and says, "Why are you crying, Tom and Lily? What is wrong?"

"Mom, look at the book. The pages are torn and missing. We cannot read the stories. We are sad," Tom says.

"Mom, we like the book. It has many pictures and stories. But we cannot see them. We are angry," Lily says.

Mom looks at the book and says, "Oh, I see. This book is very old and damaged. It was my book when I was a little girl. I loved it too, but it is not good to read anymore. I'm sorry, Tom and Lily. I should have checked the book before I gave it to you."

She wipes their tears and says, "But don't worry, I have a surprise for you. I have another book that is new and available. It has many pages and pictures too. And it has more stories about dogs and cats and other animals. Do you want to see it?"

Tom and Lily nod and say, "Yes, please, Mom. We want to see the new book."

Mom smiles and says, "OK, then. Come with me. I will show you the new book. And we can read it together."

Tom and Lily stop crying and follow Mom. They are curious and happy. They hope the new book is as good as the old book. They want to read more stories.

Tom and Amy are twins. They like to play in the park with their dog, Spot. One day, they see a big package near a tree. It is brown and has many stamps on it.

"Look, Amy, a package!" Tom says. "I wonder what is inside."

"Maybe it is a toy or a book," Amy says. "Let's open it and see."

They run to the package and tear the paper. Inside, they find a strange thing. It is round and shiny and has many buttons and lights.

"What is this?" Tom asks. "It looks like a clock, but different."

"It is not a clock, children," a voice says. "It is a time machine."

They turn around and see an old man with a long beard and a hat. He is smiling and holding a cane.

"Who are you?" Amy asks. "How do you know what this is?"

"I am the one who sent you the package," the old man says. "I am your great-great-grandfather. I made this time machine long ago, when I was young and curious. I wanted to see the past and the future, but I never found the right time to use it. Now, I am too old and tired, so I decided to give it to you. You can use it to see the ancient times, when there were dinosaurs and pyramids and knights. Or you can see the future, when there are rockets and robots and aliens. It is up to you. But be careful, and don't stay too long. You have to come back to your own time, or you will get lost."

"Have fun, children," he says. "And remember, I love you."

The moral of the story is: do not do things that are dangerous or disobey your parents.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved candy and always had some in her pocket. One day, she met her friend Timmy on the playground.

"Hi Timmy! Want some candy?" Lily asked.

"Yes please!" Timmy replied with a big smile.

Lily gave Timmy some candy and he said, "Thank you, Lily! You're so thoughtful."

Lily giggled and said, "I have a joke for you. Why did the teddy bear say no to dessert?"

"I don't know, why?" Timmy asked.

"Because he was already stuffed!" Lily laughed.

Timmy laughed too and said, "That was a funny joke, Lily. Thanks for making me laugh!"

They said thank you to the plants and then walked to the house. They were happy and proud. They had a sack of carrots and a peaceful feeling in their hearts. They couldn't wait to share their carrots and their story with Mom.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite one was Anna. Anna had long, shiny hair that Lily loved to brush and style. Lily wanted to make Anna's hair even more beautiful, so she asked her mom if she could order some shampoo for her doll.

Mom said yes, and helped Lily find a website that sold shampoo for dolls. Lily was very happy, and chose a pink bottle that smelled like strawberries. She put it in the cart and clicked the button. Mom said the shampoo would come in a few days, and Lily could not wait.

Lily was so excited when the package arrived. She ran to her room and opened it. She took out the shampoo and read the label. It said: "Warning: Do not use on real hair. This shampoo is only for dolls. It will make real hair fall out." Lily did not understand what that meant. She thought it was a joke. She wanted to try the shampoo on herself, and see if it made her hair shiny like Anna's.

She went to the bathroom and turned on the faucet. She wet her hair and squeezed some shampoo on her palm. She rubbed it on her hair and smelled the strawberries. She smiled and rinsed it off. She looked in the mirror and gasped. Her hair was not shiny. It was falling out. She had bald spots on her head. She started to cry.

Mom heard her cry and ran to the bathroom. She saw Lily's hair and the shampoo bottle. She understood what happened. She hugged Lily and said: "Oh, honey, I'm so sorry. It makes it fall out. Don't worry, your hair will grow back. But you have to be careful with what you order online. Not everything is what it seems."

Lily nodded and sniffled. She felt silly and sad. She wished she had not used the shampoo. She wished she had listened to mom. She learned a lesson that day. She never ordered anything online again without mom's help. And she never used shampoo on herself that was not for real hair. She still played with Anna, but she used water and a comb to make her hair beautiful. And she waited patiently for her own hair to grow back.

"Go away, dog! Leave our fish alone! He is our friend. He is important to us!"

The dog did not listen. He tried to knock over the bowl. Tom and Anna held the bowl tight. They hoped someone would help them.

Then they saw a man. He was the dog's owner. He heard the noise and came to see. He saw the dog, the fish and the children. He was sorry.

"Bad dog! Stop that! Come here!" He called the dog. The dog obeyed. He left the fish and went to the man. The man put a leash on the dog. He apologized to Tom and Anna.

"I'm sorry, kids. He is a good dog, but he likes to chase things. He did not mean to hurt your fish. He is important to you, right?"

Tom and Anna nodded. They were glad the man came. They thanked him.

"Yes, he is important to us. His name is Bob. He is our friend."

The man smiled. He petted the dog.

"That's nice. Bob is a good name for a fish. He is lucky to have you as friends. And you are lucky to have him. He is a beautiful fish."

Tom and Anna smiled too. They agreed.

"Yes, he is. We love him very much."

They hugged the bowl. They looked at Bob. He swam happily in the water. He did not know what happened. He did not care. He was happy to be with Tom and Anna. They were his friends. They were important to him.

"Let's climb the rock!" Tom says.

"OK, but be careful!" Mia says.

They run to the rock and start to climb. They use their hands and feet to find good spots. They feel the sun and the wind on their faces. They reach the top and look around. They see the blue sea, the white sand and the green trees.

"Wow, this is awesome!" Tom says.

"Look, there are surfers!" Mia says.

They see some people on boards, riding the waves. They look like they are having fun.

"I want to surf too!" Tom says.

"Me too!" Mia says.

They climb down the rock and run to their mom and dad. They ask them if they can surf.

"Surfing is fun, but you need to learn how to do it first," their mom says.

"Maybe when you are older, you can take some lessons," their dad says.

"But we want to surf now!" Tom and Mia say.

They look at the water and the surfers. They have an idea.

They find two big leaves on the ground. They pretend they are surf boards. They hold them under their arms and run to the water. They splash and laugh. They try to balance on the leaves and catch the waves.

They are not really surfing, but they are having a lot of fun. They are adventurous kids. They like to climb, surf and explore. They are happy.

"Look, my car can fit in this box!" Lily said. She found a small cardboard box and put her car inside. "Now it is safe and cozy."

"Let me try!" Ben said. He wanted to fit his car in the box too. But his car was bigger than Lily's car. He pushed and pushed, but it did not fit. He got angry and pulled the box hard. The box ripped and his car fell out.

"Hey, you broke my box!" Lily said. She was sad and mad. She liked her box. It was a good place for her car.

"Sorry, Lily. Your box was too small for my car. My car is better than yours. It is bigger and more expensive." Ben said. He was proud and rude. He thought his car was the best.

"No, it is not. Your car is too big and too expensive. It does not fit anywhere. It is not fun. My car is better than yours. It is smaller and cheaper. It can fit in many places. It is more fun." Lily said. She was hurt and brave. She loved her car.

They started to argue and shout. They did not want to play together anymore. They moved to different sides of the room. They were lonely and bored. They missed each other.

After a while, they looked at each other. They felt sorry and silly. They did not want to fight over their cars. They wanted to be friends again.

"Lily, I am sorry I broke your box. And I am sorry I said my car was better than yours. Your car is nice and red. Can I play with it?" Ben said. He was humble and kind.

"Ben, I am sorry I said your car was not fun. Your car is cool and blue. Can I play with it?" Lily said. She was sweet and generous.

They smiled and nodded. They swapped their cars and tried them out. They found out that both cars were fun and fast. They did not care about the size or the price. They cared about each other.

They hugged and laughed. They played together again. They were happy and friendly. They learned to share and respect. They were good friends.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with words. They make new poems with words. They mix words and sounds and have fun.

One day, they find a big book of poems. They open the book and see many words. Some words are big, some words are small, some words rhyme, some words do not.

"Look, Lily, this poem is about a cat. It says 'The cat sat on the mat and wore a hat.' Do you like it?" Tom asks.

"Yes, I like it. It is funny. But I want to make a new poem. Can we mix the words and make a new poem?" Lily says.

"OK, let us try. How about 'The hat sat on the cat and wore a mat.' Is that a good poem?" Tom says.

Lily laughs. "No, that is a silly poem. The hat is too big for the cat. And the mat is not for wearing. Let us try again. How about 'The mat sat on the hat and wore a cat.' Is that a good poem?" Lily says.

Tom laughs too. "No, that is a sillier poem. The mat is too heavy for the hat. And the cat is not for wearing either. Let us try one more time. How about 'The cat wore a hat and sat on a mat. The hat wore a cat and sat on a mat too.' Is that a good poem?" Tom says.

Lily thinks. "Yes, that is a good poem. It is funny and it rhymes. I like it. We made a new poem with words. We are good at mixing words. We are poets!" Lily says.

Tom smiles. "Yes, we are poets. We like to play with words. We make new poems with words. We mix words and sounds and have fun." Tom says.

Jenny and Ben were best friends. They liked to play and share toys. One day, they decided to create something new. They took some paper, glue, and crayons. They cut and glued and colored. They made a big lollipop.

"Look at our lollipop!" Jenny said. "It is so pretty and yummy!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben said. "Can we eat it?"

Jenny shook her head. "No, we can't. It is only for pretend. We can play with it."

Ben felt sad. He wanted to eat the lollipop. He was hungry and it looked so sweet. He waited until Jenny was not looking. He took a bite of the lollipop.

"Ow!" Ben cried. "This lollipop is not good! It hurts my teeth!"

Jenny turned around. She saw Ben with the lollipop in his mouth. She saw the paper and glue and crayon on his lips. She was angry and sad.

"Ben, why did you do that?" Jenny asked. "You ruined our lollipop! You were not supposed to eat it!"

"I'm sorry, Jenny," Ben said. "I was hungry and curious. I thought it would taste good. But it didn't. It was bad."

Jenny sighed. She felt sorry for Ben. He looked sorry and hurt. She decided to forgive him.

"It's okay, Ben," Jenny said. "But you should not eat things that are not food. They can make you sick or hurt you. Next time, ask me before you try something. And if you are hungry, I can share my snack with you."

"Thank you, Jenny," Ben said. "You are a good friend. I will not eat things that are not food again. And I will share my snack with you, too."

They hugged and smiled. They threw away the lollipop. They ate their snacks. They were sleepy. They took a nap. They learned a lesson. They were still best friends.

Sam was a rabbit who liked to hop. He hopped all over the meadow, looking for carrots and flowers. He hopped so fast that he sometimes bumped into other animals.

One day, he saw a big tunnel in the ground. He wondered what was inside. He hopped closer and peeked in. He saw a dark and long tunnel. He was curious and brave, so he decided to hop in.

"Hello, is anyone there?" he called out as he hopped deeper into the tunnel. He heard a growl and saw two bright eyes. It was a fox who lived in the tunnel. The fox was hungry and angry. He wanted to eat Sam.

"Go away, this is my tunnel!" the fox snapped. "You are not welcome here!"

Sam was scared, but he was also persistent. He did not want to give up. He wanted to see what was at the end of the tunnel. He thought maybe there was something nice and fun there.

"Please, let me pass," he said to the fox. "I just want to see what is there. I will not bother you or take anything from you."

The fox was not convinced. He bared his teeth and lunged at Sam. Sam was quick and agile. He dodged the fox and hopped past him. He hopped and hopped until he reached the end of the tunnel.

There, he saw a beautiful garden full of carrots and flowers. He was so happy and amazed. He had never seen such a place before. He hopped around and nibbled on the carrots and flowers. He felt proud and satisfied.

He heard the fox coming after him. He was still angry and hungry. He wanted to catch Sam and eat him. Sam was not afraid anymore. He had an idea. He hopped to a big carrot and pulled it out of the ground. He threw it at the fox and hit him on the nose.

"Ouch!" the fox yelped. "That hurt!"

Sam hopped to another carrot and pulled it out. He threw it at the fox again and hit him on the ear.

"Ow!" the fox cried. "Stop that!"

Sam hopped to a third carrot and pulled it out. He threw it at the fox one more time and hit him on the eye.

"Oof!" the fox groaned. "Enough!"

The fox was tired and sore. He realized that Sam was too clever and persistent for him. He decided to leave him alone and go back to his tunnel.

"Fine, you can have the garden," he said to Sam. "But don't come back to my tunnel!"

Sam smiled and nodded. He thanked the fox and said goodbye. He hopped back to the meadow, happy and full. He had found a new and wonderful place. He had also learned a lesson. He learned that being persistent can help you achieve your goals, even if you face challenges and dangers. He also learned that being kind and respectful can help you make friends and avoid enemies. He was a happy and wise rabbit.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, mom asked them to make some pancakes for breakfast. Lily and Tom were happy and took out a big pan, some eggs, some milk and some flour.

Lily cracked the eggs and poured them into a bowl. Tom added the milk and the flour and stirred them with a spoon. They mixed everything well and made a smooth batter. Then they turned on the stove and put the pan on it. They poured some batter into the pan and waited for it to cook.

But soon, they heard a loud sizzling sound and saw some smoke coming from the pan. The batter was burning and sticking to the pan. Lily and Tom were scared and ran to mom.

"Mom, mom, help! The pancakes are ruined!" they cried.

Mom came to the kitchen and saw the mess. She turned off the stove and took the pan off. She looked at the black and crispy pancakes and sighed.

"What happened, Lily and Tom?" she asked.

Lily and Tom started to complain.

"It's not my fault, mom. Tom poured too much batter into the pan. He made it too thick and lumpy." Lily said.

"No, mom. It's Lily's fault. She cracked the eggs too hard and put some shells into the bowl. She made it too runny and watery." Tom said.

Mom shook her head and said, "Lily and Tom, stop complaining. You both made mistakes. You should have followed the recipe and measured the ingredients. You should have watched the heat and flipped the pancakes. You should have worked together and helped each other. Complaining won't fix the problem. It will only make it worse."

Lily and Tom felt embarrassed. They realized that mom was right. They had been careless and selfish. They had wasted the food and the time. They had made mom unhappy.

They said sorry to mom and hugged her. They asked her to teach them how to make pancakes properly. Mom smiled and said, "That's very good, Lily and Tom. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Making pancakes is easy and fun if you follow the steps and cooperate. Come on, let's try again. I'm sure you can do it."

Lily and Tom nodded and followed mom. They cleaned the pan and the bowl. They measured the eggs, the milk and the flour. They stirred the batter and poured it into the pan. They watched the heat and flipped the pancakes. They worked together and helped each other. They made some delicious and fluffy pancakes. They were proud and happy.

They served the pancakes to mom and dad. Mom and dad praised them and thanked them. They all enjoyed the breakfast and had a good day.

The moral of the story is: Don't complain, work together and learn from your mistakes.

Sara was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of toys, but her favorite was a big orange ball. She liked to bounce it, roll it, and throw it in the air.

One day, Sara saw her dad working on his computer. He was typing and clicking and looking at the screen. Sara wondered what he was doing. She wanted to see the computer. She asked her dad, "Can I play with your computer?"

Her dad smiled and said, "No, Sara, this is not a toy. This is a tool. I use it to do my work. You can play with your toys, but not with my computer."

Sara was sad. She did not understand why her dad did not let her play with his computer. She thought it looked fun and interesting. She decided to wait until her dad was not looking, and then sneak to his desk and touch the computer.

She waited for a long time, until her dad went to the kitchen to get a drink. Then she ran to his desk and climbed on his chair. She saw the keyboard and the mouse and the screen. She reached out her hand and pressed a button.

Suddenly, the screen went black. The computer made a loud beep. Sara was scared. She did not know what she did. She heard her dad coming back. She jumped off the chair and ran to her room.

Her dad saw the black screen and the beep. He was angry. He knew Sara had touched his computer. He went to her room and said, "Sara, did you touch my computer?"

Sara nodded. She was sorry. She said, "Yes, dad, I did. I was wondering what it was. I wanted to play with it. I did not mean to break it."

Her dad sighed. He said, "Sara, I know you were curious, but you should not touch things that are not yours. You should ask before you touch. You could have damaged my computer, or hurt yourself. You should respect other people's things, and play with your own toys."

Sara felt bad. She said, "I'm sorry, dad. I won't touch your computer again. I will play with my ball. I love my ball. It is orange and fun."

Her dad hugged her and said, "I love you, Sara. I'm glad you love your ball. It is a good toy for you. But you know what? Sometimes, I wonder what it is like to play with your ball. Maybe one day, you can teach me how to bounce it, roll it, and throw it in the air."

Sara smiled and said, "Yes, dad, I can. That would be fun. We can play together."

The moral of the story is: You should not touch things that are not yours without permission. You should respect other people's things, and play with your own toys. You can also share your toys and learn from each other.

Ben and Lily were sad and angry. They did not like the grumpy boy. They said, "No, this is not your rope. This is our rope. We were here first. You have to wait your turn."

The grumpy boy did not listen. He swung on the rope and made a mean face. He said, "No, this is my rope. I don't care about your turn. Go away."

But then something funny happened. The rope broke and the grumpy boy fell on the ground. He was not hurt, but he was dirty and surprised. He cried and ran away.

Ben and Lily looked at each other and smiled. They said, "That was funny. He got what he deserved. He was a bad boy." They laughed and hugged. They did not need the rope to have fun. They had each other.

"You are welcome, Lila. I know you love fashion and I want to provide you with some tools to make your own clothes for your dolls. You can be creative and independent and have fun," her mom said.

Lila hugged her mom and then started to look at the book and the things in the box. She was very excited and happy. She decided to make a dress for her favorite doll, Rosie. She chose a pink fabric and a purple ribbon and some shiny buttons. She cut and glued and sewed and made a beautiful dress. She put it on Rosie and admired her work.

"Look, mom, I made a dress for Rosie! Do you like it?" Lila asked.

"I love it, Lila. You did a great job. You are very talented and independent. I am proud of you," her mom said.

Lila smiled and thanked her mom again. She felt proud and happy too. She wanted to make more clothes for her dolls and show them to her mom. She loved fashion and she loved her mom.

One day, Lila and Ben decided to make a mud pie for Pinky. They found a big bucket and filled it with dirt and water. They stirred and stirred until it was soft and gooey. Then they shaped it into a round pie and put some leaves on top.

They carried the mud pie to Pinky's pen and called his name. "Pinky, Pinky, we have a surprise for you!" they shouted. Pinky came running and saw the mud pie. He was very happy and wagged his tail.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play on the beach. They made sand castles and dug holes and collected shells. One day, they found a big glass jar with a lid. It was half-full of water and had something inside.

"What is it?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Let's open it and see," Ben said.

He twisted the lid and pulled it off. A bad smell came out of the jar. It was sour and made them cough.

"Yuck! What is that?" Lily said.

They looked inside the jar and saw a small fish. It was gray and had no eyes. It floated in the water and did not move.

"It's a dead fish," Ben said. "Maybe someone put it in the jar and left it here."

"Maybe it's a magic fish," Lily said. "Maybe it can grant wishes if we stir the water and say something."

She picked up a stick and poked the water. The fish did not move.

"Come on, Ben. Let's try it. Maybe we can wish for ice cream or a new toy or something," she said.

Ben shrugged and joined her. They stirred the water and said their wishes out loud.

"I wish for a big scoop of chocolate ice cream," Lily said.

"I wish for a red fire truck," Ben said.

They waited for a moment, but nothing happened. The fish did not move. The water did not change. The jar did not glow.

"It's not working," Lily said. "This fish is useless."

She threw the stick away and kicked the jar. The jar rolled on the sand and hit a rock. It broke into pieces. The water and the fish spilled out.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a huge wave coming towards them. It was as tall as a house and as angry as a lion. It had a face and teeth and eyes. It looked at them and opened its mouth.

"NOOOOO!" Lily and Ben screamed.

The wave swallowed them and the jar and the fish. It was the ocean. It was mad. It did not like that they had stirred its water and disturbed its fish. It had heard their wishes and decided to punish them. It was too late for them to run or hide. They were gone.

Tom and Lily are afraid. They drop their toys and run away. They hide behind a tree and hug each other. They say, "Sorry, sorry, sorry." They hope the voice will not find them. They wish they did not play with the football. They learn a lesson. They say, "Next time, we will be more careful."

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat their meal. Mom put two plates on the table. One had rice and beans. The other had pasta and cheese.

"Be careful, the plates are hot," Mom said. "Don't touch them with your hands."

Lily nodded. She used a fork to eat her rice and beans. She liked them a lot. She said, "Thank you, Mom. This is yummy."

Ben did not listen. He was careless. He wanted to eat his pasta and cheese fast. He touched the plate with his hand. He felt a pain. He cried, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Mom heard him. She ran to the table. She saw his hand was red. She said, "Oh, Ben, what did you do? I told you not to touch the plate. It was hot. You hurt yourself."

She took his hand and put it under cold water. She gave him a hug and a kiss. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. It will be better soon. Next time, listen to Mom and be careful."

Ben nodded. He felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I was careless. I will listen to you and be careful next time."

Mom smiled. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I love you. Now, let's eat your pasta and cheese. It's not hot anymore."

She put his plate on a mat. She gave him a fork. He ate his pasta and cheese. He liked them a lot. He said, "Thank you, Mom. This is yummy too."

Mom, Lily and Ben ate their meal. They were happy. They talked and laughed. They enjoyed their food. They were careful. They did not touch the plates.

Tom was a sailor who liked to sail on the big blue sea. He had a boat with a white sail and a red flag. He was very good at sailing, but he was also very selfish. He never shared his boat with anyone, not even his friends.

One day, he saw a small island with a lot of trees and flowers. He thought there might be treasure there, so he sailed to the island. He was very excited to find out what was there. He jumped off his boat and ran to the trees.

But he was not alone. There was a girl on the island, who lived in a hut made of sticks and leaves. She saw Tom and came out of her hut. She said, "Hello, who are you? Do you want to play with me?"

Tom looked at her and said, "No, I don't want to play with you. I want to find treasure. This is my island now. Go away!"

The girl was sad and angry. She said, "This is not your island. This is my home. You are very selfish. You can't take what is not yours. Go away!"

Tom did not listen to her. He pushed her away and ran to the trees. He looked for treasure, but he could not find any. He only found rocks and shells and nuts. He was very disappointed.

He decided to go back to his boat and sail away. But when he got to the shore, he saw that his boat was gone. The wind had blown it away, and it was too far to reach. He was very scared and sorry.

He ran to the girl and said, "Please, help me. I'm sorry I was selfish. I'm sorry I was mean to you. Can you help me get my boat back?"

The girl looked at him and said, "Why should I help you? You were very selfish. You were very mean to me. You don't deserve my help."

Tom cried and begged. He said, "Please, please, please. I learned my lesson. I will share my boat with you. I will be your friend. Please, help me."

The girl thought for a while. She felt sorry for Tom, but she also wanted him to be nice. She said, "Okay, I will help you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will never be selfish again. You have to promise me that you will share your boat with me and with others. You have to promise me that you will be my friend."

Tom nodded and said, "I promise, I promise, I promise. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

The girl smiled and said, "You're welcome. Come on, let's go. I have a raft made of logs and vines. We can use it to get your boat back. And then we can play together on the island."

Tom and the girl got on the raft and paddled to the boat. They got the boat back and sailed to the island. They played together on the island, and they had a lot of fun. Tom was not selfish anymore. He was happy to share his boat with the girl and with others. He was happy to have a new friend. He learned that sharing is better than being selfish.

The path was long and winding. They saw many things on the way, like birds, bugs, and rocks. They also met some other kids who were playing. They said hello and kept going. They wanted to reach the hill before it got dark.

They were almost there when they heard a loud noise. It was a dog barking. They looked around and saw a big, black dog running towards them. It looked angry and scary. They were afraid and ran away. But they ran in different directions. Lily ran to the left and Ben ran to the right. They split up.

They started to cry. They wanted to find each other. They wanted to go home. They wished they had never followed the new path. They wished they had stayed with the other kids. They wished they had not been so curious.

Lily was a clever girl who liked to remember things. She remembered the names of all her toys, the colors of the rainbow, and the songs her mommy sang to her. She also remembered that Santa came every year to bring her presents.

She knew that Santa came down the chimney, but she did not know how he did it. She wondered if he was very small, or very bendy, or had magic dust. She wanted to see him with her own eyes, so she made a plan.

On Christmas Eve, she did not go to bed when her mommy told her to. She hid under the sofa and waited for Santa. She heard the clock go tick-tock, tick-tock, and the wind go whoosh, whoosh. She felt sleepy, but she did not close her eyes.

Then, she heard a thump on the roof, and a jingle of bells. She peeked out from under the sofa and saw a big red boot coming out of the chimney. She gasped and crawled closer to the fireplace. She saw a red suit, a white beard, and a big sack of toys. It was Santa!

He looked around the room and smiled. He saw the cookies and milk that Lily had left for him, and the carrot for his reindeer. He ate and drank, and then put the presents under the tree. He was about to go back to the chimney, when he noticed Lily.

He winked at her and said, "Ho ho ho, hello there, little one. You are a clever girl, but you should be asleep. Don't worry, I won't tell your mommy. But next year, please go to bed on time. It's good for you, and it makes my job easier."

He gave her a hug and a kiss, and handed her a small gift. He said, "This is for you, for being so curious and brave. But don't open it until morning. It's a surprise. Merry Christmas, Lily."

He climbed back up the chimney, and Lily heard him say, "On Dasher, on Dancer, on Prancer and Vixen, on Comet, on Cupid, on Donner and Blitzen. To the top of the porch, to the top of the wall, now dash away, dash away, dash away all!"

Lily was so happy and amazed. She ran to her bed and cuddled with her gift. She fell asleep with a smile on her face. She would always remember the night she met Santa.

One day, Mommy calls them for lunch. She says, "Boys, come down the stair. I have made soup and bread for you. It is very hot and tasty."

Tom and Sam hear Mommy. They want to eat the soup and bread. They rush to the stair. They do not walk slowly and carefully. They run fast and jump on the stair.

But the stair is slippery. Tom and Sam slip and fall. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cry and scream. Mommy hears them and comes to help them. She hugs them and says, "Oh, boys, what happened? Why did you rush on the stair? You should be more careful. You could have hurt yourself badly."

Tom and Sam feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mommy. We wanted to eat the soup and bread. We did not think about the stair. We will not rush on the stair again. We will walk slowly and carefully."

Mommy smiles and says, "That is good, boys. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, let me clean your wounds and give you a kiss. Then we can go and eat the soup and bread. It is still hot and tasty."

Tom and Sam say, "Thank you, Mommy. We love you. And we love your soup and bread."

The moral value of the story is: Do not rush on the stair. Be careful and safe. Listen to Mommy.

Lily wanted to help, so she tried to open the nut too. Together, they tried and tried until the nut finally cracked open. Sam and Lily were so happy that they could share the nut with their friends.

From that day on, Sam and Lily's friendship grew even stronger. They learned that when they worked together, they could do anything. And all the animals in the forest knew that Sam and Lily were the most loyal friends.

Then, one day, a sneaky fox appeared. He said, "This land is mine. You must leave right away." Hop and Skip didn't want to, but they knew they had to be honest. So, they hopped away sadly. 

Hop and Skip never did get to settle in that lovely meadow.

Once there was a little girl and her name was Jane. Jane was only three years old and she was very poor. Her family didn't have much money.

One day Jane was playing outside when she saw a phone on the ground. She knew she wasn't allowed to pick it up, but she thought it was a very cool thing. She bent down and tried to hold it, but it slipped from her hands and broke.

"Oh no!" Jane cried. "I've broken it." She was so sad and she cried for a long time.

But then Jane heard a voice. She looked up and saw an old man coming down the street. He said, "Don't cry, little one. I can help you fix it."

The old man was very kind and gentle. He pulled out a tiny toolkit and started to repair the phone. After a few minutes, he handed it to Jane.

"There you go" he said. "It might look a bit funny now but at least it still works."

Jane was so happy and gave the old man a big hug. She thanked him and held the phone tightly in her hands.

Jane thought to herself - even though she was poor, the old man still helped her. She smiled and walked off, feeling cheerful.

"Let's examine it," Mia said. "But be careful. Don't fall in."

They went closer to the well and looked down. It was very dark and deep. They could not see anything.

"Hello!" Ben shouted. "Is anyone there?"

They heard a loud echo. "Hello! Hello! Hello!"

They giggled. It was fun to hear their voices bounce back.

"Can I try?" Mia asked. She shouted, "We are cheerful! We are cheerful! We are cheerful!"

They heard the echo again. "We are cheerful! We are cheerful! We are cheerful!"

They laughed harder. They felt happy and curious.

But then, they heard something else. A low growl. A splash. A hiss.

They stopped laughing. They felt scared and confused.

"What was that?" Ben whispered.

"I don't know," Mia whispered back. "But I don't like it."

They backed away from the well. They wanted to run away.

The crocodile was hungry. It saw Ben and Mia. It wanted to eat them.

They hoped they could escape. They hoped they could find their way back home. They hoped they would never see the well or the crocodile again.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play outside. She had a big yard with many trees and flowers. She liked to look for bugs and birds and rocks. One day, she saw a big bird with big eyes and a round face. It was an owl. Lily had never seen an owl before. She wanted to say hello.

She walked slowly to the tree where the owl was sitting. She said, "Hi, owl. You are very pretty. What is your name?" The owl looked at her and blinked. He said, "Hoo, hoo. My name is Ollie. I am an owl. What is your name?" Lily smiled and said, "My name is Lily. I am a girl. I like to play. Do you want to play with me?"

Ollie nodded and said, "Hoo, hoo. I like to play too. But I can only play at night. I am a night owl. I sleep in the day and wake up in the dark. Do you know why?" Lily shook her head and said, "No, why?" Ollie said, "Because I can see better in the dark. My eyes are very good. I can see things that you can't. I can see mice and bugs and stars. Do you want to see them too?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. But I can't stay up at night. My mom and dad say I have to go to bed when the sun goes down. They say it is good for me. They say I have to sleep and dream and grow. Do you understand?" Ollie nodded and said, "Hoo, hoo. I understand. Your mom and dad are right. You have to sleep and dream and grow. You are a day girl. I am a night owl. We are different, but we can still be friends. Do you agree?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I agree. You are a nice owl. You are harmless. You don't hurt me or scare me. You teach me new things. You are my friend. Can I come and see you again?" Ollie nodded and said, "Hoo, hoo. Of course you can. You are welcome anytime. But remember, only when I am awake. And don't forget to say goodbye to your mom and dad. They love you and care for you. They want you to be safe and happy. Do you promise?"

Lily nodded and said, "I promise. I love you, Ollie. I love my mom and dad. I love my yard and my trees and my flowers. I love everything. Thank you for being my friend. Goodbye, Ollie." She gave him a hug and ran back to her house. Ollie smiled and said, "Hoo, hoo. You are welcome, Lily. You are a sweet girl. You are my friend. Goodbye, Lily." He closed his eyes and fell asleep.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that we can be friends with different kinds of animals and people, as long as we respect their needs and habits. It also teaches that we should listen to our parents and follow their rules, because they want what is best for us.

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had a big dollhouse and many clothes for them. She liked to pretend that she was their mommy and they were her babies. She gave them names and hugs and kisses.

One day, she decided to make them breakfast. She went to the kitchen and found a cup and a spoon. She filled the cup with water from the tap and put it in the microwave. She pressed some buttons and waited for the beep. She thought she was making coffee, like her mommy drank every morning.

She took the cup out of the microwave and carried it carefully to the dollhouse. She put it on a small table and called her dolls. "Come, babies, mommy has coffee for you!" she said. She picked up one of the dolls and held it to the cup. "Drink, drink, it's hot and yummy!" she said.

But the doll did not drink. It did not move or make a sound. Lily was confused. She tried to push the cup to the doll's mouth, but the water spilled on her hand. It was very hot and it hurt. Lily screamed and dropped the doll and the cup. She ran to her mommy, crying and holding her hand.

Her mommy heard her and came quickly. She saw the mess and the cup and the doll. She understood what happened and felt sorry for Lily. She hugged her and took her to the sink. She ran cold water over her hand and said, "It's okay, sweetie, it's okay. You burned yourself, but it will get better. You should not play with the microwave or the coffee. They are not for babies. They are hot and dangerous. You have to ask me first, okay?"

Lily nodded and sniffed. She was still sad and scared. She said, "I'm sorry, mommy. I wanted to make coffee for my babies. I wanted to be like you. I love you, mommy."

Her mommy smiled and kissed her. She said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a good mommy to your dolls, but you have to be careful. Coffee is not for babies. How about some juice and cookies instead?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, please. Juice and cookies are good for babies. And for mommies too."

Her mommy agreed and took her to the table. They had juice and cookies and talked about the dolls. Lily forgot about the coffee and the burn. She was happy again.

One day, a bear and a bee were friends. They liked to play and share honey. The bear had a big jar of honey that he kept in his cave. The bee had a small hive of honey that he made with his friends.

One day, the bear was hungry. He went to his cave and looked for his jar of honey. But he could not find it. He was upset. He thought someone took his honey. He went to the bee and said, "Did you take my honey?"

The bee was surprised. He said, "No, I did not take your honey. I have my own honey. Why do you think I took your honey?"

The bear said, "Because you like honey. And my honey is gone. Where is my honey?"

The bee said, "I don't know. Maybe someone else took your honey. Maybe a fox or a raccoon. They are sneaky. They like honey too."

The bear said, "Maybe you are right. Let's look for them. Maybe we can find my honey."

The bee said, "OK. Let's go."

They went to the forest and looked for the fox and the raccoon. They asked them if they took the bear's honey. But they said no. They said they did not like honey. They liked other things.

The bear and the bee were confused. They did not know who took the bear's honey. They were sad. They went back to the cave.

When they got to the cave, they saw something shiny. It was the jar of honey. It was buried under some rocks and leaves. The bear said, "Look! There is my honey! It was here all along. I must have buried it by mistake. I forgot where I put it."

The bee said, "Oh, you silly bear. You buried your own honey. You made us look for nothing. You made us worry for nothing."

The bear said, "I'm sorry, bee. I did not mean to. I was hungry and forgetful. Will you forgive me?"

The bee said, "Of course, bear. You are my friend. Friends forgive each other. But next time, don't bury your honey. Just eat it."

The bear said, "You are right, bee. Next time, I will eat my honey. And I will share it with you. Because you are my friend. And friends share with each other."

The bee said, "Thank you, bear. You are very kind. And your honey is very sweet."

They hugged and smiled. They ate some honey and played some more. They were happy. They were friends.

When his mommy saw the button, she was surprised too! She told Timmy how nice it looked on his shirt. Timmy was so happy and excited that he couldn't stop smiling. From that day on, Timmy wore his special button every day and it made him feel very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little beetle named Benny. Benny was always busy, buzzing around the garden looking for flowers to eat. One day, Benny met a little girl named Lily. 

"Hi Benny!" said Lily. "What are you doing?" 

"I'm busy looking for flowers to eat," replied Benny. 

"Oh, I see," said Lily. "Do you want to play with me?" 

Benny thought for a moment and then said, "Sure, I can skip with you!" 

So, Lily and Benny skipped around the garden together, having lots of fun. They even found some juicy beetles to eat along the way. It was a happy day for Benny and Lily. The end.

Suddenly, Choo-Choo saw something very strange. There was steam coming out of her chimney! Choo-Choo had never seen that before. She felt a little bit better because the steam was so cheerful and made her feel warm inside.

"Help, help, Tom!" Anna cried, following him.

They ran as fast as they could, but the dog was faster. He caught up with them and barked loudly.

"Please, please, don't hurt us!" Tom and Anna begged, hiding behind a fence.

"Why did you pretend to be goats?" he asked, in a gruff voice.

"We were just playing, we wanted to have fun," Tom and Anna said, in a small voice.

"Well, you should not play like that. It is not safe, and it is not nice. Goats are goats, and children are children. You should be happy with who you are, and not try to become something else. Do you understand?" the dog said, in a stern voice.

They never pretended to be goats again, and they always played safely and kindly. They were happy to be children, and they made friends with the real goats, who liked them too.

Once upon a time there was a little bird named Lucy and she wanted to fly but she could not. Every day she would watch the other birds fly and wish she could too. She was feeling very sad. 

One day, she tried to fly but she got very tired and fell to the ground. She was very dirty.

Then a kind man came along and said to her, "Come here my little one, don't be sad. I know you can fly, you just have to try harder." 

Lucy looked at the kind man and said, "But I am so tired, I cannot fly."

The kind man said, "If you keep trying, you will get better. The way you get better is to keep practising. Then you will be able to fly."

At this Lucy felt a little bit happier and she tried again. This time she managed to fly. Everyone looking at her gave her a big round of applause.

From then on, Lucy kept practising and practising and soon she was flying like an expert.

The moral of this story is that if you keep trying and never give up, you can achieve your goals, even if it takes a lot of practice.

Later that day, the monkey was swinging from the tree when he saw a small bird that had fallen from its nest. The monkey tried to help the bird, but he accidentally dropped it. The bird was okay, but the monkey felt very sad. 

The monkey realized that he should have accepted the man's help earlier. He learned that it's okay to ask for help when you need it. From that day on, the monkey lived happily in his tree and never hesitated to ask for help again.

One day, he went to the lake with his boat and his net. He saw many fish swimming in the water. He threw his net into the lake and waited. He hoped to catch a big fish for his dinner.

But then, he heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a dark cloud in the sky. It was a storm. The wind blew hard and the rain started to pour. Ben was scared. He wanted to go back to the shore, but the waves were too big and strong. His boat rocked and tipped.

"Help! Help!" Ben shouted. "I don't want to fall into the water!"

He heard a voice from the shore. It was his friend Tom, who was also a fisherman. Tom had a rope and a hook. He threw the rope and the hook to Ben.

"Grab the rope, Ben!" Tom said. "I will pull you to the shore!"

Ben grabbed the rope and held on tight. Tom pulled the rope and the hook. He pulled Ben and his boat to the shore. Ben was wet and cold, but he was safe.

"Thank you, Tom!" Ben said. "You are a good friend!"

Tom smiled and gave Ben a hug. He also gave him a towel and a blanket. He helped him dry his boat and his net. He also gave him a fish from his own catch.

"What is that?" Lily asked, feeling frightened.

"It is a storm," Tom said. "It makes the sky dark and noisy. Sometimes it can remove the power from the house."

"Remove the power? What does that mean?" Lily wondered.

"It means the lights and the TV and the fridge will stop working. They need power to work," Tom explained.

Lily did not like that idea. She liked the lights and the TV and the fridge. She did not want them to stop working. She hugged her toy car and hoped the storm would go away soon.

But then the noise got louder and louder. And suddenly, the living room went dark. The TV and the lights and the fridge stopped working. The storm had removed the power from the house.

Lily and Tom screamed. They were very frightened. They did not like the dark and the noise. They wanted their mom and dad.

"Mom! Dad!" they cried.

Mom and dad heard them and came to the living room. They had flashlights and candles. They hugged Lily and Tom and told them not to be afraid.

"It is okay, sweeties. The storm will not hurt you. It will pass soon. And the power will come back later. We are here with you. You are safe," they said.

Lily and Tom felt better. They snuggled with their mom and dad and their toy cars. They listened to the storm and waited for the power to come back. They were not so frightened anymore.

Their mom said, "That's okay, children. I am glad you are safe. You learned a lesson today. The real treasure is not something that glows or is fancy. The real treasure is your family and friends who love you and care for you. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We love you too. You are our treasure." They smiled and hugged their mom. They went home and played with their toys. They did not want to go to the cave again. They were happy with what they had.

One day, they go to the city with their moms. They see a big train that goes under the ground. It is called a subway. Anna and Ben are curious. They want to ride the subway.

"Mom, this is so cool. How does the subway work?" Ben asks.

"Well, the subway is a train that runs on electricity. It has a driver who controls the speed and direction. It stops at different stations where people can get on and off." Ben's mom explains.

"Wow, that is very clever. I wish I could own a subway." Ben says.

"Me too. But I think it is too big and expensive. Maybe we can own a toy subway instead." Anna says.

"That would be nice. We can play with it at home." Ben says.

Tom and Mia like to play with their cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They like to make them go fast and make noises. Sometimes they race their cars on the floor or on the table.

One day, they decided to have a big race with all their cars. They lined them up on the floor and said "Ready, set, go!" They pushed their cars as hard as they could and watched them zoom across the room. They cheered and shouted for their cars.

Tom's car was very fast and soon it was in front of all the others. Mia's car was also fast, but not as fast as Tom's. She wanted to win the race, so she tried to catch up with Tom's car. She was very competitive.

As they reached the end of the floor, Mia's car got closer and closer to Tom's car. She pushed harder and harder. Then, she did something naughty. She reached out and rubbed Tom's car with her hand. She hoped to slow it down or make it go off course.

But her plan backfired. When she rubbed Tom's car, she also rubbed her own car. Both cars lost speed and started to wobble. They went off the floor and crashed into the wall. They fell down and stopped.

Tom and Mia looked at their cars. They were sad and angry. They had ruined their race and their cars. They started to cry and blame each other. They forgot to have fun.

Their mom heard them crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw their cars on the floor and the wall. She asked them what happened. They told her their story. She shook her head and said "That was not nice. You should not rub each other's cars. You should play fair and share. Racing is fun, but not when you are too competitive. Next time, be kind and careful."

She helped them pick up their cars and fix them. She gave them a hug and a kiss. She told them to try again and have fun. She said "It's not always about winning. It's about having a good time."

Tom and Mia nodded and said sorry to each other. They hugged and smiled. They decided to have another race, but this time, they would not rub each other's cars. They would play nice and have a good time.

Sara and Ben like to play in the garden. They have a big plant that grows red flowers. They water the plant every day and talk to it.

One day, Sara has a new toy. It is a scale that can weigh things. She wants to weigh the plant. She says to Ben, "Let's weigh the plant. It is so big and thick. I want to know how much it is."

Ben says, "No, Sara. We can't weigh the plant. It is too heavy and we might hurt it. The plant likes to stay in the ground. It does not like to be moved."

Sara does not listen to Ben. She tries to pull the plant out of the ground. She pulls and pulls, but the plant does not come out. She pulls harder and harder, but the plant does not move. She gets angry and yells, "Come out, plant! I want to weigh you!"

The plant does not like Sara's yelling. It shakes and shivers. It drops all its red flowers on the ground. The flowers are sad and wilted. The plant is sad and droopy.

Ben sees what Sara has done. He is shocked and sad. He says to Sara, "Look, Sara. You made the plant unhappy. You made the flowers fall. You were mean to the plant. The plant is our friend. We should be nice to it."

Sara sees the plant and the flowers. She feels sorry and ashamed. She says to Ben, "You are right, Ben. I was mean to the plant. I did not think about how it feels. I only wanted to weigh it. I am sorry, plant. I am sorry, Ben. Can we fix it?"

Ben says, "I don't know, Sara. Maybe we can. Maybe we can water the plant and give it some food. Maybe we can sing to it and tell it we love it. Maybe the plant will forgive us and grow new flowers. But we have to be gentle and careful. We have to respect the plant."

Sara says, "Yes, Ben. We will do that. We will be gentle and careful. We will respect the plant. We will be its friends. We will not weigh it again. We will only weigh things that are not alive, like rocks and toys."

They hug each other and the plant. They hope the plant will be happy again. They learn a lesson about plants and weighing.

"Maybe we need a book of spells," Lily said. "Let's look in the attic. Maybe we can find one there."

"Look, I found a book!" Ben said. He picked up a thick book with a star on the cover. He opened it and saw strange words and pictures. "Maybe this is a book of spells!"

He showed it to Lily. She was curious. She pointed to a page with a picture of a moon and stars. "What does this say?" she asked.

Ben tried to read it. He sounded out the words. "It says...Dream...Spell. If you say this spell before you sleep, you will have a wonderful dream."

Tim and Sue are friends who like to play in the park. One day, they see a big billboard near the road. The billboard has a picture of a dog and some words that they cannot read.

"Look, Sue, a dog!" Tim says, pointing to the billboard.

"I like dogs. They are nice and dependable. They can do tricks and protect you," Sue says.

"Me too. I wish I had a dog. Do you think we can touch the dog on the billboard?" Tim asks.

"I don't know. It is very high. Maybe we can lift each other up and reach it," Sue suggests.

They go to the billboard and try to lift each other up. Tim lifts Sue first, but she is too short to touch the dog. Then Sue lifts Tim, but he is also too short. They try again and again, but they cannot touch the dog.

They are about to give up when they hear a voice behind them.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing?" the voice says.

They turn around and see a man with a camera. He is smiling and holding a leash. On the other end of the leash, there is a real dog. It is the same dog as on the billboard.

"We are trying to touch the dog on the billboard," Tim says.

"Well, you don't have to do that. This is the dog on the billboard. His name is Rex. He is a model for a pet store. I am his owner and photographer. Do you want to pet him?" the man says.

"Really? Can we?" Sue says.

"Sure, he is very friendly and dependable. He loves kids. Here, you can lift him up and hug him," the man says.

He helps Tim and Sue lift Rex up and hug him. Rex licks their faces and wags his tail. Tim and Sue are very happy. They thank the man and Rex for letting them pet him.

They go back to the park and play some more. They decide that Rex is the best dog ever. They hope to see him again on the billboard or in real life.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mom. They found a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, some sugar, and some milk. They poured everything in the bowl and started to stir.

"Stir, stir, stir!" Lily said. "We are good cooks!"

"Yes, we are!" Tom said. "Mom will love our cake!"

But they stirred too hard and too fast. The bowl tipped over and the batter spilled on the floor. It made a big mess. Lily and Tom were scared. They heard Mom coming.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "What do we do?"

"Hide!" Tom said. They ran to the living room and hid behind the chest. The chest was big and brown and had toys inside.

Mom came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She was angry. She shouted, "Who did this? Lily? Tom? Where are you?"

Lily and Tom felt helpless. They knew they did something bad. They wanted to say sorry, but they were afraid of Mom. They stayed behind the chest and did not make a sound.

Mom looked around the kitchen and the living room. She could not find Lily and Tom. She sighed. She was not only angry, but also worried. She loved Lily and Tom very much. She wanted to talk to them and hug them.

She went back to the kitchen and started to clean the mess. She saw a note on the table. It said, "We love you, Mom. We made a cake for you. Lily and Tom."

Mom smiled. She understood. She knew Lily and Tom were trying to do something nice for her. She was not angry anymore. She was proud of them.

She went to the living room and called, "Lily? Tom? Come out, please. I want to see you."

Lily and Tom heard Mom's voice. They peeked from behind the chest. They saw Mom smiling. They felt happy. They came out and ran to Mom. They hugged her and said, "Sorry, Mom. We made a mess. We wanted to make a cake for you."

Mom hugged them back and said, "It's okay, my loves. I appreciate your thought. But next time, please ask me first before you use the kitchen. And don't hide from me when you make a mistake. I will always love you, no matter what."

Lily and Tom nodded. They learned their lesson. They said, "We love you, Mom. Thank you for cleaning the mess. Can we help you?"

Mom said, "Of course. You can help me by being good and honest. And maybe later, we can make a real cake together. How does that sound?"

Lily and Tom cheered. They said, "That sounds great, Mom. You are the best!"

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be honest, to admit their mistakes, to apologize, and to ask for permission. It also shows the love and forgiveness of a mother.

Lily knew that Max was protecting her, so she knelt down and hugged him. She said, "It's okay, Max. We can play with the big dog too." Max wagged his tail and ran to play with the big dog. Lily smiled and knew that Max would always protect her.

Lily didn't know what a cell was, so she asked the butterfly, "What's a cell?" The butterfly explained, "It's my home where I rest and sleep. It's where I keep my wings safe." 

Lily thought that was very interesting and said, "I wish I had a cell too. I could keep my pretty dresses safe in there." The butterfly smiled and said, "You don't need a cell to be pretty and graceful like me. Just keep twirling and dancing in your dresses, and you'll be just as beautiful."
