One day, Tom saw a big box in the living room. He wondered what was inside. He asked his mom, but she said it was a surprise. She told him not to touch it or open it. She said he would find out soon enough. Tom was curious, but he nodded and went to play with his toys.

The next day, Tom woke up early. He ran to the living room, hoping to see the surprise. But the box was gone. He looked around, but he could not find it. He felt sad and confused. He asked his dad, but he said it was a secret. He told him to get ready for school. He said he would tell him later. Tom was disappointed, but he obeyed and got dressed.

At school, Tom could not stop thinking about the box. He wondered what was in it and why his parents were hiding it from him. He did not pay attention to his teacher or his friends. He did not join the games or the songs. He just sat in his chair and frowned.

When Tom came home from school, he saw something amazing. In front of his house, there was a shiny new bike. It had red wheels, a blue frame, and a yellow bell. It had a big bow on it and a card that said: "To Tom, from Mom and Dad. We love you. Happy birthday!" Tom was overjoyed. He ran to his parents and hugged them. He thanked them for the wonderful gift. He realized that the box was the bike, and that his parents were not hiding it, but saving it for his special day. He felt silly for frowning and not trusting them. He apologized and said he loved them too.

Tom rode his bike around the house, feeling happy and proud. He rang his bell and waved to his friends. He smiled and said he had the best parents and the best birthday ever. He was a helpful and grateful boy.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They found a big box with a lock on it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there are toys or candy in the box," Lily said.

"Or maybe there are monsters or bugs," Tom said.

They looked for a key to open the lock, but they could not find one. They tried to break the lock with a stick, but it was too hard.

"Let's ask Dad to help us," Lily said. "He can fix anything."

They ran to the house and found Dad in the garage. He was working on his bike.

"Dad, Dad, can you help us?" Lily said. "We found a big box with a lock, but we don't have a key."

"Sure, I can help you," Dad said. "Where is the box?"

They showed him the box in the garden. Dad looked at the lock and took out a tool from his pocket.

"This is a powerful tool," Dad said. "It can cut metal and wood. Watch out, it can be loud and hot."

He turned on the tool and made a noise like a bee. He cut the lock with the tool and opened the box.

"Wow, Dad, you are so powerful," Tom said.

They looked inside the box and saw a lot of books and papers.

"What are these?" Lily asked.

"These are old books and papers from my grandpa," Dad said. "He was a writer and a teacher. He liked to tell stories and teach things. He gave me this box before he went to the sky."

"Can you read us some stories, Dad?" Tom asked.

"Of course, I can," Dad said. "Let's sit down and read together. Maybe we can learn something new."

They sat down and read some stories from the books. They laughed and asked questions. They had fun and felt happy. They thanked Dad for fixing the lock and opening the box. They hugged him and said they loved him.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a new thing on a bench. It is round and gray and has holes. Tim says, "What is that?" Sam says, "I don't know. Let's look."

They go to the bench and touch the thing. It is cold and hard and dirty. Tim says, "It smells bad." Sam says, "Maybe it is a toy." He picks it up and shakes it. Some black dust falls out. Tim says, "Ew, gross." Sam says, "Maybe it makes noise." He blows into it. Nothing happens.

A man comes to the bench. He is angry. He says, "Hey, that's mine. Give it back." He grabs the thing from Sam. It is his ashtray. He uses it to put out his cigarettes. He says, "You kids are careless. You could have hurt yourself. This is not a toy. It is dangerous. Go away."

Tim and Sam are scared. They run away from the bench. They say, "Sorry, mister. We didn't know." They don't want to meet the man again. They don't like his ashtray. They think it is ugly and nasty. They decide to play somewhere else.

Tom and Lily liked to design things with their crayons and paper. They made houses, cars, animals and flowers. One day, they decided to design a forest. They drew many green trees, brown dirt, blue sky and yellow sun. They also drew some red and black bugs, some gray and white birds and some brown and black bears.

"Look at our forest!" Tom said to Lily. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Lily said. "But I think we need something else. Something to make it more fun."

"What do you mean?" Tom asked.

Lily pointed to a corner of the paper. "There. We can draw a path. And then we can pretend we are walking in the forest and exploring."

Tom liked the idea. He took a brown crayon and drew a path that went from one side of the paper to the other. He and Lily put their fingers on the path and started to move them along.

"Let's see what we can find in the forest!" Lily said.

They moved their fingers past the trees, the bugs, the birds and the bears. They made noises like they were talking to them. They had fun.

But then, they came to the end of the path. There was nothing there. Just white paper.

"Uh-oh," Tom said. "Where does the path go?"

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it goes to another forest. Or maybe it goes to a secret place."

They looked at each other. They were curious. But they were also worried. What if there was something scary or bad at the end of the path? What if they got lost or stuck?

"Should we keep going?" Tom asked.

Lily thought for a moment. Then she shook her head. "No, I don't think so. I think we should go back. It is safer and nicer in our forest."

Tom nodded. He agreed. He and Lily moved their fingers back along the path. They said goodbye to the trees, the bugs, the birds and the bears. They came back to the start of the path.

They looked at their forest. They smiled. They were happy.

They put their paper on the wall. They hugged each other.

"We made a good forest," Tom said.

"Yes, we did," Lily said. "But maybe next time, we can make a shorter path. Or a different path. Or no path at all."

They laughed. They went to get some juice and cookies. They were hungry. They were friends. They loved to design things.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box of blocks in the attic. They decided to build a castle with the blocks. They worked hard and made a big castle with towers and walls and a gate.

"Look at our castle!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and strong!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben said. "But I want to make it bigger and better!"

Ben took some blocks from Lily's tower and added them to his tower. Lily was angry and took some blocks from Ben's wall and added them to her wall. They started to fight and pull and push the blocks. Soon, their castle was broken and the blocks were in a big row.

"Stop it!" Lily said. "You are mean and selfish!"

"No, you stop it!" Ben said. "You are bossy and greedy!"

They were so loud that their mom heard them and came to the attic. She saw the row of blocks and the angry twins.

"What is going on here?" Mom said. "Why are you fighting over the blocks?"

"Lily took my blocks!" Ben said.

"Ben took my blocks!" Lily said.

Mom shook her head and said, "You are both wrong. The blocks are not yours or mine. They are ours. We share them and play with them together. Fighting over them is not nice or fun. It only makes you sad and tired."

Mom picked up a black block and said, "Look at this block. It is black, but it is not bad. It can be part of a castle or a car or a train or anything you want. It can be a friend to the other blocks, no matter what color they are. But if you throw it or break it, it is not useful or happy. It is just a block."

Lily and Ben looked at the black block and then at each other. They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We are sorry, Lily. We are sorry, Ben."

They hugged each other and Mom and said, "We love you, Mom. We love you, Lily. We love you, Ben."

They picked up the blocks and started to build a new castle. They shared the blocks and helped each other. They made a bigger and better castle than before. They smiled and laughed and had fun.

They learned that sharing is caring and that blocks are friends. They also learned that yawning is a sign of being sleepy and that it is time to go to bed. They said good night to Mom and to their castle and to their blocks and went to sleep. They dreamed of more adventures with their toys.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a doll and Ben had a truck. They liked to pretend that their toys were real and had adventures.

"Look, my doll is a princess and she lives in a castle," Sara said, holding her doll high.

"My truck is a fire truck and it can save people from fires," Ben said, making siren noises.

They were having fun, but they also wanted to see their mom. She was in the kitchen, making a cake for their dad's birthday. She had told them not to come in until she was done.

"I wonder what kind of cake mom is making," Sara said.

"Maybe it's a chocolate cake. I love chocolate," Ben said.

They decided to sneak a peek at the cake. They tiptoed to the kitchen door and opened it a little bit. They saw their mom holding a big bowl and a spoon. She was putting something in the bowl.

"What is she doing?" Sara whispered.

"I think she is weighing the flour. She needs to know how much to use," Ben whispered.

They watched as their mom poured some flour from a bag into the bowl. She looked at a photo on the counter. It was a photo of their dad when he was a little boy. He had a big smile and curly hair.

"Who is that?" Sara asked.

"That's dad. He was a baby like us," Ben said.

They saw their mom smile at the photo. She looked happy, but also worried. She put the photo down and looked at the clock.

"Oh no, I'm running out of time. I need to finish the cake before dad comes home," she said to herself.

She didn't see Sara and Ben at the door. They felt sorry for their mom. They wanted to help her.

"Let's go and give her a hug. Maybe that will make her feel better," Sara said.

"OK, let's go," Ben said.

They ran into the kitchen and hugged their mom. She was surprised, but also happy.

"Hi, sweeties. What are you doing here?" she asked.

"We wanted to see you. We love you, mom," Sara said.

"We love you, too. And we love dad. Can we help you with the cake?" Ben asked.

Their mom smiled and kissed them.

"Of course you can. You are the best helpers ever. Thank you for being so sweet," she said.

She gave them each a spoon and let them stir the batter. They had fun making the cake with their mom. They forgot about their toys in the living room. They only cared about their mom and their dad. They knew they would have a great birthday party.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with pots and pans. Lily had a big pot of rice and Tom had a small pan of eggs.

"Look, I made rice for you!" Lily said, holding the pot. "Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Tom said, smiling. He put his pan on the table and took a spoon.

Lily poured some rice on his plate. But she poured too much. The rice was hot and it spilled on Tom's hand.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom screamed. He dropped the spoon and shook his hand. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Lily was scared. She did not mean to hurt Tom. She dropped the pot and ran to Tom. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry! I'm sorry! Are you okay?"

Tom was crying. He felt the rice burning his skin. He hugged Lily back and said, "It's okay. It's okay. It was an accident."

Mom heard the scream. She was in the living room, reading a book. She was alert. She knew something was wrong. She ran to the kitchen and saw Lily and Tom.

"What happened?" Mom asked, worried. She saw the rice on the floor and on Tom's hand. She quickly took Tom to the sink and ran cold water on his hand. She said, "It's okay, sweetie. It's just a little burn. It will heal soon."

Lily followed Mom and Tom. She felt bad. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Tom. I was trying to be nice. I wanted to share my rice."

Mom smiled and said, "I know, honey. You were very nice. But you have to be careful with hot things. They can hurt you and others. Next time, ask me for help, okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I'm sorry."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, honey. I love you. And I love your rice. Maybe we can eat it later, when it's cooler."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. I love you too. And I love Tom."

Tom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love your rice. Thank you for sharing."

Mom, Lily and Tom hugged and kissed. They were happy. They cleaned up the mess and went to the couch. They watched a movie and ate some cookies. They forgot about the scream and the rice. They had fun.

Anna and Ben liked to play with their books. They had many books with pictures and words. Some books had stories about animals, some had stories about people, and some had stories about magic.

One day, they found a new book on the shelf. It was big and old and had no pictures. It had many words, but they were hard to read. The book had a mysterious name: The Book of Secrets.

"What is this book?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it has stories we don't know," Ben said.

They opened the book and looked inside. The pages were blank. There were no words, no stories, no secrets.

"Maybe we have to add our own stories," Anna said.

"How do we do that?" Ben asked.

"Maybe we have to use our imagination. We can think of anything we want and write it down," Anna said.

They took a pencil and a paper and started to write. They wrote about a dragon, a princess, a pirate, and a fairy. They wrote about a castle, a ship, a forest, and a cave. They wrote about adventures, dangers, friends, and enemies. They wrote and wrote and wrote.

They did not notice that the book was changing. The blank pages were filling up with their words. The words were becoming pictures. The pictures were becoming stories. The stories were becoming secrets.

The book was magic. It was adding their stories to its own. It was making them part of its mysterious world.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play games. They had many games, but their favorite was tic-tac-toe. They used a big napkin and a marker to draw the board and the Xs and Os. They took turns to put their marks on the napkin, trying to make a line of three.

One day, they decided to play for a prize. The prize was a shiny red car that their dad had bought for them. It was very expensive and they both wanted it. They agreed that whoever won the most games would get the car.

They played and played, but they were both very good at tic-tac-toe. They tied many times, and no one could win. They started to get tired and hungry, but they did not want to stop. They wanted the car so much.

Then, Lily had an idea. She said to Ben, "Let's make the game harder. Let's use two napkins and two markers. One napkin will be blue and one will be green. One marker will be black and one will be white. You can only use the black marker on the blue napkin, and I can only use the white marker on the green napkin. And we have to put our marks on both napkins at the same time. The first one to make a line of three on both napkins wins the car. Do you want to play?"

Ben thought that sounded fun and hard. He said, "OK, let's play. I will win the car."

They got another napkin and another marker and started the new game. They were very careful to follow the rules. They had to think a lot and look at both napkins. It was harder than before, but they still tied many times. They played and played, until they ran out of space on the napkins.

They looked at the napkins and counted their lines. They both had two lines of three on each napkin. They tied again. They could not believe it. They looked at each other and then at the car. They both wanted it, but they both deserved it.

They did not know what to do. They felt sad and angry. They started to cry. They cried so loud that their mom heard them. She came to see what was wrong. She saw the napkins and the marker and the car. She asked them what happened.

They told her about their game and their prize and their tie. They asked her who should get the car. She smiled and hugged them. She said, "You both played very well and very fair. You both worked hard and had fun. You both are winners. And you both can share the car. How about that?"

Ben and Lily stopped crying and smiled. They liked that idea. They said, "Thank you, mom. We love you. And we love each other. And we love the car."

They hugged their mom and each other. They took the car and played with it together. They were happy. They did not need another napkin or another marker. They had everything they needed.

Lily and Tom were twins who loved to gaze at the stars. Every night, they would sneak out of their room and climb to the roof of their house. They would lie on a big blanket and look at the bright dots in the sky. They would make up stories about the stars and their friends.

One night, they saw a big red star that was brighter than the others. Lily said, "Look, Tom, that star is so pretty. Maybe it is a special star that can make our wishes come true. What do you wish for, Tom?"

Tom said, "I wish for a luxury car, like the one that Mr. Jones has. It is shiny and fast and has a loud horn. I want to drive it and go to the park and the zoo and the beach. What do you wish for, Lily?"

Lily said, "I wish for a luxury dress, like the one that Mrs. Smith has. It is soft and sparkly and has a big bow. I want to wear it and go to the party and the ballet and the museum. Do you think the star will hear us, Tom?"

Tom said, "I hope so, Lily. Maybe we should say our wishes louder, so the star can hear us better. Let's shout together, on the count of three. One, two, three!"

They shouted their wishes as loud as they could, hoping the star would listen. But they did not know that the star was not a star at all. It was a rocket that was flying very fast and very close to the earth. It was carrying a bomb that was very big and very dangerous. It was going to explode and make a lot of fire and smoke and noise.

The rocket heard their shouts and thought they were enemies. It changed its course and aimed at their house. It flew faster and faster, until it hit the roof where Lily and Tom were lying. There was a loud boom and a bright flash and a lot of heat and pain. Lily and Tom never got their luxury car and dress. They never saw the stars again.

One day, they decide to perform a story about wild animals. Lily puts on a lion mask and a furry coat. Ben wears a monkey hat and a brown shirt. They roar and jump and swing around the room.

"Look at us, we are wild and free!" Lily says.

"Ooh ooh aah aah, we are funny and smart!" Ben says.

They have a lot of fun, but they also make a big mess. They knock over books and pillows and toys. They spill juice and crackers on the floor. They do not notice how messy they are.

Mom and dad come to watch their performance. They clap and smile, but they also frown and sigh.

"What a wonderful show, Lily and Ben!" mom says. "But what a messy room!"

"You are very creative, Lily and Ben!" dad says. "But you also need to clean up!"

Lily and Ben feel proud and happy, but they also feel sorry and guilty. They love to perform, but they do not like to make a mess.

"Sorry, mom and dad," Lily says.

"Sorry, mom and dad," Ben says.

They hug their mom and dad and say thank you. Then they help to tidy up the room. They put away their toys and costumes. They wipe the juice and crackers. They stack the books and pillows.

They learn that performing is fun, but cleaning is important. They also learn that wild animals are not always messy. They promise to be more careful next time. They still love to play pretend, but they also love to keep their room neat.

Tom and Lily were playing with a puzzle on the floor. They liked puzzles very much. They had many pieces with different colors and shapes. They tried to fit them together to make a picture.

"Look, I found the piece for the dog's nose!" Lily said, holding a brown piece.

"Good job, Lily! And I found the piece for the dog's tail!" Tom said, holding a black piece.

They smiled and put the pieces in the right place. The puzzle was almost done. They only needed a few more pieces.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was their big brother, Sam. He came into the room and saw the puzzle.

"What are you doing, you babies?" he said. "This puzzle is too easy for you. Let me show you a real puzzle."

He kicked the puzzle and made the pieces fly everywhere. Tom and Lily gasped. They saw their puzzle break into many pieces. Some pieces went under the bed, some went behind the sofa, some went out of the window.

"Hey, stop it, Sam! That's not nice!" Tom said, angry and sad.

"Ha ha ha, that's funny!" Sam said, laughing. He did not care about Tom and Lily. He ran out of the room.

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt very bad. They wanted to finish their puzzle. They liked their puzzle. But now their puzzle was gone. They could not find all the pieces. They could not make the picture.

They started to cry. They hugged each other. They wished Sam was nice to them. They wished they had their puzzle back.

They yawned. They were tired of crying. They wanted to sleep. They crawled into their bed. They closed their eyes. They hoped to have a better day tomorrow.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One day, they decided to play hide and seek in their house. Tim was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran to the bathroom and saw the toilet. She had an idea. She took the big towel from the rack and covered herself with it. She sat on the toilet and waited for Tim to find her.

Tim looked for Lily in every room. He could not see her anywhere. He was getting tired and bored. He thought maybe Lily was hiding in the bathroom. He opened the door and saw the toilet. He saw the big towel on it. He thought it was strange. He said, "Lily, are you there?"

Lily did not answer. She wanted to surprise Tim. She stayed very quiet and still. She hoped Tim would go away. But Tim was curious. He walked to the toilet and pulled the towel. He saw Lily sitting on it. He was shocked. He said, "Lily, what are you doing?"

Lily smiled and said, "I was hiding from you. I fooled you. I win!"

Tim was not happy. He said, "That's not fair. You can't hide on the toilet. That's gross. And what if someone needed to use it? The bathroom is busy now. You have to get off."

Lily did not want to get off. She said, "No, I like it here. It's cozy and warm. And no one needs to use it. We are the only ones home."

Tim and Lily were scared. They knew they were in trouble. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were just playing."

And Tim, why did you let her do that? You should know better. You are both very naughty. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Tim and Lily got off the toilet and ran to their rooms. They felt bad and sad. They wished they had played somewhere else. They learned their lesson. They never hid on the toilet again.

Tim and Mia were twins who liked to wander around the park. They saw many things, like trees, flowers, birds and dogs. Sometimes they met other children and played with them. They were very intelligent and curious.

One day, they wandered near a big fence. Behind the fence, there was a lot of noise and smoke. They heard machines and people shouting. They wondered what was behind the fence.

They found a hole in the fence and crawled through it. They saw a big building with many pipes. The pipes were metal and had steam coming out of them. Some of the pipes were broken and had water spilling out of them. The twins thought the pipes were interesting and wanted to touch them.

"Look, Tim, this pipe is warm and shiny. Can I touch it?" Mia asked.

"No, Mia, don't touch it. It might be hot and hurt you. And we should not be here. This is not our place. Let's go back to the park." Tim said.

But Mia did not listen. She reached out her hand and touched the pipe. She screamed. The pipe was very hot and burned her hand. She cried and ran back to Tim.

"Tim, Tim, help me. The pipe burned me. It hurts. I'm sorry. I should have listened to you." Mia said.

Tim hugged Mia and tried to calm her down. He saw a man coming towards them. The man was wearing a helmet and a vest. He looked angry.

"Hey, you kids, what are you doing here? This is a dangerous place. You could have been hurt or killed. How did you get in here? Where are your parents?" The man asked.

Tim and Mia were scared. They did not know what to say. They wished they had never wandered near the fence. They wished they had stayed in the park. They learned a hard lesson. They hoped the man would not be too mad at them. They hoped Mia's hand would be okay. They hoped their parents would not be too mad at them. They hoped they could go home soon.

"Can we pet them, mom?" Lily asked.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play in the park every Sunday with their mom and dad. They liked to swing, slide, and run on the grass. They also liked to feed the ducks in the pond.

One Sunday, they saw a big dog near the pond. The dog was black and had sharp teeth. It barked very loud and ran towards them. Anna and Ben were fearful. They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench. They cried and hugged them.

"Mom, dad, help! There is a big dog!" Anna said.

"Don't worry, sweeties. We will protect you. The dog won't hurt you," dad said.

But the dog did not stop. It jumped on the bench and bit dad on the arm. Dad screamed and pushed the dog away. Mom grabbed Anna and Ben and ran to the car. She tried to close the door, but the dog was faster. It got inside the car and bit mom on the leg. Mom screamed and kicked the dog. Anna and Ben were very scared. They cried and screamed too.

The dog bit them all. They bled and hurt. No one came to help them. The dog was happy. It ate them all. The end.

"Wow, Ben, you are very good!" Anna says. She claps her hands and smiles. "Can I try too?"

"Sure, Anna, here you go!" Ben says. He gives the ball to Anna and she throws it too. But she throws it too far and it lands in the bushes.

"Oh no, where is the ball?" Anna says. She runs to the bushes and looks for the ball. Ben follows her.

They search and search, but they cannot find the ball. They are sad and tired. They sit on the grass and eat some blueberries.

"These blueberries are very tasty, but I miss the ball," Anna says.

"Me too, Anna, me too," Ben says.

They hear their mom calling them from the house.

"Anna, Ben, it's time for your nap!" mom says.

"Nap? But we want to play!" Anna says.

"Sorry, sweeties, but you need to rest. You can play more later," mom says.

"OK, mom, we will come," Ben says.

They get up and take their basket with them. They walk to the house and give their mom a hug and a kiss.

"Maybe we will find the ball after our nap," Anna says.

"Maybe, Anna, maybe," Ben says.

They go to their room and lie on their beds. They close their eyes and fall asleep. They dream of blueberries and balls.

Lily liked to jog with her dad in the park. She felt fast and strong when she ran. She also liked to look at the trees and the birds and the flowers. Sometimes she saw other people jogging too, and she waved at them.

One day, as they were jogging, Lily saw a big branch on the path. It was brown and dry and had many sharp points. She thought it looked like a monster. She was scared and stopped running. She pointed at the branch and said, "Dad, look! A monster!"

Her dad smiled and said, "That's not a monster, Lily. That's just a branch. It fell from a tree. It can't hurt you. Come on, let's jog around it."

Lily was not sure. She looked at the branch again. It still looked like a monster. She said, "No, dad. I don't want to jog around it. I want to go home."

Her dad saw that Lily was really scared. He did not want to make her feel bad. He was a polite dad. He said, "Okay, Lily. We can go home. But first, let's say goodbye to the branch. Maybe it's lonely and needs a friend."

Lily was curious. She said, "Say goodbye to the branch? How?"

Her dad said, "Like this. Watch me." He jogged up to the branch and said, "Hello, branch. You look very nice today. I'm sorry you fell from the tree. I hope you find a new home soon. Goodbye, branch." Then he jogged back to Lily.

Lily was amazed. She said, "Wow, dad. You talked to the branch. Did it talk back?"

Her dad said, "No, it didn't. But maybe it heard me and felt happy. Do you want to try?"

Lily nodded. She was brave. She jogged up to the branch and said, "Hello, branch. I'm Lily. I'm sorry I was scared of you. You're not a monster. You're just a branch. I hope you have a good day. Goodbye, branch." Then she jogged back to her dad.

Her dad hugged her and said, "Good job, Lily. You were very polite to the branch. I'm proud of you. Now let's go home and have some juice."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, dad. I like juice. And I like jogging with you. And I like branches too. They're not so scary after all."

"Wow, can I see?" Tom asked, reaching for the stone.

But as he did, he bumped his head on the box. The box was old and weak, and it broke with a loud rip.

"Oh no!" Tom and Lily cried. "Our tunnel is broken!"

They looked at the hole in the box. They felt sad and angry.

"How can we fix it?" Lily wondered.

"Maybe we can use some tape," Tom suggested. "Or some glue."

They ran to the house and asked their mom for some tape and glue. She gave them some and told them to be careful.

They went back to the garden and tried to repair their tunnel. They put some tape over the hole, but it was not enough. They added some glue, but it was too sticky. They tried to push the box together, but it was too hard.

They sighed and gave up. They sat on the grass and looked at their broken tunnel.

"Maybe we can make a new tunnel," Lily said. "With a better box."

"Or maybe we can play something else," Tom said. "Like catch or hide and seek."

They thought for a moment. Then they smiled at each other.

"OK, let's play catch," Lily said. "You're it!"

She threw the shiny stone at Tom and ran away. Tom caught the stone and chased after her. They laughed and had fun.

They forgot about their broken tunnel. They still had their treasure and their friendship.

Later, their mom called them for lunch. She had made some tasty sandwiches and juice for them.

They ran to the house and washed their hands. They thanked their mom and ate their lunch.

They were happy and full. They decided to play some more after lunch.

Maybe they would find another box and make another tunnel.

Or maybe they would find something else to do.

They didn't mind. They had each other and their imagination.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the snow. They had a great time making snowmen, throwing snowballs and sliding on the ice. They wore warm coats, hats, gloves and scarves to keep them cozy.

One day, they decided to explore the woods behind their house. They saw many animals, like rabbits, squirrels and birds. They also found a big hill that looked fun to climb. Ben and Lily raced each other to the top, laughing and shouting.

But when they got to the top, they saw a scary sight. A big, black bear was sleeping on the other side of the hill. It had a red scarf around its neck, just like Lily's. The twins were very afraid and wanted to run away.

But as they turned around, Lily stumbled on a rock and fell down. Her scarf came off and flew in the air. The bear woke up and saw the scarf. It thought it was a snack and grabbed it with its teeth.

Ben saw what happened and wanted to help his sister. He was brave and ran towards the bear. He yelled and threw snowballs at it, hoping to scare it away. The bear was angry and roared at Ben. It dropped the scarf and chased him.

Lily got up and saw her brother in danger. She was brave too and ran after them. She picked up a big stick and hit the bear on the nose. The bear was hurt and surprised. It stopped and ran away.

Ben and Lily hugged each other and thanked each other for saving their lives. They picked up Lily's scarf and ran back to their house. They told their mom and dad what happened and showed them the scarf. It had a big hole in it from the bear's bite.

Their mom and dad were very proud of them and glad they were safe. They said they were very brave and smart. They also said they should not go to the woods alone again. They gave them hot chocolate and cookies and hugged them tight.

Ben and Lily were happy and relieved. They learned a lesson and had a great adventure. They still liked to play in the snow, but they stayed away from the bear's hill. They also took good care of their scarves, especially Lily's. It had a scar, but it was also a souvenir.

"Look at me, Ben, I'm the king of the tree!" Lily shouted.

"Bang!" The bullet hit the branch where Lily was sitting. The branch broke and Lily fell down. She screamed and cried. Ben ran to her and hugged her.

"Lily, Lily, are you okay?" Ben asked.

Lily was hurt and scared. She had a cut on her arm and a bump on her head. She was sorry for not listening to Ben.

"Ben, I'm sorry, I was silly," Lily said. "You were right, it was too high. And there was a bad man with a gun. He tried to shoot me. He thought I was a bird."

"Hey, you, bad man, stop!" Ben said. "You hurt my friend! You are mean and stupid! You don't shoot at people, you only shoot at cans!"

"I'm sorry, kids, I'm sorry," the man said. "I didn't mean to shoot at you. I thought you were a bird. I was wrong. I was not wise. I should have looked more carefully. I should have been more careful. I hope you are not badly hurt. Can I take you to the doctor?"
